invoices.summary:
LPH arrived at the residence to perform a comprehensive electrical system check evaluation throughout the home. The evaluation included inspecting the main electrical panel and subpanel, checking the condition of the breakers and visible electrical connections, evaluating grounding and bonding components, and looking for signs of corrosion, deterioration, overheating, or other potential electrical safety concerns.

LPH also tested accessible receptacles throughout the home, checked switches and electrical devices for proper operation, and inspected for loose devices and connections. A few loose electrical devices were tightened as LPH went around the home testing the receptacles. Accessible GFCI receptacles and their protective functions were checked where applicable, along with visible wiring conditions and the general condition of the home’s accessible electrical components.

Additional areas evaluated included accessible lighting fixtures and their operation, visible smoke and carbon monoxide detection equipment, exterior receptacles and weatherproof covers where accessible, and visible electrical connections and equipment throughout the home. LPH also looked for signs of damaged devices, improper installations, deterioration, and other conditions that could affect the safety or reliability of the electrical system. The remainder of the home’s accessible electrical components appeared to be in good working condition based on the evaluation performed.

During the evaluation, Gail reported noticeable voltage drops when new electrical loads begin drawing power. After tightening the panel connections, LPH applied pressure to the service cable wiring and could hear electrical arcing, with some circuits experiencing intermittent operation. These conditions raise serious concerns regarding the integrity of the existing electrical connections and the potential for overheating, equipment damage, or electrical failure.

The existing main electrical panel is approximately 45 years old and completely full, while the subpanel is nearly at capacity. Due to the age and condition of the equipment, the reported voltage fluctuations, and the audible arcing and intermittent circuit operation, LPH discussed replacing the existing main panel with a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel and installing whole-home surge protection. A separate option for a complete 200 Amp underground electrical service replacement, including a new meter base and exterior emergency disconnect, was also discussed.

All findings and available options were reviewed with Gail, including the concerns identified with the existing electrical equipment and the benefits of the recommended upgrades. Gail would like approximately one week to review the options and determine how she would like to proceed.

LPH will follow up with Gail by phone in approximately one week to discuss her decision and determine the next steps. The estimates outlining the available options, along with today’s electrical system check evaluation, will be emailed to Gail for her review.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. We appreciate the opportunity to evaluate your electrical system and look forward to assisting you with your electrical needs in the future.

estimates.name: Standard Panel Replacement
estimates.summary:
Electrical Panel Replacement & Whole-Home Surge Protection

Reason for Replacement

The existing electrical panel has been in service for approximately 45 years and is showing signs of deterioration after decades of electrical loading. The main panel is completely full, and the subpanel is nearly at capacity, leaving limited room for additional circuits and future electrical upgrades.

The homeowner has reported noticeable voltage drops when new electrical loads begin drawing power. During the electrical evaluation, LPH tightened the panel connections; however, when pressure was applied to the service cable wiring, audible electrical arcing could still be heard, and some circuits were observed experiencing intermittent operation.

These symptoms raise serious concerns regarding the condition of the existing electrical connections and distribution equipment. Deteriorated connections can create excessive resistance, localized overheating, and electrical arcing, potentially damaging equipment and increasing the risk of electrical failure or fire.

Due to the age and condition of the existing equipment, the audible arcing, intermittent circuit operation, and limited panel capacity, LPH recommends replacing the existing electrical panel rather than continuing to rely on deteriorated components. Simply tightening connections or replacing individual breakers may not adequately address the overall condition of the existing panel.

Scope of Work Includes:

* Remove the existing approximately 45-year-old electrical panel.
* Install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel.
* Transfer and properly terminate the existing branch circuits in the new panel.
* Install new breakers throughout the panel as required for the existing circuits.
* Properly separate neutral and grounding conductors within the panel as required.
* Inspect and verify electrical connections, terminations, and grounding.
* Install top-tier whole-home surge protection at the new electrical panel.
* Properly label the new panel and individual circuits.
* Test the completed installation and verify proper operation of the electrical system.

Benefits of Replacing the Existing Panel

Improved Electrical Safety: Replacing the aging panel and associated breakers addresses deterioration within the existing distribution equipment. New equipment and properly completed terminations help reduce the risks associated with worn components and unreliable electrical connections.

Addressing Arcing and Intermittent Circuits: The reported arcing and intermittent circuit operation are significant warning signs that require attention. Replacing the panel provides an opportunity to inspect and properly reconnect the existing branch circuits and evaluate the affected connections. Any damaged service conductors or other components outside the panel replacement scope may require additional repairs.

Improved Power Reliability: A new panel and properly terminated connections can help resolve problems caused by deteriorated panel components or connections. However, because voltage fluctuations can also originate from the service conductors, utility supply, or other parts of the electrical system, further investigation may be necessary if the symptoms persist.

Additional Circuit Capacity: The new 42-space Eaton CH panel provides additional breaker spaces, improving circuit organization and allowing greater flexibility for future electrical additions. The existing subpanel and the home’s overall electrical load will still need to be considered when planning future upgrades.

Whole-Home Surge Protection: LPH will install a whole-home surge protective device to help protect sensitive electronics, appliances, and other connected equipment from damaging voltage surges caused by lightning, utility disturbances, and other electrical events.

Peace-of-Mind Warranty

The new Eaton CH electrical panel and breakers are protected by a 10-year parts and labor warranty while maintaining an active LPH Service Partner Plan (SPP) membership, providing continued coverage and added peace of mind.

Long-Term Value

Replacing the existing electrical panel will modernize a critical part of the home’s electrical infrastructure while addressing concerns associated with aging equipment, limited circuit capacity, and potentially deteriorated connections.

The new Eaton CH panel, properly terminated branch circuits, and whole-home surge protection will provide an improved foundation for electrical safety, reliability, and future circuit additions.

Important Note: This option covers the electrical panel replacement and whole-home surge protection only. It does not include replacement of the underground electrical service, meter base, or exterior service equipment. If the source of the voltage fluctuations or arcing is found to involve the incoming service conductors or equipment outside the panel, additional repairs or a complete service replacement may be necessary.

All work will be completed in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements and the requirements of the local authority having jurisdiction.

estimates.name: Priority Underground Service Replacement
estimates.summary:
200 Amp Underground Electrical Service Replacement

Reason for Replacement

The existing electrical service equipment has deteriorated significantly due to age, prolonged electrical loading, and the demands placed on the home’s electrical system. The main electrical panel is completely full, and the subpanel is also nearly at capacity, leaving limited room for additional circuits while placing continued demands on the existing equipment.

The homeowner has reported noticeable voltage drops when new electrical loads begin drawing power. During the electrical evaluation, LPH tightened the panel connections; however, when pressure was applied to the service cable wiring, electrical arcing could still be heard, and some circuits were observed experiencing intermittent operation.

These conditions are serious warning signs that the existing service connections and electrical distribution equipment may have deteriorated to the point where reliable electrical contact can no longer be assured. Loose or deteriorated connections can generate excessive heat and electrical arcing, potentially damaging equipment and increasing the risk of electrical failure or fire.

Due to the combination of noticeable voltage fluctuations, audible electrical arcing, intermittent circuit operation, deteriorated equipment, and heavily loaded panels, LPH recommends replacing the existing electrical service rather than continuing to rely on aging components. Simply tightening connections or replacing individual breakers would not adequately address the overall condition of the existing service equipment.

A complete service replacement will provide new service equipment, updated electrical distribution, improved circuit capacity, and a modernized grounding and bonding system to help restore reliable power delivery and reduce the risks associated with the deteriorated installation.

Scope of Work: 200 Amp Underground Electrical Service Upgrade

LPH will modernize the home’s electrical service by replacing the existing service equipment with a new 200 Amp system, including a new exterior emergency disconnect and a new interior electrical panel.

Scope of Work Includes:

* Remove the existing deteriorated electrical panel and associated service equipment.
* Install a new 200 Amp meter base.
* Replace the underground service entrance conductors and associated connections as required by the approved scope and utility requirements.
* Install a new exterior 200 Amp emergency disconnect to provide an accessible means of shutting off power to the home during an emergency or when servicing the electrical system.
* Install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel.
* Transfer and properly terminate existing branch circuits in the new panel.
* Install new breakers throughout the panel as required for the existing circuits.
* Properly separate neutral and grounding conductors within the new panel.
* Upgrade the grounding and bonding system to meet applicable electrical code requirements.
* Install top-tier whole-home surge protection at the new electrical panel.
* Install protective conduit for exterior service conductors where applicable to protect against physical damage and environmental exposure.
* Properly seal applicable service entry points to help prevent moisture intrusion.
* Label the new electrical panel and individual circuits.
* Inspect and verify electrical connections, terminations, grounding, and bonding.
* Coordinate required permits, inspections, and PPL scheduling as applicable.
* Test the completed installation and verify proper operation of the electrical system.

Why a Complete Replacement Is Recommended

1. Addressing Electrical Arcing and Intermittent Power

Audible arcing when pressure is applied to the service cable wiring, combined with circuits intermittently going in and out, indicates a potentially hazardous connection or equipment failure. Electrical arcing can produce intense localized heat, damage conductors and terminals, and increase the risk of an electrical fire. These conditions warrant prompt corrective action.

2. Correcting Voltage Fluctuations Under Load

Noticeable voltage drops when new electrical loads start can indicate excessive voltage drop, deteriorated connections, inadequate conductors, or another supply-side or distribution problem. A complete service replacement will allow the affected service components and connections to be replaced, although the underlying cause of the voltage fluctuations must be verified rather than assumed.

3. Replacing Deteriorated Electrical Equipment

The existing equipment has experienced decades of service and prolonged electrical loading. Aging breakers, bus connections, and terminations can deteriorate over time. Replacing the existing panel and service equipment will establish a new foundation for dependable electrical distribution rather than continuing to rely on components showing signs of deterioration.

4. Improving Electrical Capacity and Organization

The main panel is completely full, and the subpanel is nearly full. The new 42-space Eaton CH panel will provide additional circuit spaces and a modernized distribution arrangement. The new 200 Amp service will also provide greater capacity where supported by the home’s calculated electrical load and the utility service.

5. Adding an Exterior Emergency Disconnect

The new exterior emergency disconnect will provide an accessible means of disconnecting power to the home. This improves accessibility for emergency response and servicing while modernizing the home’s service equipment.

6. Protecting Connected Electronics and Appliances

The new whole-home surge protective device will help protect sensitive electronics, appliances, and other connected equipment from damaging voltage surges caused by lightning, utility disturbances, and other electrical events.

Underground Service Protection and Longevity

The new service equipment will be installed with appropriate protection and sealing to help minimize exposure to physical damage and moisture intrusion. Exterior service conductors will be installed in protective conduit where applicable to the installation and utility requirements.

Replacing the service connections, meter base, exterior emergency disconnect, and interior electrical panel will address the major components included in this service replacement and help establish a more reliable electrical infrastructure for the home.

Peace-of-Mind Warranty

The new Eaton CH electrical panel and breakers are protected by a 10-year parts and labor warranty while the homeowner maintains an active LPH Service Partner Plan (SPP) membership, providing continued coverage and additional peace of mind.

Long-Term Value

This project is more than a routine electrical panel replacement. It addresses documented concerns involving voltage fluctuations, audible arcing, intermittent circuit operation, aging service equipment, and limited panel capacity.

By replacing the existing service equipment, installing a new exterior emergency disconnect, upgrading grounding and bonding, and adding whole-home surge protection, LPH will help address the conditions affecting the home’s electrical reliability while providing a modernized 200 Amp electrical service designed to support the home’s needs for years to come.

All work will be completed in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements and the requirements of the serving utility and local authority having jurisdiction.

invoices.summary:
Electrical System Check Summary

LPH performed an electrical system evaluation throughout the home to assess the condition and operation of the electrical system, identify potential safety concerns, and verify proper operation where accessible. During the evaluation, LPH reviewed the electrical panel and circuit protection, checked for visible signs of deterioration or overheating, inspected accessible wiring and connections, and performed electrical testing to evaluate proper voltage and breaker operation.

Electrical Panel and Arc-Fault Breaker Findings

During the inspection, LPH noticed light carbon dust deposits near the Eaton BR-style dual-function arc-fault breakers inside the electrical panel. To verify proper operation, LPH began testing the breakers using an appropriate circuit tester. The initial breaker tested failed to trip as intended, prompting LPH to test every arc-fault breaker in the panel.

During this process, seven 20-amp Eaton BR-style dual-function arc-fault breakers failed. Two breakers visibly sparked through their clear test buttons and experienced internal component failure, producing an immediate burnt odor. The remaining five breakers made loud electrical noises consistent with coil chattering before failing.

These failures indicate that the affected breakers have experienced internal component malfunctions and can no longer be relied upon to provide their intended circuit protection. Since these devices are designed to protect electrical circuits from dangerous fault conditions, leaving failed breakers in service creates a safety concern and may increase the risk of electrical overheating or fire.

LPH performed additional voltage testing to confirm proper voltage and evaluate the overall stability of the electrical system. The remainder of the system tested stable at the time of evaluation. Based on the testing performed, the breaker failures appear to be an isolated anomaly rather than an indication of a system-wide electrical problem. However, the exact cause of the failures has not been confirmed.

Receptacle and Switch Wiring Evaluation

LPH also identified that the home’s receptacles and switches were wired using the stab-back method, in which conductors are inserted into push-in terminals on the devices rather than secured under the side-terminal screws. Although this wiring method is commonly found in residential properties, these connections can become less reliable over time and may be more susceptible to loosening or developing poor electrical contact under certain conditions.

LPH opened accessible electrical boxes to inspect the wiring and connections. No loose connections were identified during the inspection. While no immediate connection issues were found, LPH will continue to monitor the condition of these connections during the home’s yearly electrical system checks to identify any developing concerns and recommend corrective action if necessary.

Recommended Corrective Action and Customer Approval

LPH recommended the immediate replacement of all seven failed 20-amp Eaton BR-style dual-function arc-fault breakers. The approved scope of work includes:

* Removing the seven failed arc-fault breakers.
* Supplying and installing seven new, compatible 20-amp Eaton BR-style dual-function arc-fault breakers.
* Inspecting accessible breaker connections and affected panel areas for signs of heat damage or deterioration.
* Verifying proper voltage and testing the affected circuits following installation to confirm proper operation.

The homeowner has approved the recommended work. Due to a time constraint with the homeowner’s appointment, the down payment and scheduling arrangements will need to be completed following the conclusion of this call.

Because this is a pressing electrical safety concern, LPH will make every effort to schedule the approved work as soon as possible.

Today’s invoice and electrical evaluation will be emailed to the homeowner for their records.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. We appreciate the opportunity to address this electrical safety concern and look forward to completing the necessary repairs as soon as possible.

estimates.name: Breaker Replacement
estimates.summary:
Critical Electrical Safety Concern – Failed Arc-Fault Breakers

During today’s electrical evaluation, LPH noticed light carbon dust deposits near the Eaton BR-style dual-function arc-fault breakers inside the electrical panel. To confirm proper operation, LPH began testing the breakers using an appropriate circuit tester. The initial breaker tested failed to trip as intended, prompting further testing of every arc-fault breaker in the panel.

During testing, seven 20-amp Eaton BR-style dual-function arc-fault breakers failed. Two breakers visibly sparked through their clear test buttons and experienced internal component failure, producing an immediate burnt odor. The remaining five breakers emitted loud electrical noises consistent with coil chattering before failing.

These results indicate significant internal failures within the affected breakers, preventing them from functioning as designed. Circuit breakers are essential safety devices that protect electrical wiring from dangerous conditions. When these protective devices fail, the affected circuits may no longer have the intended protection against electrical faults, increasing the risk of overheating and potential electrical fires.

System Voltage Testing and Overall Condition

LPH performed additional testing to confirm proper voltage throughout the electrical system and found the remaining system to be stable at the time of evaluation. Based on the testing performed, the failure of these seven breakers appears to be an isolated anomaly rather than an indication of a system-wide electrical problem. However, the exact cause of the breaker failures cannot be confirmed without further investigation.

LPH’s Recommendation: Immediate Breaker Replacement

LPH recommends replacing all seven failed breakers immediately rather than leaving them in service. Due to the internal failures observed during testing, these breakers can no longer be relied upon to provide their intended circuit protection.

Scope of Work:

* Remove the seven failed 20-amp Eaton BR-style dual-function arc-fault breakers.
* Supply and install seven new, compatible 20-amp Eaton BR-style dual-function arc-fault breakers.
* Inspect accessible breaker connections and affected panel areas for signs of heat damage or deterioration.
* Verify proper voltage and test the affected circuits following installation to confirm proper operation.

Although the remainder of the electrical system tested stable, the seven failed breakers represent a significant safety concern that should be addressed promptly. Replacing these devices will restore the intended circuit protection to the affected circuits and help reduce the risk of electrical hazards.

estimates.name: Water softener
estimates.summary:
Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 16 grains per gallon. A hardness level of 16 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, shower heads, and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a cabinet water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. Benefits of the system include improved soap and detergent performance, reduced spotting and scaling, softer-feeling water, and increased protection and efficiency of plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances.

The proposed installation location for the City Soft system is near the existing water heater to allow for efficient integration into the home’s main water distribution system. The softener’s backwash drain lines will be routed and connected to the existing main drain located behind the washer connecting to the washer drain. Technician will have to open up the drywall. at the proposed installation area. The system also requires a dedicated electrical outlet for operation and regeneration cycles. An outlet is provided. Once installed, the system will provide conditioned water to the entire home and help minimize the long-term effects of hard water and chlorine exposure on the plumbing system.

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. First we discovered that this electrical system is currently within the “end of life” range, which means the longevity is in question. Lastly, there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are up-to-date. However, the bedroom areas are missing some units. Lastly, we identified an areas with missing GFI protection, which is in the bathroom/laundry area. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. estimates.name: Water softener
estimates.summary:
A water softener reduces hard minerals—primarily calcium and magnesium—in your home's water. If you have hard water, installing one can make a noticeable difference in cleaning, bathing, and maintaining your plumbing and appliances.
Top 7 benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale buildup
Helps prevent the white, chalky deposits that form on faucets, showerheads, glass shower doors, and inside pipes and water-using appliances.
2. Softer-feeling skin and hair
Many people find their skin feels less dry and their hair feels easier to manage because soap rinses away more easily. A softener does not treat skin conditions, however.
3. Cleaner dishes and glassware
Reduces mineral spots, cloudy glassware, and residue left behind after washing.
4. Softer laundry
Clothes and towels may feel less stiff, and you can often use less laundry detergent because soft water allows soap to work more effectively.
5. Longer-lasting appliances
Helps limit mineral scale in water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and other equipment, potentially improving efficiency and reducing maintenance.
6. Less cleaning and scrubbing
Spend less time removing hard-water rings, crusty faucet deposits, and soap scum from sinks, tubs, and showers.
7. Potential savings over time
Reduced scale buildup, lower soap consumption, and fewer mineral-related repairs can help offset the cost of the system.

1. Helps prevent expensive water damage
If a pipe bursts, a toilet keeps running, or an appliance hose leaks, Flo can detect abnormal water flow and automatically close the main water valve. This can help protect floors, ceilings, cabinets, and finished basements.
2. Detects very small leaks
Its daily MicroLeak tests can identify leaks as small as a drop per minute, potentially catching a hidden plumbing leak before it becomes a bigger problem. ￼
3. Alerts you when you're away
Receive notifications through the app, text, email, or phone call when unusual water activity is detected. This is especially useful on vacations or when you have a second home.
4. Lets you shut off water remotely
You can turn your home's main water supply on or off using the app, without having to locate the valve in an emergency.
5. Tracks water usage and pressure
See usage history, flow rate, and water pressure, and learn which fixtures may be consuming more water than expected. It may also reveal running toilets or other wasteful leaks.

LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, Jim had some electrical questions/project ideas that he wanted answered and/or options provided. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, most of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel. However, there are a few recommendations we assessed during this inspection. 

First we discovered that the sub panel is older in age and not wired to todays electrical standards for safety. Lastly, there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. Lastly, we identified multiple areas with missing GFI protection, which include the kitchen and main bathroom. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

invoices.summary: This morning I arrived at the Radanovic family home to perfrom their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon my arrival Mr. Radanovic informed me he only wanted me to check his main service. I found only one discrepancy which was a shared neutral in the sub panel. Two separate circuits using one neutral can lead to an overload of the neutral. This overloading can cause damage, burning, or loss of neutral connection. IF this neutral were to lose its connection, the two circuits remaining energized could overload with no exit path and become potentially 240v circuits, destroying any appliances or equipment not rated to handle that much voltage. I have provided an option to replace these two circuits with an appropriate double pole breaker. That is my only recommendation for today. If you have any questions or concerns please do not hesitate to reach out. Thank you.

invoices.summary:
This afternoon I arrived at the Rivera family home for their complimentary system check, and to address concerns regarding a tripping circuit. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found it to be a roughly 40+ year old Crouse & Hinds 100A panel. The panel only has a small amount of available space remaining with tandem breakers being our only opportunity for edition in the panels current state. I found that the home has 5 window units which at times are all operating at once, this is absolutely grounds for causing a circuit to trip, especially with other electronics plugged into this same circuit. I am providing 3 options today, with one being a combination of the two in a bundle. 

The first option I will be providing is to install two tandem 20A breakers on our last available breakers available, and then to drill outside the home to run PVC conduit up the sides of the house to both the front bedroom window, and then the bedroom in the back alley between the homes. From there we will drill back into the house underneath the window where we will install a single outlet to shed the load for two window units on that circuit. 

The second option I will be providing is a full service upgrade. This option consists of replacing the entire main electrical service consisting of breaker panel, and outdoor meterbase and service wiring which runs through the roof of the porch and into the basement breaker panel. This option will include removing active fuse box circuits and incorporating them into the panel. 

The final option I will be providing is a bundle of both of these projects at once. In doing all of the work at once you are eligible for savings on the total project cost.

I have provided a copy of our companies membership during todays visit, this membership comes with a built in 15% discount which will be shown as potential savings within the provided estimates.

If you have any questions regarding these estimates, or concerns, please do not hesitate to reach out. Thank you for your time and we look forward to our next visit.

invoices.summary:
LPH completed a thorough electrical system check to evaluate the home’s overall electrical safety, reliability, and proper operation. During the evaluation, we inspected the electrical service, panel, circuit breakers, accessible wiring and connections, receptacles, switches, grounding and bonding, GFCI protection, smoke and carbon monoxide detection, and accessible interior and exterior electrical devices. We looked for signs of corrosion, moisture intrusion, physical damage, deteriorated components, loose connections, improper installations, and other potential electrical safety concerns.

During today’s evaluation, several receptacles were found to have deteriorated due to moisture exposure, corrosion, and physical damage. The following options were presented to the homeowner to address these concerns and improve the home’s electrical safety.

Approved Work Completed:

* Basement Receptacles: Replaced two existing receptacles with new weather-resistant GFCI receptacles. One existing device had suffered extensive corrosion due to moisture entering through the block walls, while the other had sustained physical damage that caused the face of the receptacle to break apart.
* Garage Receptacle: Replaced one worn-out receptacle showing signs of corrosion with a new weather-resistant GFCI receptacle to improve electrical shock protection and provide a more durable device.
* Back Porch Receptacle: Replaced one severely deteriorated exterior receptacle that lacked GFCI protection and was exposed to direct rainfall. Water had entered the electrical box and soaked the receptacle, leaving the device and screw terminals in a state of significant deterioration. LPH installed a new weather-resistant GFCI receptacle along with a proper in-use weatherproof cover to provide protection against moisture exposure while the receptacle is being used.
* Smoke Detector Installation: Installed five new battery-operated smoke detectors equipped with sealed 10-year lithium batteries throughout the home.
* Combination Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Detector: Installed one new battery-operated combination smoke and carbon monoxide detector equipped with a sealed 10-year lithium battery in the upstairs hallway to provide early warning of potential fire and carbon monoxide hazards.

The homeowner approved all presented options, and all approved work was completed. The newly installed receptacles and GFCI devices were tested, and proper operation was verified. The newly installed smoke and combination smoke and carbon monoxide detectors were also tested to verify proper operation.

All completed work was tested and verified to be operating properly at the time of service.

Today’s electrical system check evaluation and invoice will be emailed to the homeowner. Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. We appreciate the opportunity to take care of your electrical needs and look forward to servicing you again in the future.

estimates.name: Water softener
estimates.summary:
A water softener removes the minerals that make water “hard,” mainly calcium and magnesium. These minerals are naturally found in groundwater and can cause buildup on faucets, inside pipes, and in water-using appliances.
 1. Less white scale and mineral buildup
Helps prevent chalky deposits on faucets, showerheads, glass shower doors, and inside pipes and water heaters. Existing buildup may still need cleaning.
2. Soap and shampoo work better
Soft water makes it easier to create a lather, reduces soap scum, and can leave skin feeling less dry or tight after bathing.
3. Easier cleaning around the house
You may spend less time scrubbing white spots off sinks, tubs, shower walls, and fixtures.
4. Helps protect appliances
Reducing scale can help water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and other water-using equipment operate more efficiently and potentially last longer.
5. Softer-feeling laundry
Clothes and towels may feel less stiff, and fabrics may accumulate less mineral residue.
6. Can reduce plumbing maintenance
By limiting new scale formation, a softener can help prevent mineral deposits from narrowing pipes and clogging fixtures.
7. Potential savings on cleaning products
Because soap and detergent work more effectively in soft water, you may be able to use less of them, depending on the product and your water hardness.

invoices.summary: This morning I arrived at the Harrison family home for their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies. However, Mrs. Harrison informed me that they have had a history of blowing the fuses that supply power to their hot water heater. After performing an analysis of the system I noted several things. First, and most importantly, I noted that the wire which supplies power to the disconnect is undersized. The water heater requires a 30A (amp) supply in order to properly function. The wire which is currently in use is only rated AT MOST to handle 20A. The heater, the disconnect itself, and the breaker are all designed for a 30A load, where as the wiring, which acts as the bridge for all of these systems is only designed for 20A. Secondly, the Harrisons have been using 20A replacement fuses for this 30A system which is why they have been blowing with such frequency. Unfortunately, stepping the fuses up to 30A could become a potential fire hazard with the wire unable to handle that load. If 30A fuses are installed, that wire may burn and become damaged well before that fuse would ever blow. I have some indication of potential heat as it seems the ends of the stripped insulation on the hot wires has begun to soften and partially deform. I encouraged the Harrisons to continue to use these 20A fuses until they are able to replace the system. While they may blow more frequently, it is all that can be done until we replace the wiring, which is imperative. I have provided two options. The first which is most recommended would consist of replace the disconnect with a modern electrical disconnect requiring no fuses, and to replace the wire. The second option would be to replace the wire solely to avoid potential overheating. If you have any questions or if you would like to move forward with these options, please do not hesitate to reach out. Thank you, and we will see you in our next visit!

LPH arrived at the residence to perform a thorough electrical system check evaluation. During the evaluation, we reviewed the electrical panel and breakers, inspected for signs of overheating and deterioration, discussed whole-home surge protection, and evaluated the exterior receptacles for proper weather protection and safe operation. We also discussed the installation of customer-supplied exterior light fixtures.

During the inspection, LPH identified three older-style Cutler-Hammer arc-fault breakers exhibiting excessive heat buildup and extensive carbon dust accumulation on the electrical panel cover. These conditions may indicate deterioration of the breakers and warrant replacement to help restore reliable circuit protection and reduce the risk of continued overheating.

We also discussed the benefits of installing whole-home surge protection at the main electrical service. Transient voltage spikes can occur from utility fluctuations, lightning activity, and the everyday operation of electrical equipment throughout the home. Over time, these voltage fluctuations can contribute to premature wear of sensitive electronic components in appliances, LED lighting drivers, and other household electronics. The homeowner has experienced premature LED bulb failures and flickering throughout the home. Although these symptoms can have multiple causes, whole-home surge protection provides an added layer of defense against damaging voltage surges and helps protect the home’s electrical devices and appliances.

Additionally, LPH identified the need to replace the rear porch receptacle with a weather-resistant GFCI receptacle and an extra-duty, in-use bubble cover. The existing cover cannot close while the awning remains plugged in, leaving the receptacle vulnerable to moisture and water intrusion. The recommended replacement will provide protection from the elements while the awning is connected, helping reduce the risk of corrosion, nuisance tripping, and premature receptacle failure.

All findings and recommended options were thoroughly reviewed with the homeowner, including the replacement of the three arc-fault breakers, installation of whole-home surge protection, replacement of the rear porch receptacle and protective cover, and installation of the homeowner-supplied exterior light fixtures.

The homeowner elected to move forward with all recommended options. The work has been scheduled for November 9th, and a down payment was collected.

estimates.name: Whole home surge protection
estimates.summary:
Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

invoices.summary:
Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 5 grains per gallon (GPG) and the chlorine level to be . 5 ppm. A hardness level of 5 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, shower heads , and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a City Soft water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. Benefits of the system include improved soap and detergent performance, reduced spotting and scaling, softer-feeling water, and increased protection and efficiency of plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances.

The proposed installation location for the City Soft system is near the existing water heater. The water softener inlet would come from the water meter approximately 20’ away. The softener’s backwash drain lines will be routed and connected to the existing main drain located near the water meter. The system also requires a dedicated electrical outlet for operation and regeneration cycles. The home’s electrical panel is located approximately 20 feet away, and an outlet will need to be installed and provided at the equipment location prior to or as part of the installation. Once installed, the system will provide conditioned water to the entire home and help minimize the long-term effects of hard water and chlorine exposure on the plumbing system.

invoices.summary:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, Susan had a few electrical questions prior to electrical inspection that we went through and answered today.

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel.

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. Thirdly, we identified an area with missing GFI protection, which is for the washer. Lastly, we identified about half of the outlets and switches in the home that were not replaced and still contained backstabbed style connections. This connection style will increase the chances of these connections, loosening up overtime, damaging device(look shown for the switch in the garage), and could cause power loss or safety issues. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

invoices.summary:
Out to home today for the yearly plumbing system check. Upon arrival to home, there was one major concern. Homeowner stated they noticed water in their garage about a week ago. Homeowner believed that it may have been from the roof at first as they are having repairs performed. They were able to identify moisture coming from the laundry room. Upon closer inspection, found that the copper lines feeding the laundry valve had a pin-hole. Made homeowner aware that LPH will need to open access behind to perform repairs to piping. LPH will open access, however we do not offer any repair services for walls, ceilings, or trim. 

From there, performed the full home plumbing system check. Tested water quality inside the home to verify the water softener is working properly. Identified that the salt tank is getting low and needs salt. Tested water pressure to the home. Found water pressure to be higher than recommended at this time at 80 PSI. Suggested repair option to correct water pressure inside the home to a recommended 40-60 PSI. Also performed inspection and flush of water heater. 

No other concerns are present at this time. Went over pricing for recommended repairs. Homeowner approved laundry repairs at this time. Shut down water to home. Cut access from garage to pinpoint the leak. Disconnected old hoses from washer/dryer combo and removed old valve assembly. Installed new risers from garage access in pex piping including new service valves inside the wall. Per homeowner request, removed outdoor faucet accessible from garage. Installed and mounted washer machine valves inside access. Due to size of new valves installed, the door was unable to close properly. Prior to the valve replacement, the old washer hoses were tucked inside the wall. When installing the washer hoses, routed new hoses through valve access rather than the lower opening to prevent the new hoses from kinking. Lastly, LPH did not reconnect the steam function for the dryer per homeowner request. Upon completion of repairs, restored water to the home and tested for leaks. No leaks found at this time. One year guarantee given on repairs performed today. Remaining estimates provided are good for 60 days. Thank you for trusting LPH.

Today, I completed an annual electrical system inspection and found that the main electrical panel is approximately 40 years old. The typical lifespan of a main electrical panel is 25–30 years, depending on maintenance, servicing, and overall condition.

The existing main panel is a Challenger panel. These panels have been associated with breaker reliability issues, including breakers failing to trip when required. This can lead to overheating, damage to connected components, and potential electrical hazards. Given the age of the panel, there is an increased concern regarding the reliability and safe operation of its components.

I recommend replacing both the main electrical panel and the subpanel. Although the subpanel appears to be newer than the main panel, its exact age could not be determined during the inspection.

Additionally, I observed that the kitchen lacks GFCI protection at applicable receptacles. GFCI protection is required in designated locations where electrical receptacles may be exposed to water or moisture, in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements. I recommend upgrading the affected receptacles to provide the appropriate level of protection.

All recommended solutions were presented to the homeowner, and the invoice was emailed for review.

invoices.summary:
This estimate includes having Lancaster Plumbing and Heating make a warranty repair on the water softener. It would include removal of the mechanical parts of the head that control the stages of the water softeners regeneration. This repair is covered under both the manufacturer’s parts warranty and Lancaster Plumbing and Heating’s labor warranty.

We came out today to take a look at the water softener because it was showing an error code. The error code was indicating that there was a motor failure. This usually means that during regeneration the computer was telling the spacer stack assembly to switch positions and it took too long or got stuck.

The technician began diagnosing the issue by disconnecting power and trying a hard reset of the electrical components. This did not fix the issue, so the technician provided an estimate to perform a warranty repair. The warranty repair included replacing the spacer stack assembly, and the motor that drives the functions for the spacer stack assembly. Once the repair was completed, the technician put the water softener through an abbreviated regeneration twice in order to verify that the system was now working properly. Both attempts on the abbreviated regeneration were successful and everything was in proper operation at this time.

The technician did discover a secondary issue, but it had to do with the Brian tank. The homeowners have been using salt pellets instead of salt crystals, and this is caused bridging within the brine tank. The technician suggested that the salt be dug out of the brine tank in order to fix this issue. Moving forward we did recommend the use of salt crystals because they do dissolve easier with these particular systems.

If you have any other questions or concerns that arise after today’s visit, please do not hesitate to give us a call. Thank you for continuing to trust Lancaster Plumbing and Heating with all of your home service needs. 
This estimate includes having Lancaster Plumbing and Heating unload the brine tank in order to remove a large chunk of salt pellets.

invoices.summary:
The customer mentioned that a leak was occurring beneath the bathtub after taking a bath. The customer also noted that the tub spout had been struck while a child was taking a bath. The technician removed the tub/shower valve trim to inspect the area behind the valve, which is located behind the master bathroom vanity, avoiding the need to cut an access hole in the wall. No visible water damage or signs of active leaking were found during the inspection.
The technician then inspected the tub strainer and found it to be very loose. After removing the strainer, the technician discovered that plumber’s putty had not been applied to help seal the strainer in conjunction with the rubber gasket beneath the tub drain. The technician applied plumber’s putty and properly tightened the tub strainer to help ensure a watertight seal.
After completing the repair, the technician and customer filled the bathtub three separate times to test for leaks. No further leaking was observed during testing. Based on these results, the technician did not find it necessary to remove the wood paneling on the kitchen ceiling to access the area beneath the bathtub.

invoices.summary:
Service Call Summary – Booster Pump Inspection

A technician was dispatched today after the homeowner reported hearing the booster pump activate when no water was being used. The homeowner stated that this issue has been occurring intermittently for several months. Upon inspection, the technician checked the unit’s air bladder pressure and confirmed that it was at the proper level. All plumbing fixtures, including toilets and faucets, were inspected to ensure there were no visible drips or leaks. No error codes were present on the unit, and the system correctly indicated when the pump was operating and when it was in standby mode. The homeowner mentioned that he had replaced a toilet flapper several weeks ago. A possible cause of the issue is that the toilet flapper is not sealing properly, allowing water to slowly leak into the bowl and causing the toilet to periodically refill. This could trigger the booster pump to activate even when no other water is being used. The technician monitored the system for at least 15 minutes while downstairs to verify that the pump did not activate unexpectedly. During this observation period, the pump operated as expected and did not cycle on randomly.nAt the time of inspection, the system was functioning properly, and no issues were found with the booster pump or its air bladder. Thank you for trusting LPH with your service needs!

C. Exhaust is being pulled back into the combustion intake due to the venting installation

E. Microbial growth was found inside the supply ductwork
F. Evaporator coil is pitched slightly backwards
G. Some issues on the supply ductwork where multiple supply runs are installed right next to each other. There was also a damaged connection to the first floor bathroom. 
H. Customer has issues with 2nd floor maintaining temperatures in heating and cooling seasons. 

We went over all of these findings, and are ordering parts to install a dual UV system, oversized MERV 16 filter to improve air quality and airflow drastically, new vent terminations. Thank you for trusting LPH with your plumbing needs. We strive to provide professional, high-quality service on every visit, and your feedback helps us continue improving.

The homeowner requested that the heat tape and insulation under the mobile home be inspected. The homeowner has lived at the residence for approximately 17 years and has not experienced any issues with the water lines freezing.

Technician tested the electrical outlet supplying the heat tape and verified that the outlet is properly grounded and operating correctly. During the inspection, Technician observed that the water main is currently wrapped with approximately 1/8-inch-thick Seal Seal foam insulation, which is typically used for foundation applications. This insulation provides minimal protection against freezing temperatures.

Technician recommends replacing the existing insulation on the water main with 1/2-inch to 1-inch-thick pipe insulation to provide additional protection from freezing temperatures. Approximately 25 feet of insulation would be required to properly insulate the exposed water main.

Technician also recommends insulating the pit where the water main enters the mobile home from below grade. Regular R-19 insulation should be installed around the pit to help retain heat and provide additional protection for the water main during freezing temperatures.

invoices.summary:
LPH completed a heating system inspection on a 10-year-old Trane gas furnace. At this time, all system components are operating properly.

During the inspection, LPH observed that the blower wheel was slightly dirty and noted potential microbial growth in the supply plenum. LPH also found that the blower motor capacitor was slightly out of specification.

Recommendations:
LPH recommends performing a furnace cleaning to remove buildup from the blower wheel and clean the supply plenum. LPH also recommends replacing the blower motor capacitor to help maintain proper system operation and reduce the risk of unexpected breakdowns.

Performing these preventative maintenance services can help improve airflow, support system efficiency, and reduce the risk of premature component failure. If microbial growth is confirmed, appropriate cleaning and treatment should be performed as needed.

LPH also discussed indoor air quality (IAQ) package options with the homeowner and provided available options for consideration. The homeowner respectfully declined the recommended services at this time.

LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, Jason reported some concerns and project ideas for this home. We were informed that Jason wanted options for new panels to be installed to replace the existing main and sub panel. Jason also wanted an option to install all new washer and dryer receptacles in the garage for easier accessibility. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, most of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel. However, there are a few recommendations we assessed during this inspection. 

First we discovered that these panels are the Zinsco brand, which is a brand that lost their UL listing many years ago and is no longer allowed to be installed. This brand along, with two other brands that have similar issues, no longer have any replacement parts or breakers available. Second we noticed that this electrical system is currently within the “end of life” range, which means the longevity is in question. Lastly, there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does not meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was identifying that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are either not currently installed or past their 10 year lifespan. Lastly, we identified multiple areas with missing GFI protection, which is the bathroom, the washer in the basement, kitchen and exterior. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

invoices.summary: This morning we arrived at the Lowrie family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon our arrival, Mrs. Lowrie informed us of some concerns related to the outdoor shed, and a receptacle that did not seem to be working. We performed a thorough evaluation of the shed and found that the breaker supplying this building was switched off. We reset the breaker and power was restored to the shed. As far as the outlet, we determined that the device had an internal failure due to exposure to moisture. The cover on the receptacle is not rated to be in direct exposure to the elements. We provided an option to replace this receptacle and install a bubble cover. We discussed with Mrs. Lowrie her distaste for the color and performance of some of the switches and outlets in the home which are ivory at the moment. I provided an estimate to replace all of the switches and outlets in the home due to their age, as well as the ability to pick the color the Lowrie’s would prefer. Finally, we provided an estimate to replace the homes full service, and secondarily the breaker panel alone. The reason is primarily the age of the service, on average panels last between 30-35 years, this panel has since eclipsed that. In total we found no major discrepancies, but encouraged the replacement of the outdoor receptacle which has failed. If you have any questions or concerns please do not hesitate to reach out to us. Thank you and take care!

The existing 1.5 HP submersible well pump is approximately 20 years old. Technician recommends replacing the existing pump with a new 2 HP submersible well pump to provide the appropriate pumping capacity for the depth of the well. A 2 HP submersible well pump is rated for well depths up to approximately 900 feet. The existing pump is currently set at approximately 760 feet, and the total well depth is approximately 935 feet.

Due to the depth of the well and the pump setting, 1” galvanized well pipe is required instead of 1” poly well pipe. Technician recommends replacing the existing 20-year-old galvanized well pipe and well wire along with the new well pump. Replacing these components will provide new piping and wiring throughout the well and help eliminate potential issues associated with the age of the existing components.

The existing well control box is also approximately 20 years old. Technician recommends replacing the control box with the new pump to ensure the electrical components are properly matched to the new 2 HP pump. Technician also recommends replacing the existing pressure tank and tank tee assembly. The new tank assembly would include a 40/60 pressure switch, pressure gauge, pressure relief valve, and drain-down valve. Replacing these components at the same time will provide a complete upgrade of the well system’s pumping and pressure-control components.

Technician also recommends installing a whole-house sediment filter to help reduce sediment entering the home’s plumbing system from the well water. The sediment filter will help protect plumbing fixtures, water treatment equipment, and other plumbing components from sediment

invoices.summary:
Upon arrival, tech met with Paige. She stated that when she runs her kitchen sink, it backups up from a floor drain in the garage. It’s an on and off issue. The downstairs bathroom they noticed also has water on the floor which they haven’t used in years. They had a backup 2 weeks ago but her husband was able to restore flow. Tech had her flush a toilet and run the kitchen sink, there is no backup at this time. When tech looked at down the trap that’s located in the basement, and observed that the pipe itself was rotting away. She also stated that her bathtub was backing up. We ran water and it backed up within seconds. Tech presented two options. With her approval, we performed a video inspection. We first inspected the kitchen branch from a cleanout in the garage going towards the stack. We came across some pvc and cast iron. It was holding water, had buildup and was deteriorating. We then inspected from the trap back. We came across deteriorating cast iron pipe holding water and some buildup. From the trap out to the city main was orangeburg pipe that transitions to pvc at the curb. The orangeburg was warping, holding water, debris and had some sections being squished due to ground settlement. Those sections were not round but oval causing a loss in circumference. The pvc had some buildup. Tech explained that the pipe is compromised and strongly suggests a replacement. Tech presented a solution. She does not want to move forward at this times. She is going to look over the option with her husband. Tech will follow-up. Thanks for trusting Lancaster plumbing and heating.

This is to do a sewer line replacement from the first floor toilet to the curb. LPH would use an excavating machine to expose the existing compromised pipe. Once the compromised pipe is located, LPH will remove it and then lay a bed of crushed stone down. LPH will hand excavate on the inside of the home using jackhammers and other equipment to expose the existing sewer line. Once the sewer line is exposed, LPH will remove it and then lay down a bed of crushed stone. LPH will then start to connect the new scheduled 40 PVC sewer line and floor drain. Once the sewer line is connected, LPH will use hydraulic cement on the inside and outside foundation wall. Another bed of crushed stone will be placed on top of the PVC pipe and backfill will begin. Backfill will be tamped to a raked finish. The homeowner is responsible to finish the landscaping. The concrete in the basement will be completed to a smooth finish. The sidewalk out front will be filled with crushed stone until we finish the concrete (weather permitting) The concrete is included in this estimate. We will install a new Saniflo toilet in the basement bathroom, connect the vanity to it and then connect onto the stack. The homeowner is responsible to moving all personal belongings in the basement area we will be performing the work. The kitchen line will be re routed above ground in the garage. This will cancel the garage floor drain. We will install a new laundry tub with a pump and connect the washing machine and basement kitchen sink. It will then tie onto the sewer line.

invoices.summary:
Performed heating system check on a Bryant gas furnace. Noticed during the check that the gas valve on the furnace was over feeding. Attempted to adjust gas pressures as per the manual by locking system into low and high fire. Both low and high fire pressures were significantly higher than what was stated on the rating plate. High fire was running at about 4.1 inches of water column whereas we wanted between 3.2-3.8 (ideally 3.5). Low fire was sitting at around 1.1 inches of water column whereas we wanted between 0.5-0.65. Gas pressure was not able to be adjusted at the gas valve when locked into low and high fire, therefore I recommend replacing the entire gas valve as the over feeding is a problem both for safety and efficiency of the unit. 

Offered to change the gas valve with David and Kathleenk’s approval. Ordered part from Peirce-Phelps's and it will be ready for counter pickup tomorrow. Will be returning sometime later this week/early next week to perform that work.

All other measurements for this visit can be referred to on the system evaluation form.

invoices.summary:
We were called out to provide options to remedy any power loss concern for Evan and his family. Upon arrival, we spoke with Evan, who informed us of what exactly he was looking for in portable generators systems, and wanted some clarity on some information that he researched on his own time. After speaking with Evan, we got a great understanding of what he was looking for to be installed in this home and for length of the time that he planned on staying in this home. We were looking to install a new 50 amp plug on the exterior of the home with a twist lock style receptacle, a new 50 amp breaker that will be protected and controlled by an interlock kit that will fit this panel cover exactly. We also looked at the outdoor unit to assess the amperage/wattage usage and noticed that it will work with the two generators that Evan was looking into(8,500W or 11,000W). However, we did inform Evan that if he went with the 8.5 KW style generator, he would be very limited in total usage after the outdoor unit, freezer, and well pump were under use.

Evan also had a question/concern with his water pipe for his water heater, and if it needed to be properly grounded/bonded. We informed Evan that the equipment grounding conductor, feeding this water heater is acting as the main grounding source and bonding it by other means would be more on the redundant side than actual productive dispersion side. If Evan still wanted a separate ground wire installed from the main panel to the water heater location, we could take care of that. However, it is not needed by national electric code standards, per NEC 250.104(B). 

The options provided and invoice for today’s visits will be emailed to Evan for his record and to review. We thank you for allowing us into your home and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

Thank you for having us out today to look at your humidifier and go over options to address concerns. To recap, there is significant biological growth on the existing humidifier and the damper is broken. 

We went over airflow, source control, and the humidity needs of a home this size. Given the size, I did not recommend using another bypass humidifier due to capacity. I also recommended a germicidal UV and large media filter. The UV will directly combat microbes in the air. The enhanced filter will significantly improve fine particle capture and reduces the air friction inside the system to allow for better and easier airflow. 

I am sending over options for both humidifiers, as well as a germicidal UV system and large Media Filter.

invoices.summary: This afternoon I arrived at the Mitchell family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon my arrival, Mr. Mitchell informed me of some concerns related to the location of his breaker panel. Upon performing an inspection I found the breaker panel to be located in the downstairs bathroom. According to NEC revision 1993, breaker panels are not allowed to be located in any bathroom facilities, The code defines a bathroom (Article 100) as any area including a basin (sink) with one or more fixtures like a toilet, tub, or shower. Even a half-bath or powder room with just a sink and a toilet legally meets this definition. Therefore, overcurrent devices and service panels are still forbidden under NEC 240.24(E). For this reason, I have built the Mitchell’s an option to relocate their main electrical panel to a separate location in the basement outside the bathroom, and away from other water piping related systems. Otherwise I presented several other estimates regarding some code compliance features in the home. Ultimately I found the main electrical systems to be in goof physical condition with no signs of deterioration. If you have any questions or concerns related to todays visit, please do not hesitate to reach out! Thank you for having us out today and I look forward to our next visit!

During today’s visit, we did not complete the full plumbing system check. The homeowner was more concerned about a leak under her bathroom faucet, and in addition she wanted us to look at the major components of the plumbing system, which included the water softener and water heater. We tested the water and discovered the water softener to be doing its job, but the homeowner is still having issues with water staining on her dishes and glassware. 

We did set the water softener to soften the water from 20 grains instead of 18 and in addition to that the water softener was only regenerating every 21 days. This is also a setting that we changed so the water softener would regenerate more often since the water is harder in this area. We also discussed how the discharge line for the water softener is not to code. We did provide an estimate to correct this issue.

We did provide estimates for two other things that we discovered. The expansion tank that is installed at the cold water inlet on the water heater, has failed and should be replaced. In addition, the outside hose faucet located at the rear of the home, leaks from both the vacuum breaker and packing nut when the hose faucet is turned on and connected to a hose. The homeowner only had us replace the cartridges in the two handle lavatory faucet in the primary on suite bathroom. 

While replacing the cartridges, the brass stem extension screw, broke off inside the old cartridge. The technician due diligence with trying to source the part three of our vendors, but had no success. The technician discovered that the particular faucet is no longer manufactured and they no longer make that specific set, screw to anchor the handle down to the cartridge. The technician did share all of this information with the homeowner and was able to direct her to a place where she can go and look at new faucets. Once they have those picked out, they will give us a call back to approve the estimate that was provided to have us install. Customer supplied lavatory faucets.

If you have any other questions or concerns that arise after today’s visit, please do not hesitate to give us a call. Thank you for continuing to trust Lancaster Plumbing and Heating with all of your home service needs.

I had the pleasure of meeting with the homeowner today to discuss options for converting their existing oil-fired boiler to a natural gas system.

The homeowner has already contacted UGI regarding the installation of a natural gas meter, but the meter has not yet been installed. During our consultation, we reviewed two replacement options: a high-efficiency combi boiler that would provide both heating and domestic hot water, and a traditional gas boiler paired with an indirect hot water storage tank.

We also discussed the additional work required for the conversion. If the homeowner chooses the conventional gas boiler option, the existing chimney will need to be properly lined before installation. Additionally, a new dedicated electrical circuit will need to be run from the main electrical panel to the boiler to meet current electrical code requirements and pass inspection.
