invoices.summary:
Today, I completed the annual electrical system inspection and found the main electrical panel to be in very poor condition. The panel has significant rust and is over 30 years old. Due to its age and deteriorated condition, I recommend replacing the main electrical panel to help ensure the safety and reliability of the home’s electrical system. As electrical components age, breakers can become less reliable, increasing the risk of failure, overheating, and potential electrical hazards.

John was not present during today’s inspection; however, his mother-in-law accompanied me during the evaluation. I informed her of my findings and recommendations and advised her that I would contact John directly to discuss them.

The homeowner also reported that the breakers trip when using a portable heater or air conditioner in the attic. These appliances draw a significant amount of power, which may exceed the capacity of the existing circuit. I recommended installing a dedicated circuit in the attic to accommodate these appliances and help prevent recurring breaker trips.

Lastly, the homeowner reported that the exterior outlet and lamppost were not functioning. Upon evaluation, I found that the GFCI outlet had failed and was no longer supplying power. I also found that the switch controlling the lamppost was beginning to fail. I informed the homeowner that replacing the GFCI outlet and the failing switch would help restore proper functionality to both fixtures.

Recommendations:

* Replace the main electrical panel due to its age, significant rust, and poor condition.
* Install a dedicated attic circuit, if appropriate, to accommodate the portable heater or air conditioner and help prevent breaker trips.
* Replace the failed exterior GFCI outlet.
* Replace the failing lamppost switch.

invoices.summary:
Technician investigated concerns of sewer gas odor entering the main-floor master bathroom shower area and laundry room. Technician checked the water level in the master bathroom shower drain and inspected the 3” vent termination through the roof, which is located directly above the master bathroom. The 3” vent was found to extend approximately 6–8” above the roof.

Technician explained that windy conditions can create a Venturi effect at the vent termination, potentially drawing air through the vent system and affecting the water seal in the shower P-trap. Wind can also create direct downdrafts through the vent, which may contribute to sewer gas odors entering the home. Technician discussed raising the existing vent termination and adding a U-bend configuration using two 3” 90° fittings to help reduce the potential for wind-driven downdrafts.

Technician also recommended installing a 2” Trap Guard in the shower drain. The Trap Guard allows water to drain normally while providing an additional barrier to help prevent sewer gas from entering the home if the P-trap water seal is compromised.

The main-floor laundry room is equipped with two laundry drains, each with a 2” P-trap. One of the drains is not regularly used, and the water in the P-trap may be evaporating and allowing sewer gas to enter the laundry room. The unused drain will either be used for the dehumidifier discharge to maintain the P-trap water seal or capped to prevent sewer gas from entering through the drain.

The homeowner plans to purchase a trap guard before addressing the vent through the roof.

Upon performing an analysis of this system I found that our breaker, which was installed at the time of the meter replacement, was only producing an output of 67 volts, as opposed to the 240v requirement. I identified that the PV system was OFF prior to doing these tests, and removed the breaker. I determined that this had to be a breaker fault considering the system was off and offering no interference. I determined it would be wise to replace the breaker since it was covered under warranty. After replacement I tested the breaker both under PV power, and with the solar disconnected and was receiving proper voltage. Mrs. Trolley also asked me to investigate a low voltage system and see if it was salvageable for speakers, which I found it not to be. I cut back the wires so they were out of view. The only recommendation I had was to update several smoke detectors. If you have any questions please do not hesitate to reach out!

LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, homeowner reported some issues with her outside outlets not working correctly. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel.

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. Lastly, we identified two areas with missing GFI protection, which is the bathroom and for the washer in the basement. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. The basic electrical package was approved and completed today. We installed all new GFI protection for both exterior receptacles, GFI receptacles on the first floor, and for the bathroom/washer receptacle in the basement. All receptacles were to the homeowners approval and tested and working properly prior to leaving today. However, we had to adjust the box in the basement bathroom/laundry area, which involved an open section of drywall that we cannot repair. We sealed this area up with white silicone and took $50 off the total job to satisfy this issue. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

We were called out today because of a leak that was discovered at the geothermal pre-heating water tank. Upon arrival Rachel briefed the technician about the leak that was discovered and then took the technician down to the basement to see exactly what was going on. As the technician began inspection the the tank and surrounding area, it was quickly determined that the leak wasn’t going to be repairable. The leak itself is coming from the tank, and not a part or water line connected to the tank. After sharing this info with the home the technician did discuss a couple of options that could be done moving forward, but wanted to speak with the field supervisor about what would be best. Before the technician was able to go over the estimates completely, Rachel had to depart for a scheduled doctor’s appointment. The technician finished the estimates and was able to email them over in order for Rachel to look at while she was in the waiting room at her appointment.

This estimate includes having Lancaster Plumbing and Heating replace the standard electric water heater with a hybrid water heater. In addition we would also remove, properly dispose of the existing geothermal pre-heating water tank and cap the existing water lines.

Once our estimate was approved, we went to work with removal of the existing tanks. Before draining the water heaters down, we did have to figure out how to disable the research pump for the existing geothermal preheating tank. After some back-and-forth with our HVAC managers and doing some research, we discovered that we could disconnect the pump from its power source and in doing so would not interrupt The heating aspect of the geothermal system. Once the new water heater was in, we restored water to the home and began filling out the tank. Once the tank was filled, we were able to inspect all new connections to ensure everything was flowing properly and water tight. The Weber’s were extremely happy with the effort we put in today and with the final look of the install.

If you have any other questions or concerns that arise after today’s visit, please do not hesitate to give us a call. Thank you for continuing to trust Lancaster Plumbing and Heating with all of your home service needs.

estimates.name: Everything Option
estimates.summary:
Exterior Receptacle Replacement

LPH will replace three exterior receptacles that are not rated for outdoor use. During the evaluation, visible corrosion was found inside the receptacles, along with rust on the mounting screws, indicating moisture intrusion over time. Two of these receptacles are exposed to direct rainfall and currently have standard gray covers that do not provide adequate protection when water reaches the devices.

To help prevent further moisture damage and improve protection against the outdoor elements, LPH will replace all three receptacles with weather-resistant devices. The two existing gray covers will be upgraded to extra-duty, weatherproof in-use bubble covers, which are designed to provide protection while cords remain plugged in. All associated electrical boxes will be properly resealed to help prevent additional water intrusion.

Why this matters: Exterior receptacles are continually exposed to changing weather conditions, and moisture can accelerate corrosion, compromise electrical connections, and increase the risk of electrical faults. These upgrades will provide improved protection against rain and moisture while helping extend the service life of the receptacles.

Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

estimates.summary:
A Moen Flo is a smart water monitoring and leak-detection system for your home. It’s designed to help prevent expensive water damage from leaking pipes, broken hoses, running toilets, or burst plumbing.
What does a Moen Flo do?
1. Detects leaks
Monitors the water flowing through your home's main water line.
Learns your household's normal water-use patterns.
Can detect unusual water flow that may indicate a leak.
2. Automatically shuts off your water
If it detects a serious leak or abnormal water use, it can automatically turn off your home's main water supply to help prevent flooding.
You can also shut the water off remotely using the app, depending on your setup.
3. Monitors water usage
Shows how much water your household uses.
Can help identify unusual usage, such as a toilet that keeps running.
4. Sends alerts to your phone
- Notifies you about possible leaks, unusual water use, and other problems.
Moen says its system can detect some leaks as small as one drop per minute. It needs to be properly installed and configured, and it isn't a guarantee against all water damage.

invoices.summary: Tech arrived and found a four flash code on the smart screen on the Water heater. It is an electric water heater prestige model. That code states that the unit shut itself off due to how high the temperature was getting. Tech found that the thermostat was tripped. Tech reset thermostat and the code still read. Tech then checked voltage and continuity to the elements and found both to be where they should be. Tech then disconnected the wires going to the smart screen then plugged it back in. The code went away at this time. Tech called tech support to find out the underlying problem. Tech explained everything to tech support, tech support stated that there is no active code so they cannot help. Tech was unable to figure out why the thermostat tripped. When tech was putting everything together the unit kept shutting off due to it sensing water. Tech verified that there is nothing wet touching the unit. Currently there is a solid red light indicating that the sensor is wet. Tech sees rust on the unit and believes that the unit could be leaking from the tank ever so slightly. Homeowner stated that the frequently have to go to the unit and Manuel open the valve that shuts the unit off. As of now homeowner has hot water, tech made sure to stay to ensure water got hot. Tech found it very peculiar that the water heater was rusting at such a young age. Homeowner is on a well, so technician wanted to check the acidity in the water. Technician found that the water is acidic and it is at 6. You want it around seven because that is neutral. Technician left a quote to install an acid neutralizer. Homeowners have to discuss financing and then reach out to Lph. Thank you for trusting Lph.

The homeowner would like to install a new toilet in the main floor laundry room. To complete the installation, the technician will modify the existing drain and water supply piping.

Technician performed a thorough plumbing system inspection on all accessible plumbing fixtures throughout the home to evaluate overall operation, drainage, water flow, and visible plumbing conditions. During the inspection, technician identified a few concerns within the plumbing system and discussed recommended solutions with the homeowner to address the issues found. Technician reviewed available repair and improvement options to help maintain proper system performance and prevent future plumbing problems.

estimates.name: Everything option
estimates.summary:
The trip lever/tub stopper in the 2nd-floor hallway bathroom bathtub is not functioning because the existing lever is broken. The bathtub is equipped with a PVC Watco waste and overflow assembly. Technician recommends replacing the broken trip lever with a new PVC Watco trip lever compatible with the existing waste and overflow assembly. This will restore proper operation of the bathtub stopper, allowing the stopper to open and close as intended for filling and draining the bathtub.

The existing second-floor hallway bathroom toilet is a standard-height, round-bowl toilet that is older and outdated. Technician recommends replacing the existing toilet with a new comfort-height, elongated-bowl toilet. The comfort-height design provides added comfort and ease of use, while the elongated bowl offers additional seating space. The new toilet will also use less water per flush, helping improve water efficiency and reduce overall water consumption. Technician will remove the existing toilet, install the new toilet with a new wax ring and supply connection as needed, and test the toilet to ensure proper flushing, filling, and operation with no leaks.

During the annual plumbing system check, Technician noticed that the main-floor kitchen sink drain gurgles when draining. Technician inspected the kitchen sink drainage system and found that the drain is not properly vented. Improper venting can restrict airflow within the drainage system, causing gurgling noises and potentially affecting the drain’s ability to discharge wastewater properly. Technician recommends installing an air admittance valve (AAV) on the kitchen sink drain to provide the necessary airflow and help maintain proper drainage. This will help equalize pressure within the drain piping, reduce gurgling noises, and allow wastewater to drain more efficiently. Technician will install the air admittance valve in an accessible location and test the kitchen sink drain to verify proper operation.

During the plumbing system inspection, Technician noticed that the existing sump pump pit is not equipped with a sump pump. Water was present inside the pit, indicating that groundwater is entering the sump pit and that the basement may be susceptible to groundwater accumulation and potential flooding. estimates.name: Sewer line replacement
estimates.summary:
This is to do a sewer line replacement from the trap on the inside of the basement to the curb. LPH would use an excavating machine to expose the existing compromised pipe. Once the compromised pipe is located, LPH will remove it and then lay a bed of crushed stone down. LPH will hand excavate on the inside of the home using jackhammers and other equipment to expose the existing sewer line. Once the sewer line is exposed, LPH will remove it and then lay down a bed of crushed stone. LPH will then start to connect the new scheduled 40 PVC sewer line. Once the sewer line is connected, LPH will use hydraulic cement on the inside and outside foundation wall. Another bed of crushed stone will be placed on top of the PVC pipe and backfill will begin. Backfill will be tamped to a raked finish. The homeowner is responsible to finish the landscaping. The concrete in the basement will be completed to a smooth finish. The sidewalk out front will be filled with crushed stone until we finish the concrete (weather permitting). The concrete is included in this estimate. The trap will be relocated to the outside of the home. Once we have the pipe cut at the curb, we will perform a video inspection from the curb to the main. If there are any concerns, additional options will be presented to the homeowner.

This estimate includes having Lancaster Plumbing and Heating clear a blockage at the kitchen sink. It will involve disassembling the tubular PVC drain piping from the food waste disposer down to the p-trap.

We came out today because of a leak leak and back up at the food waste disposer. Upon arrival, the homeowners explained what was going on when they discovered the issue which allowed the technician quickly determine what the issue was. The technician discovered that the locking collar for the equipment was not locked in place, and in addition determined that that side of the double bay sink was backed up. 

After further discussion, the technician learned that there were certain things going into the disposer that shouldn’t have been. We also learned that too much food was going down at one time. An estimate was provided to take apart the center drain outlet in order to clear the blockage. Upon disassembling the drain, we did discover a large quantity of food between the first section of drain piping and the second fitting that attaches to the P-trap. We were able to quickly get the blockage clear and the drain piping reassembled. Once everything was back together, the technician tested everything to ensure there were zero leaks and proper flow.

We did provide an estimate to install a customer supplied food waste disposer and to also replace the center drain outlet piping. We are not saying that there needs to be an immediate replacement. This would be a preventative maintenance replacement due to the amount of rust we saw at the locking collar. We also don’t know the condition of the rubber gasket that creates a water tight seal. At this time, everything was in proper operation and leak free.

If you have any other questions or concerns that arise after today’s visit, please do not hesitate to give us a call. Thank you for continuing to trust Lancaster Plumbing and Heating with all of your home service needs.

LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, no electrical concerns/questions were reported prior to our electrical inspection. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel.

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. First, we discovered that the water meter doe meet today’s grounding standards but the gas piping does not. This grounding system is designed to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was identifying that the existing smoke detectors are either expired or missing. Lastly, we identified that the front exterior receptacle is no longer secured to the wall. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. invoices.summary: Out to home today for fluctuating and low water pressure throughout the home. Homeowner states this has been an ongoing issue for quite some time now. Upon arrival, tech met with Sam. He owns the garage apartment in the back alleyway of 335. He stated all lines are flowing but whenever it rains he has water come out of a hole in the floor and floods the garage. He had a company out to the home and attempted to cable it but was unable to restore flow. They told him he needed a jetting. Tech observed the water in the hole in the garage floor. Tech believes it is a floor drain. The gutter connecting onto that line is right outside the foundation wall. Tech presented two options. Sam wanted to move forward with the jetting since the last company was unsuccessful with the cable. With his approval, techs performed a sewer line jetting. Tech had to run a cable due to something blocking the line going back to the home and would not allow the jetter to enter. Tech pulled back bundles of wipes two times. The second time we also retrieved roots and a piece of crushed stone was stuck in the cable. Tech showed Sam his findings. We were eventually able to jet the line. While retrieving the jetter, we got stuck multiple times. We were unable to get the camera in the vent so we performed a video inspection from the gutter drain. Tech had Sam flush a toilet multiple times and we could hear and see the flush come down. The terra-cotta pipe had multiple bellies holding water and had root penetration. We lost visibility and couldn’t push any further. Tech located the camera and explained to Sam that the line is a common line with 333 and where we located it was on that side of the property. He called the owner of 335 but tech didn’t get permission to enter the basement. Tech will upload photos and videos. Due to the condition of the pipe, there is no warranty for the work performed today. Any future backups will be a standard charge. Tech explained to Sam that being that the sewer line runs on 3 different properties, he would have to get permission from both other properties and then give us a call back so we can give an appropriate estimate for replacement. He stated 335 and 333 are rentals. At this time, the line is temporarily flowing. Thanks for trusting Lancaster plumbing and heating.

Upon arrival, tech met with Catherine. She showed me the standpipe where the backup occurred after she took a shower this morning. We took a look outside and found a puddle of water next to a cleanout in the backyard. Tech slowly removed the cleanout cap and a gush of water and sewage came out. She stated she just had her septic tank flushed about a month ago. Tech took a look at the tanks just to confirm they weren’t full. Tech presented a solution and with her approval, tech used drain equipment and was able to restore flow. We ran the shower for approximately 10 minutes to ensure there was no backup. We then performed a video inspection of the main line. From the cleanout back to the home was pvc pipe that transitions to terra-cotta, cast iron and then abs. We came across root penetration at the pvc to terra-cotta connection. The cast iron was starting to deteriorate from the inside out and the abs was level and holding water in one section. From the cleanout out to the baffle, we came across pvc pipe that had slight buildup and some water being held in one section of the pipe. The bottom of the cleanout was broken as well. Tech explained all his findings to Catherine as we performed the inspection. She stated she can not afford to replace or repair it due to her finances. Tech explained that he understands but this is something that should be done sooner then later to avoid any future backups. She stated she did not want any options but then agrees for tech to email them to her. Tech was unable to present options to her, she had somewhere to be. estimates.name: Bathroom ventilation and drainage
estimates.summary:
When flushing the toilet in the main floor hallway bathroom, a gurgling sound can be heard coming from the bathtub drain. This may indicate an issue with the existing drain and venting configuration. Upon inspection, the existing bathtub drain consists of 1-1/2” copper piping connected to an S-trap configuration, which is not properly vented and can interfere with the drainage system’s ability to maintain proper airflow. When the toilet is flushed, the sudden discharge of water through the drainage system can create pressure fluctuations that may cause air to be pulled through the bathtub trap, resulting in the gurgling sound. Improper venting can also affect the bathtub trap seal, potentially allowing sewer gases to enter the home if the water seal is compromised. The home’s main plumbing vent is supplied from the top of the main waste stack.

Technician recommends replacing the existing 1-1/2” copper bathtub drain piping with 2” PVC piping and replacing the corroded brass bathtub waste and overflow assembly. This will provide updated drain piping and a new waste and overflow assembly while allowing the existing drain configuration to be evaluated and corrected as needed. Technician will assess the existing S-trap arrangement and determine the appropriate corrections to improve drainage and provide proper venting in accordance with applicable plumbing code requirements.

Technician also recommends inspecting the plumbing vent through the roof to check for possible obstructions, such as debris or other blockages, that could restrict airflow through the vent system. A restricted vent can contribute to gurgling sounds, slow drainage, and improper pressure balance within the plumbing system. Clearing any obstructions found may help restore proper airflow. These recommended repairs and inspections are intended to improve drainage performance, reduce the gurgling sound when flushing the toilet, and help maintain the proper water seal in the bathtub drain trap. Additional venting modifications may be necessary depending on the existing plumbing configuration and the findings during the repair.

invoices.summary: We were called out to evaluate why the breaker that controls the smoke detectors would constantly trip. Upon arrival, we met with Ryan who informed us that yesterday they noticed all of the power off in their son’s bedroom and no power for the smoke detectors. Ryan then led us to the breaker panel and identify the breaker that was giving them issues. From here, we did a thorough evaluation of the entire system and circuit to identify the main issue. We were able to conclude that the sump pump itself failed internally, which was caused the breaker to respond accordingly. We also determined that the son’s bedroom no power issue was a reactionary issue from the other portion of the tandem breaker tripping constantly. The son’s bedroom circuit on its own, is in good shape and functioning correctly at this time. Once we remove the sump pump from the circuit, the entire circuitry was working as it should. Ryan wanted an option to install a dedicated circuit for the sump pump which can be completed. We would use the large coil of unused wire in the basement to the sump pump receptacle and hooking it up to a new breaker to completely separate the sump pump circuit from the smoke detector circuit. We also recommend that the culprit breaker be replaced as preventative maintenance and safety precaution. We also highly recommend that all of the smoke detectors in the home be replaced as well due to them being past their 10 year lifespan. One of the smoke detectors on the second floor hallway area, had a broken plug adapter, which was replaced today along with the culprit breaker. The new smoke detector will come with a 10 year parts warranty and the breaker will come with a one year part and labor warranty. We also left options to run the sump pump wire and install a breaker as well as replacing all the remaining smoke detectors. All unapproved options will be emailed to Ryan for his record and to review. We thank you for trusting us to solve your electrical concerns and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

estimates.name: Water softener  - with spp
estimates.summary:
Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 19 grains per gallon (GPG) and the chlorine level to be 1.0 ppm. A hardness level of 19 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, showerheads, and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a City Soft water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. Benefits of the system include improved soap and detergent performance, reduced spotting and scaling, softer-feeling water, and increased protection and efficiency of plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances.

The proposed installation location for the City Soft system is near the existing water heater to allow for efficient integration into the home’s main water distribution system. The softener’s backwash drain lines will be routed and connected to the existing main drain located behind the water heater at the proposed installation area. An outlet is provided. Once installed, the system will provide conditioned water to the entire home and help minimize the long-term effects of hard water and chlorine exposure on the plumbing system.

During my inspection, I found a tripped breaker controlling the affected lighting circuit. After resetting the breaker, the lights returned to normal operation.

I removed the main panel cover to inspect the newly installed breakers, verify their installation, and evaluate the overall condition of the electrical panel. The main panel was found to be in great condition, and the newly installed breakers were the correct type and appeared to be properly installed.

However, I did notice that the main electrical panel does not have a whole-home surge protection device installed. Whole-home surge protection helps protect larger appliances and sensitive electronics from damaging voltage spikes and electrical surges. I recommended installing a surge protection device, which includes a lifetime warranty and $100,000 in connected equipment coverage, subject to the manufacturer’s terms and conditions. The homeowners had a few additional questions and concerns. Since I was already on-site, I offered to perform a general electrical system evaluation.

During this evaluation, I found that most of the receptacles throughout the home utilize backstab connections. These connections can loosen over time, potentially resulting in intermittent power, loss of electrical continuity, overheating, or damage to the receptacles. Although these issues are not guaranteed to occur, I recommended replacing the affected receptacles and terminating the wiring using the appropriate screw-terminal connections to help reduce the risk of future electrical issues. This recommended repair includes a 10-year parts and labor warranty.

The homeowner also expressed concerns regarding the lighting in the office area. I will provide an estimate for installing four 6-inch recessed lights to improve the room’s overall illumination. invoices.summary:
LPH arrived at the residence to perform a comprehensive electrical system check evaluation throughout the home. During the evaluation, LPH inspected the main electrical panel and accessible electrical components, checked breakers and visible connections for signs of deterioration, overheating, corrosion, and improper installation, and evaluated the condition of accessible receptacles, switches, lighting devices, and other electrical components throughout the home. LPH also checked accessible GFCI protection, exterior receptacles and weatherproof covers, and visible wiring conditions for potential safety concerns.

Main Electrical Panel: The existing 42-year-old Crouse-Hinds electrical panel was evaluated and found to have several concerning conditions. Rust was observed on multiple breakers, along with heat discoloration above the main breaker. The original breakers were also noticeably loose, and when gently moved, audible electrical arcing could be heard. These conditions raise concerns regarding deteriorated breaker connections, potential overheating, and the reliability of the existing electrical equipment. Due to the age of the panel and the observed deterioration, LPH discussed replacing the existing panel with a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel and installing new compatible breakers to improve the safety and reliability of the home’s electrical distribution system.

Basement Circuit: LPH discussed the existing 20-amp basement circuit, where the wiring method involves conductors inserted into the back of the receptacle devices. These connections are beginning to loosen, raising concerns about maintaining reliable electrical contact. Loose electrical connections can create resistance, heat buildup, and potential arcing. LPH reviewed the benefits of correcting these connections using an appropriate wiring and termination method.

GFCI Protection Throughout the Home: LPH evaluated GFCI protection in applicable areas throughout the residence and discussed locations where protection is incomplete, including portions of the kitchen. Proper GFCI protection helps reduce the risk of electrical shock in areas where receptacles may be exposed to moisture or where electrical equipment is used near water. Available options for improving protection in the applicable areas were discussed with the homeowner.

Upstairs Electrical Devices: Several electrical devices upstairs were identified as deteriorated and in need of replacement. The homeowner acknowledged these conditions and stated that addressing the interior device replacements would be part of a future project that they could handle independently.

Attic Above the Garage: LPH identified a live tap box in the attic above the garage. This electrical connection point was discussed with the homeowner as an item requiring attention to ensure the wiring and enclosure are properly installed, protected, and maintained in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements.

Exterior Receptacles: LPH evaluated the accessible exterior receptacles and discussed the need for appropriate GFCI protection and suitable weatherproof covers for the remaining exterior devices. Proper outdoor-rated receptacles and covers help protect electrical connections from moisture and environmental exposure while reducing the potential for corrosion, electrical failure, and shock hazards.

All findings and recommendations were reviewed with the homeowner, including the primary concern involving the deteriorated Crouse-Hinds electrical panel and the additional items identified throughout the home. The homeowner stated that the interior device replacements were something they could address as part of a future project and requested estimates for the electrical panel replacement and the recommended exterior receptacle improvements.

The requested estimates, along with today’s electrical system check evaluation, will be emailed to the homeowner for review and consideration.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. We appreciate the opportunity to evaluate your electrical system and look forward to servicing you again in the future.

estimates.name: 200 amp panel replacement
estimates.summary:
Electrical Panel Replacement – Crouse-Hinds Panel

Reason for Replacement

LPH recommends replacing the existing 42-year-old Crouse-Hinds electrical panel due to its age and visible signs of deterioration. The panel has exceeded its typical service life, and several concerning conditions were identified during the electrical evaluation.

Signs of rust were observed on several breakers, along with heat discoloration above the main breaker. These conditions can indicate deterioration and potential overheating within the electrical panel. Additionally, the original breakers were noticeably loose in their connections. When the breakers were gently moved, a light amount of electrical arcing could be heard, raising concerns about the integrity of the breaker-to-bus connections and the potential for unreliable electrical contact.

As electrical panels and their components age, connections can loosen, contact surfaces can deteriorate, and corrosion can develop. These conditions can increase electrical resistance, generate excessive heat, and contribute to electrical arcing. If left unaddressed, deteriorated connections can damage the panel and breakers while increasing the potential for electrical failure or fire.

Due to the age of the panel, rust on the breakers, heat discoloration, and audible arcing associated with movement of the original breakers, LPH recommends replacing the existing electrical panel rather than continuing to rely on deteriorated equipment.

Installing a new electrical panel will provide modern electrical distribution equipment, new breakers, and properly established connections to improve the safety and reliability of the home’s electrical system.

Scope of Work Includes:

* Remove the existing 42-year-old Crouse-Hinds electrical panel.
* Install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel.
* Transfer and properly terminate the existing branch circuits.
* Install new breakers appropriate for the existing circuits and new panel.
* Inspect existing branch-circuit wiring for signs of damage or deterioration at accessible connection points.
* Properly establish neutral and grounding connections in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements.
* Inspect and verify electrical terminations and connections.
* Properly label the new electrical panel and individual circuits.
* Test the completed installation and verify proper operation of the electrical system.

Benefits of Replacing the Existing Panel

Improved Electrical Safety: Replacing the aging panel addresses concerns associated with deteriorated equipment, rust, heat discoloration, and loose breaker connections. New equipment and properly established connections help reduce the risks associated with overheating and electrical arcing.

Reliable Breaker Connections: The original breakers have become noticeably loose, and movement produced audible arcing. A new panel with compatible breakers will provide new breaker mounting and contact components, helping establish reliable electrical connections.

Reduced Risk of Overheating: Rust and heat discoloration are warning signs that warrant attention. Replacing the panel allows the affected equipment to be removed and the connected wiring to be inspected for damage before being terminated in the new panel.

Modern Electrical Distribution: A new 42-space Eaton CH panel provides a modern electrical distribution system designed to accommodate compatible breakers and support the home’s electrical needs.

Future Electrical Flexibility: The new panel provides additional circuit spaces for potential future electrical additions, subject to the available service capacity and the home’s calculated electrical load.

Peace-of-Mind Warranty

Your new Eaton CH electrical panel and breakers are protected by a 10-year parts and labor warranty while maintaining an active LPH Service Partner Plan (SPP) membership, providing continued coverage and added peace of mind.

Long-Term Value

Replacing the existing Crouse-Hinds panel is a proactive investment in the safety and reliability of the home’s electrical system. With the panel approximately 42 years old and showing signs of rust, heat discoloration, loose breaker connections, and audible arcing, continuing to rely on the existing equipment presents avoidable concerns.

A new electrical panel will replace the deteriorated components, provide properly established breaker connections, and help restore dependable electrical distribution throughout the home.

All work will be completed in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements and the requirements of the local authority having jurisdiction.

invoices.summary:
Electrical System Check Evaluation

LPH performed a comprehensive electrical system check throughout the home, evaluating the electrical panel, breakers, wiring connections, receptacles, switches, GFCI protection, smoke detection, and exterior electrical service equipment.

The home is in great working order and was found to be fully up to code based on the items evaluated during today’s inspection. GFCI protection is present in all required locations, and all receptacles and switches are in great physical condition, with no visible signs of damage or deterioration.

During the evaluation, we discussed with the homeowners that the home was wired using backstab connections at the receptacles and switches. Although these devices are currently in great shape with no visible signs of degradation or connection issues, backstab connections are known to be more susceptible to loosening and premature failure over time compared to properly secured screw-terminal connections. No immediate concerns were identified, but this is something the homeowners should be aware of for future maintenance considerations.

The electrical panel, breakers, and internal connections were inspected and found to be in great condition. Breakers are properly sized for their respective circuits, and no loose connections or visible signs of overheating or deterioration were identified. Smoke detection is up to date, and the home has the required GFCI protection in place.

The only items identified during today’s evaluation were the lack of exterior sealing around the top and sides of the meter base and the absence of ceiling lighting in the home’s three bedrooms.

LPH reviewed options with the homeowners to seal the exterior meter base to help prevent moisture intrusion and to install ceiling fans with lights in the three bedrooms. The homeowners approved the meter base sealing, which was completed today, and scheduled the ceiling fan wiring and installations for January 11th. A down payment has been collected toward the scheduled work, and the necessary parts will be ordered in preparation for the installation.

Overall, the home’s electrical system is in excellent condition, with no immediate electrical concerns identified during today’s evaluation.

Today’s invoice and electrical system check evaluation will be emailed to the homeowners for their records. Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure speaking with you, and we look forward to servicing you again in the future.

invoices.summary: We were called out to evaluate why the dryer was not working at all. Upon arrival, we spoke with the homeowner to get a complete understanding of this issue. We started our thorough evaluation at the dryer receptacle and breaker panel. We started by testing by voltage at both locations, and identified that one of the phases for the breaker was only sending 22V and the other was sending the proper 122V. We immediately identified that this  breaker would need to be replaced. We also identified some signs of corrosion inside the Dryer receptacle, so we recommend the dryer receptacle to be replaced as well. The immediate electrical correction package was approved and completed today. The new breaker installed was tested and working properly along with the driver receptacle. We will offer a one year worry free warranty for the new breaker installed today. We thank you for allowing us in your home to correct your electrical concern, and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

invoices.summary:
Technician arrived to address odor suspected to be coming from HVAC system. Upon arrival I found the system was calling for cooling and the AC condenser was running, but the blower was not running. There was ice on the lines and some after present on the floor and on the gas line. I also noticed an odor of burnt electronics inside the furnace. Performed testing on the furnace by jumping out the control wiring on the ECM motor. Confirmed blower motor has failed. There are no burn marks on either board and both are sending voltage. Due to the nature of the failure I couldn’t test the rest of the system. I did scope the heat exchanger, where significant rusting is present. There is a possibility that replacing the blower may uncover other issues. I will be in touch tomorrow with exact pricing and availability for the repair. We will also reach out to schedule an install consult for replacing the furnace. 

During my visit I noticed water slowly dripping from the ceiling above the furnace. We found that the refrigerator water line was severely damaged and it began spraying water when the refrigerator was moved. Was able to shut off the service valve and restore water to the home. 

Furnace is left open but powered off to allow it to dry out.

invoices.summary:
This afternoon I arrived at the Lippart family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies. The one recommendation I had was regarding the main breaker panel. The panel appears to be in good physical condition with no signs of rusting, corrosion, or burning. However, the panel has eclipsed what we would deem to be the average life expectancy for breaker panels. The panel is over 40 years old now. As panels age, the safety features within their breakers can begin to fail to function in the event of an electrical fault. Separate from this, should any breakers fail, or need to be replaced, it can be difficult to find replacements as they do not manufacture these parts anymore. 
LPH also noticed that the appliances in the home are missing active surge protection to defend against any spike of voltage that can enter/be produced inside of the home and potentially damage motherboards or other electrical components inside appliances. A whole home surge protection device that gets mounted and connected at the panel will help defend against these harmful spikes of voltage. The device installed will come with lifetime parts warranty and up to $100,000 of repair or replacement(whichever is less) coverage in the event that a grounded appliance/equipment(the appliance/equipment that come with a home such as A/C, Furnace, other home intergraded heating system(boilers and water heaters), water purification system, range, microwave, refrigerator, and etc.) becomes damaged due to a surge with this device installed. *Whole home surge protection device is NOT a power conditioner, meaning that the home surge device will not eliminate the minor flickering for bulbs entirely but will alleviate most of the major/noticeable flickering/strobbing*. I provided estimates to replace the full electrical service, separately the panel alone, and lastly to install a whole home surge protection device. IF you have any questions or would like to move forward with any of these estimates please do not hesitate to reach out! Thank you.

invoices.summary:
Homeowner showed the technician the condensation pump located in the basement at the Bosch furnace installed by LPH. Homeowner explained that the condensation pump had been experiencing intermittent issues with turning on and/or keeping up with the amount of condensation being produced. During these occurrences, the thermostat would display an error indicating that the system was waiting for the unit. LPH previously replaced the thermostat twice without resolving the issue. LPH also replaced the condensation pump twice; however, the problem continued to occur, most recently the previous week while the air conditioning system was running.

Technician connected a hose to the boiler drain at the well pressure tank to introduce water into the condensation pump and simulate the drainage from two units running simultaneously. During testing, technician observed that the condensation pump was discharging water too slowly to keep up with the incoming water flow. Technician inspected the existing 3/8-inch PEX discharge tubing and determined that it was restricting the discharge flow. Technician replaced the existing 3/8-inch PEX tubing with 3/8-inch vinyl tubing. After replacing the tubing, technician tested the condensation pump again and observed improved water flow and a faster discharge rate. This correction improved the pump’s ability to remove water during testing.

Due to the ongoing nature of this issue and the previous attempts to resolve it, technician waived the dispatch fee and completed the discharge tubing replacement at no additional charge.

estimates.name: Life Safety Device Circuit
estimates.summary:
LPH will install a new, dedicated electrical circuit from the electrical panel to the location where the oxygen pump is stationed. The oxygen pump is currently causing nuisance tripping of the brand-new arc-fault circuit breaker, which was previously replaced in September after similar issues began following the delivery of a new machine to the home.

The concern is that the oxygen pump may be contributing to the issue in two ways: the possibility of overloading the existing shared circuit with other electrical devices, or electrical interference generated by the pump’s internal condenser and electronic components that may be triggering the arc-fault breaker’s sensitive detection circuitry after approximately one hour of operation.

Installing a dedicated circuit will separate the oxygen pump from other electrical loads and help eliminate concerns associated with sharing the existing circuit. Using a standard circuit breaker, where permitted by applicable electrical code and the equipment manufacturer’s requirements, will also help address potential nuisance tripping associated with the pump’s electronic operation.

This solution is intended to provide a more reliable power source for the oxygen pump, reduce the likelihood of unexpected interruptions, and provide the homeowner with greater peace of mind when relying on this equipment.

invoices.summary:
Arrived and performed the following repair: Replace ECM blower motor and module. Test system operation for any further damage. Due to coil freezing and water leak above furnace there exists the possibility of additional repairs being needed after the blower is replaced.

1 year full warranty on new motor 

After repairing the system, I tested the system in heating mode. Confirmed good gas pressure before combustion, then started combustion analysis after the furnace had ran for a few minutes. Carbon monoxide readings in the exhaust were extremely high (over 1000ppm air free). I ran to the venting to inspect it and found a hose dripped over it, as well as the venting itself installed incorrectly. Tested again with the burner door open to rule out cross contamination of the exhaust and CO was still above safety limit. Ruled out any vent blockage. At this time I have shut off the gas to the furnace as it is unsafe to operate due to a failed heat exchanger. At this time the heat exchanger is back ordered. We are working to see what warranty credit options are available and will be out tomorrow to give pricing on replacing the furnace.

invoices.summary:
Out to home today for two major concerns. The priority for today has to do with the outdoor faucets. All faucets are extremely aged and do not work very well. The faucet on the side of the home is installed to where it sticks out and is a tripping hazard. The front and back faucets leak when in use and allow water to leak inside the home. The faucet on the front of the home is not easily accessible and will need the ceiling opened to gain access. Created a faucet replacement package where the front and back faucets are replaced with frost-proof fixtures with new valves installed inside. The side faucet is to be capped and removed. 

The next concern has to do with slow drainage and leaks inside the home. The bathroom upstairs in general does not drain very well and takes time to drain. Observed venting issues as the water goes down slowly followed by bubbling of air. Bathroom group is vented through a pipe going through the roof and is likely restricted preventing proper air flow into the waste system. Other fixtures not tied to the bathroom group drain properly and have no issues. Aside from ventilation issues, homeowner states they toilet does not flush like it used to. Observed water staining around the base of the toilet, which could be causing the water accumulation in the ceiling down below. Suggested replacement of the fixture to provide a modern and proper flush and replace the seal at the floor. Provided option to perform leak search in ceiling. Lastly, the tub drain stopper has broken. Made suggestion to replace tub drain assembly and replace with a more conventional toe-tap style drain. 

Went over all pricing today with homeowner. Pricing provided today is valid for 60 days. If there are any question or if you would like to schedule one of these repairs, please reach out to our office. Thank you for trusting LPH.

estimates.name: Installation of Toilet Upstairs
estimates.summary:
During evaluation, homeowner noticed the toilet has been flushing slower and slower lately. With age of toilet, internals channels of the toilet may be starting to clog up from hardwater deposits and bacteria causing a lower quality flush. Suggested replacement of the fixture for a modern better flushing unit. 

This solution includes replacement of the toilet fixture. LPH to install new comfort height elongated toilet with new slow-close seat from Gerber. With replacement of fixture, new mounting hardware and shut off valve will be installed.

*In rare cases, there may be damage to the flange and mounting surface. Additional repairs may be necessary and will be provided if necessary.

estimates.name: Waste & Overflow replacement
estimates.summary:
Homeowner stated that their stopper for their tub has broken and would like a repair option. 

This solution includes full replacement of the waste & overflow which would update the stopper to a more conventional toe-tap style. Includes brushed nickel finish.

estimates.name: Priority Outdoor Faucet Package
estimates.summary:
Replacement of outdoor faucets on the front and back of the home. Package includes installation of new internal service valve and up to date frost-proof faucets mounted to the home. For the front faucet, LPH will need to open access in the ceiling of the basement to gain access to piping to perform repairs. 

*LPH will open access, however we do not offer any repair services for walls, ceilings, or trim. 

For the side faucet at the porch, old faucet will be removed and capped off closer to home to reduce trip chance in the walk way. Inside home, old supply piping will be removed and capped.

estimates.name: Leak Search & Drain Evaluation
estimates.summary:
Homeowners have noticed water leaking from the ceiling from time to time above their front door. They are unsure if it is coming from the plumbing or another location. 

This solution includes opening up the ceiling above the front door to evaluate condition of drain piping in ceiling and perform leak search. If walls need to be opened up in addition, pricing will be updated to Tier 3.

estimates.name: Vent Drain Cleaning
estimates.summary: During evaluation, identified slow drains all throughout upstairs bathroom. Identified cause to be poor venting in the bathroom. Everything goes down properly but is not vented properly causing water to escape much slower than normal. Bathroom is vented from an undersized pipe going through the roof. This solution includes performing draining cleaning from roof access to open up vent and restore proper drainage to bathroom group. If accessible, drain cleaning will be performed from an attic access

Upon arrival, tech met with Erik. He stated he noticed sewage around the floor drain in the basement on Tuesday. Tech observed the area and found toilet paper and other buildup. Tech had Erik flush a toilet and found the water to fluctuate in the floor drain and rise. We checked the outside trap and found the water level to be high in the riser pipe. estimates.name: Kitchen/laundry drain repipe
estimates.summary:
Technician snaked the laundry and kitchen drain due to slow drainage and the presence of an existing underground cast-iron drain line. To help improve drainage and reduce the potential for future blockages associated with the existing underground piping, Technician recommends rerouting the laundry and kitchen drain above ground. The new drain piping would connect to the existing 4-inch main waste stack, eliminating the need for the drain line to run underground. Technician also recommends installing an air admittance valve (AAV) beneath the kitchen sink to provide proper venting for the drainage system. This will help maintain proper air flow within the drain piping and improve drainage performance for both the kitchen sink and laundry tub.

Technician found that the basement laundry tub/kitchen drain was backing up and draining slowly. Technician removed the existing P-trap from the laundry tub drain and used a cable machine to clear the drain line, which runs underground and connects to the existing cast-iron piping. While cabling the drain, technician encountered an obstruction approximately 10–15 feet into the underground drain line but was able to break through and clear the blockage. Technician continued running the cable through the drain line to the full length of the cable machine, approximately 70 feet, to help ensure the line was clear.

After completing the drain cleaning, technician reinstalled the P-trap and filled the laundry tub with water twice to test the drainage. Both tests confirmed that the water drained properly without backing up, indicating that the drain was flowing freely at the time of service.

invoices.summary: This morning I arrived at the Iwanowski family home to conduct their first annual electrical system and safety check. At the time of my arrival the iwanowskis informed me that they had no immediate electrical concerns. I informed them of the agenda for the day and proceeded to my analysis of their home. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies. I did however take note of the systems age. Being installed in 1976, that would have this panel aged at 50 years old. We encourage replacement of panels traditionally around 30-35 years, evidently this panel has eclipsed that. I informed Mr. Iwanowski of the common failures of panels that reach the 50 mark, and the reasons for providing my estimate. Physically, the panel is in great condition. Very clean with no signs of rust, corrosion, or overheating, but the primary concern is the age of the main breaker. I provided an estimate for the panel replacement during today’s visit almost solely due to the panels age. I provided a second option for gas and water bonding in the home, the reason for this estimate is to prevent potential electrical shock hazards when using water or gas appliances in the home. These estimates have been mailed to the Iwanowskis. Ultimately the home appears to be in good condition electrically. If you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to reach out! Thank you for sharing your home with me this morning and I look forward to our next visit!
