estimates.summary:
LPH will rewire the unfinished basement and install six new dedicated circuits from the existing basement subpanel. This upgrade will provide properly distributed electrical service for the basement’s current and planned uses, reduce the electrical load on the existing circuits, and provide the appropriate protection for the new receptacles and connected equipment.

Basement Rewiring – Six New Circuits

1. Dedicated 15-Amp Radon Fan Circuit

* Install one new 15-amp circuit dedicated to the radon fan.
* Install a single receptacle at the designated location, with conduit piped down the wall to provide a protected wiring method.

This dedicated circuit will provide a separate power source for the radon fan rather than relying on a shared circuit serving other basement equipment and receptacles.

2. Dedicated 20-Amp Exercise Area Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit to supply the basement exercise area.
* Install three receptacles to accommodate the designated exercise equipment.
* Install two receptacles along the wall bordering the mechanical room.
* Reuse the existing conduit at the designated location, remove the existing receptacle wiring, and install new wiring and a new receptacle.

Providing a dedicated circuit for the exercise area will help accommodate the electrical demand of the equipment without adding additional loads to the general basement receptacle circuit.

3. Dedicated 20-Amp Basement Kitchenette Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit to supply the planned basement kitchenette.
* Install two receptacle locations at the designated areas.
* Pick up the upstairs kitchen island receptacle as part of this circuit using wiring accessible from the basement.

Including the upstairs kitchen island receptacle on this new circuit will help remove its load from the existing circuit serving the basement lighting, screened-in porch, and existing exterior receptacles. This will help distribute the electrical demand more appropriately and reduce the likelihood of nuisance tripping on the existing circuit.

This circuit will provide a separate power source for the kitchenette and kitchen island receptacles, helping distribute the electrical load as the basement living space is developed.

4. Dedicated 20-Amp Fireplace Heater Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit dedicated to the basement fireplace heater.
* Install one receptacle at the designated location, with conduit piped down the wall.

A dedicated circuit will help accommodate the heater’s electrical demand without unnecessarily loading the general-purpose basement receptacle circuit.

5. Dedicated 20-Amp Exterior Hot Tub Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit from the basement subpanel, routed across the basement and drilled through the exterior wall to the back porch.
* Install one weather-resistant GFCI receptacle with an appropriate in-use bubble cover to supply the 120-volt inflatable hot tub.

Because this receptacle will serve equipment used around water, proper ground-fault protection is particularly important. GFCI protection is designed to quickly interrupt power when an electrical fault creates a potentially dangerous shock hazard.

The final circuit and receptacle arrangement will need to meet the hot tub manufacturer’s electrical requirements and applicable code requirements for the installation location.

6. Dedicated 20-Amp General Basement Receptacle Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit to supply the remaining designated basement receptacles.
* Reuse the existing conduit at one location and install a new receptacle.
* Cut in one receptacle along the stairway wall.
* Install three additional receptacles at the designated locations, using conduit down the block walls as needed.

This additional circuit will provide convenient receptacle access throughout the basement while distributing the electrical demand across multiple circuits instead of continuing to rely on the existing overloaded arrangement.

Basement Circuit Protection

The six new circuits will be installed from the existing basement subpanel using the appropriate wiring methods and circuit protection for their intended applications. The estimate includes:

* Four 20-amp dual-function AFCI/GFCI circuit breakers.
* One 20-amp AFCI circuit breaker.
* One 15-amp AFCI circuit breaker.

AFCI protection is designed to detect certain dangerous electrical arcing conditions that can lead to fires. GFCI protection helps reduce the risk of electrical shock by detecting ground faults and interrupting power. Dual-function breakers combine both protective features in one device.

The specified breakers will provide the intended protection for the new circuits while helping bring the installation into compliance with applicable electrical code requirements.

Existing Basement Wiring – Junction Box Transition

Currently, one existing circuit supplies the basement lighting and receptacles, exterior receptacles, screened-in porch receptacles, and kitchen island receptacle. This places a substantial number of electrical loads on a single circuit and can contribute to nuisance tripping when multiple devices are operating.

As part of this project, LPH will disconnect and transition the existing basement wiring as necessary, installing accessible junction boxes along the basement ceiling to maintain continuity for the existing circuits. This will allow the existing wiring to remain operational while the new circuits take over the designated basement receptacle loads and the upstairs kitchen island receptacle is transferred to the new kitchenette circuit.

The goal is to distribute the electrical demand more appropriately, reduce the burden on the existing circuit, and provide a more functional electrical layout for the basement and the home’s connected areas.

Whole-Home Surge Protection Recommendation

With the installation of multiple new circuits and sensitive AFCI/GFCI protective devices, LPH recommends adding a whole-home surge protector at the main electrical panel.

Modern electrical equipment, appliances, and electronic circuit boards can be damaged by voltage surges originating from utility disturbances, lightning-related events, or electrical equipment cycling on and off within the home. These events can also contribute to premature wear or damage to sensitive electronic components.

A whole-home surge protector provides an additional layer of defense by helping divert damaging transient voltage away from the home’s electrical system and connected equipment. It is particularly beneficial for homes with modern appliances, HVAC equipment, electronics, and other sensitive devices.

Although surge protection cannot prevent every type of electrical disturbance or guarantee that equipment will never be damaged, it is a worthwhile protective upgrade for the home.

Additional 20-Amp Exterior Circuit From the Main Panel

LPH will install one additional 20-amp circuit from the main electrical panel to supply two receptacles serving the main garage area: one receptacle inside the garage below the electrical panel and one exterior receptacle on the opposite side of the wall.

This installation will include:

* Routing the new circuit from the main panel and dropping down the wall to the designated locations.
* Installing a GFCI-protected receptacle at the designated exterior location.
* Installing one receptacle inside the garage below the electrical panel.
* Providing convenient power sources for both interior garage and exterior use.
* Providing a more suitable power source for the garage microwave, reducing reliance on the existing garage door opener receptacle and extension cord.

Currently, the microwave is being powered through the garage door opener receptacle using an extension cord. This is not an ideal arrangement for an appliance that draws substantial current, particularly when the circuit may already be supplying other equipment. A properly installed receptacle on a new circuit will provide a more appropriate power source and help reduce nuisance tripping caused by shared electrical loads.

Exterior Receptacle Repairs and Weather Protection

LPH will also address the damaged exterior receptacles by replacing the existing devices with new weather-resistant receptacles and providing the required GFCI protection.

This portion of the work includes:

* Two weather-resistant GFCI receptacles.
* Two weather-resistant duplex receptacles.
* Reuse of the existing boxes and appropriate bubble covers where suitable.

Weather-resistant receptacles are designed to better withstand outdoor environmental exposure. Combined with appropriate GFCI protection and suitable covers, these replacements will help reduce the risk of moisture-related deterioration, electrical faults, and shock hazards.

The existing boxes are already equipped with appropriate bubble covers, so the existing covers will be retained where they are in suitable condition and compatible with the new receptacles.

Additional Grounding and Bonding Improvements

LPH recommends completing the home’s grounding and bonding system by installing a grounding clamp on the existing metal water line and adding approximately 5 feet of grounding conductor to bond the home’s gas piping system as required by applicable electrical code.

* Water Line Grounding: Install an approved grounding clamp on the existing metal water line and connect it to the home’s grounding electrode system as appropriate. This will address the incomplete grounding arrangement and help establish the required electrical connection to the metal water piping where applicable.
* Gas Line Bonding: Install approximately 5 feet of additional grounding conductor to properly bond the home’s gas piping system to the electrical grounding system, as required by applicable code provisions.

Proper grounding and bonding help provide a safe, intentional path for fault current, allowing protective devices to operate as intended during an electrical fault. These connections also help reduce dangerous voltage differences between metal piping systems and other grounded electrical components.

Completing these improvements will help bring the home’s grounding and bonding system into compliance with applicable electrical code requirements and provide an additional layer of protection for the home’s occupants and electrical equipment.

Installation, Testing, and Completion

All new circuits will be routed from the designated electrical panels using appropriate wiring methods, conduit, junction boxes, and circuit protection for their intended applications. LPH will complete the installation in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements, verify the new connections, and test the installed devices and circuits for proper operation.

The overall goal of this project is to provide a safer, more organized, and more functional electrical system for the unfinished basement and surrounding areas. By adding dedicated circuits for the radon fan, exercise equipment, kitchenette, fireplace heater, and hot tub, transferring the upstairs kitchen island receptacle to the new kitchenette circuit, expanding general receptacle capacity, and addressing the exterior electrical concerns, LPH will help accommodate the home’s electrical needs while reducing dependence on the existing heavily loaded circuit.

LPH will replace the existing expired smoke detectors throughout the home with new smoke detectors equipped with 10-year sealed lithium battery power. This upgrade will provide the homeowner with reliable smoke detection while eliminating the need for routine battery replacements over the detectors’ service life. All new detectors will be properly installed and tested to verify operation, helping maintain dependable early-warning protection for the home and its occupants.

LPH recommends replacing the existing 34-year-old Crouse-Hinds electrical panel with a brand-new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel while retaining the home’s existing 200-amp service capacity.

Although the existing Crouse-Hinds panel is rated for 200 amps, its age and original design make replacement a worthwhile investment in the home’s electrical safety, reliability, and ability to accommodate modern electrical demands. Electrical panels are responsible for distributing power throughout the home and providing overcurrent protection to individual circuits. As panels age, breakers and internal connection points can experience wear, deterioration, and reduced reliability. Breaker connections on the bus bar can also loosen over time, potentially causing overheating, arcing, or unreliable circuit operation.

Why Upgrade the Existing Panel?

1. Aging Electrical Equipment

At approximately 34 years old, the existing Crouse-Hinds panel has provided decades of service. However, its age warrants consideration of replacement before deterioration or component failures create a more urgent situation. Replacing the panel allows LPH to install new equipment rather than continuing to depend on aging internal components and connections.

2. Better Support for Today’s Electrical Demands

Modern homes typically place greater demands on their electrical systems than they did decades ago. Today’s households rely on larger appliances, home office equipment, entertainment systems, exercise equipment, electronic devices, and other electrical loads that may not have been anticipated when the original panel was installed.

The existing panel’s 200-amp rating does not automatically mean the home needs a larger service. However, replacing the older panel provides an opportunity to improve circuit organization, evaluate the home’s electrical distribution, and accommodate additional circuit protection and future electrical projects where capacity permits.

3. Upgrade to a New 42-Space Eaton CH Panel

LPH will replace the existing Crouse-Hinds panel with a new 42-space Eaton CH panel. This provides a modern panel assembly with additional circuit spaces to help organize the home’s electrical system and accommodate future circuit additions, subject to the available service and load capacity.

The new panel will also provide a suitable platform for compatible circuit breakers and modern protective devices as needed for the home’s electrical requirements.

4. Improved Long-Term Reliability and Serviceability

Replacing the existing panel allows LPH to evaluate the incoming service conductors, grounding and bonding connections, neutral and ground terminations, and branch-circuit connections as part of the installation. This includes inspecting the breaker connections at the bus bar for looseness, signs of overheating, or other conditions that may affect safe operation. This helps identify concerns that may otherwise remain hidden within aging equipment.

A new panel can also make future electrical maintenance and troubleshooting more straightforward by providing current, compatible equipment and a more organized circuit layout.

5. Opportunity to Incorporate Whole-Home Surge Protection

As part of the panel replacement, LPH recommends installing whole-home surge protection to help protect sensitive electronics and appliances from damaging voltage transients originating from utility disturbances, lightning-related events, and electrical equipment cycling within the home.

Modern appliances and electronic equipment contain circuit boards and sensitive components that can be vulnerable to voltage surges. Whole-home surge protection provides an additional layer of defense for the home’s electrical system and connected equipment.

Scope of Work

LPH will:

* Remove the existing 34-year-old Crouse-Hinds electrical panel.
* Install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel while maintaining the existing 200-amp service rating, provided the existing service components and installation support that configuration.
* Transfer the existing branch circuits to the new panel using compatible circuit breakers and appropriate wiring methods.
* Inspect breaker connections at the bus bar and address any loose, damaged, or overheated connections identified during the installation.
* Inspect and address grounding, bonding, neutral, and equipment grounding connections as required for the installation.
* Verify circuit identification and organize the panel directory.
* Evaluate the existing service connections and associated components for any additional concerns identified during replacement.
* Test the completed installation to verify proper operation.
* Provide whole-home surge protection as a recommended additional upgrade, if included in the approved scope.

The Long-Term Benefit

Replacing the existing Crouse-Hinds panel is a proactive investment in the home’s electrical infrastructure. Rather than waiting for aging equipment to develop a problem, the homeowner can move forward with a modern panel that offers additional circuit spaces, improved serviceability, and a better foundation for future electrical upgrades.

The goal is not simply to replace a panel because it is old. It is to update an aging, critical electrical component so the home’s distribution system is better positioned to serve the family’s current needs and future electrical demands.

invoices.summary:
Please mail invoice and estimate 

Thank you for trusting LPH with your plumbing needs. We strive to provide professional, high-quality service on every visit, and your feedback helps us continue improving.

We would greatly appreciate hearing about your experience with the technician who served you today. Your feedback regarding the quality of work performed, communication, professionalism, and overall service is extremely valuable to us.

Thank you again for choosing LPH. We truly appreciate your business and the opportunity to serve you!

The homeowner was informed that the new hot and cold water lines installed approximately four years ago were reportedly not insulated. Technician inspected the underside of the mobile home and confirmed that the hot and cold water lines are insulated. Technician also verified that the heat tape installed on the water main is operational and that the heat tape outlet is functioning properly.

During the inspection, Technician observed that sections of the underside of the mobile home were missing insulation beneath the subfloor, as well as plastic sheeting. These missing materials may contribute to heat loss and increase the risk of the plumbing lines freezing during cold weather. Technician provided the homeowner with several referrals to assist with insulating the underside of the subfloor and providing additional protection for the existing hot and cold water lines.

Technician explained that if the homeowner is unable to find someone to complete the insulation work, Derrick may be able to assist with insulating the underside of the mobile home. However, LPH does not typically perform insulation work on mobile homes beyond insulating and protecting the water lines.

The homeowner also reported an issue with the electric heater located beneath the kitchen cabinet, which is not operating properly. An electrician is scheduled to visit the home on Monday to evaluate the heater and address the issue.

Thank you for allowing me into your home today to discuss replacement options for your current air conditioning system.

As requested, I have emailed the proposals for your review so you can discuss the situation and available options with your insurance company before making a final decision.

invoices.summary:
Technician was dispatched today to investigate a puddle of water on the left side of the chimney in the garage.

Upon inspection, the technician determined that the sewer line exits on the opposite side of the home, making it unlikely to be related to the issue. Additionally, there are no drain lines located near the chimney.

The technician found that the main water line enters the home on the right side of the chimney. Although there is a small possibility that the main water supply line could be contributing to the issue, the technician does not believe this is the most likely cause for the following reasons:

1. No indication of a continuous underground leak: The municipality has not contacted the homeowner regarding unusual water usage or a potential discrepancy between water consumption and meter readings. While this does not definitively rule out an underground leak, there is currently no known indication of one.
2. The water intrusion is intermittent: The homeowner has reported that this issue has been occurring over the past several months, but the puddle does not consistently return or progressively worsen. Because the main water line is pressurized, a leak in this line would generally be expected to produce a more continuous water loss, although the severity can vary depending on the type and location of the leak.

Based on the findings, the technician believes the issue is more likely related to the chimney or water intrusion from rain. The homeowner appears to experience the problem primarily after rainfall, and the technician observed staining along the bottom corner of the chimney. These findings suggest that water may be entering through or around the chimney.

Recommended Next Steps

We recommend having a qualified chimney professional inspect the chimney and determine whether there are any issues allowing water to enter the garage. If the chimney professional determines that the chimney is not the source of the water intrusion, further investigation of the home’s main water supply line may be necessary.

If the municipality contacts the homeowner regarding unusual water usage or a possible water meter discrepancy, we also recommend following up on those findings to help determine whether the main water line may be involved. 

If you have any questions or need further assistance, please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you for trusting LPH with your service needs!

LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, no electrical concerns were reported prior to our inspection. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, most of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel. However, this panel is only receiving 120V out of the 240 V that is required to have proper functionality of this panel. We’ve identified that both the basement panel and apartment panel are receiving the same voltage issues. This voltage issue is stemming from the outside service, losing 1/2 of it hot wires, which is causing an entire building issue.

We were not able to do the full electrical system check since half the home was not receiving proper power and we couldn’t evaluate if all the systems were indeed functioning correctly at this time. We did provide two solutions to remedy the main issue that the homeowners are dealing with. They did not move forward with any options today. However, they will inform us of their decision in the future. We thank you for having us out to evaluate your system, and we look forward to servicing in the future.

invoices.summary: This morning I arrived at the Strohl household for the annual electrical system and safety check. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies, however I noted several items in need of updating. First I noted the lack of proper smoke protection in the home. The house lacks up to date detectors, or detectors in the bedrooms. I also identified two double tapped breakers in the main breaker panel. This can lead to potential overheating and or failures within these breakers as they are not rated to handle two separate loads. Finally, I identified the lack of gas bonding in the home. Without effective bonding, stray electricity that may end up on the homes natural gas piping has no safe path off. I have provided several options and packages to complete all above listed work. If you have any questions related to today’s visit, please do not hesitate to contact us! Thank you and take care!

estimates.name: Premium Electrical Package
estimates.summary:
LPH will replace all smoke detectors in home. 2x HW Combination. 2x Batt Smoke.

LPH will install 2 tandem breakers to mitigate double tapping. 

LPH will install gas bonding. This option has LPH installing a #4 THHN stranded copper wire at the main breaker panels grounding bar, and extending said wire to a point on the homes main gas manifold where it will be connected via a cold water clamp. Protecting from potential electric shock hazards while using gas related systems in home and damage to appliances using gas ignition.

LPH will install a whole home surge protection device at the main breaker panel, protecting all circuits and appliances in the home from electrical surges.
Device comes with 50A breaker included in pricing.
LPH honors a lifetime unit replacement warranty for device should it be damaged by a surge.
Manufacturer honors a $100,000 dollar appliance damage warranty for any devices or systems damaged by a surge whilst device is installed.

invoices.summary:
LPH returned to the home to complete the emergency electrical service replacement due to the severely deteriorated condition of the existing exterior electrical service. During the initial evaluation, extensive aluminum oxide corrosion was found on the main neutral conductor inside the exterior meter base, along with substantial corrosion on the meter base itself and the upper service cable. Moisture was also present around the service cable entry point, creating a serious electrical safety concern and an increased risk of service failure, voltage fluctuations, equipment damage, and potential fire hazards.

Completed Scope of Work:

* Shut down the electrical service and disconnected the existing service conductors from the utility supply.
* Removed the existing service head, upper service cables, exterior meter base, and deteriorated service conductors feeding the home.
* Installed a new meter base and a new 200-amp exterior emergency disconnect.
* Installed new PVC raceway to protect the service conductors from direct exposure to moisture, rain, and ultraviolet rays.
* Installed new 200-amp service conductors from the service head through the meter base and exterior disconnect.
* Installed new 200-amp, four-wire conductors from the exterior disconnect into the home’s main electrical panel.
* Extended and properly terminated the existing grounding conductors at the new exterior disconnect.
* Installed a new grounding bar inside the exterior disconnect to provide proper termination for the grounding conductors.
* Separated the neutral and grounding conductors within the main electrical panel and installed a new grounding bar.
* Removed the existing neutral-to-ground bonding connection in the main panel to accommodate the new exterior service disconnect configuration.
* Installed a bonding bridge on the exterior of the home to provide a proper connection point for additional grounding and bonding systems, including telephone and cable services.
* Sealed the new exterior equipment, raceway, and wall penetrations with silicone to help prevent future moisture intrusion.
* Reconnected the utility service conductors using permanent compression crimps and installed new protective covers.
* Restored power to the home and tested the electrical service to verify proper operation.

Final Testing & Completion:

LPH completed the service replacement and verified that the new electrical service was properly energized and functioning as intended. All work was tested prior to leaving the home, and the electrical system was operating properly at the time of completion.

This replacement addresses the significant corrosion and moisture-related deterioration identified during the initial evaluation while providing a new, properly protected 200-amp service configuration. The new exterior disconnect also provides an accessible means of shutting off power to the home from outside.

Payment was collected for the completed services. Today’s invoice will be emailed to the homeowners. Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure working with you, and we look forward to servicing you again in the future.

invoices.summary:
Heating and Cooling System Inspection – Amana HVAC System

LPH completed a heating and cooling system inspection on an 11-year-old Amana gas furnace and AC system. The furnace was operating properly; however, the system’s cooling efficiency was below optimal levels.

During previous service visits, LPH determined that the system was low on refrigerant. During today’s inspection, LPH confirmed that the system remains low on refrigerant, indicating a potential refrigerant leak that requires further investigation.

Recommended Maintenance:

LPH observed that the furnace blower assembly and AC coil are dirty. LPH recommends cleaning the indoor and outdoor units to help improve system efficiency, restore proper airflow, enhance cooling performance, and reduce the risk of premature equipment breakdowns.

Refrigerant Leak Detection and Repair:

LPH recommends performing a refrigerant leak search to identify the source of the leak. Once the leak has been located, additional costs will apply for diagnosing the necessary repairs, completing the repairs, and recharging the system with the appropriate amount of refrigerant.

System Replacement Consideration:

The HVAC system is over 10 years old and is outside the manufacturer’s warranty coverage. Due to the age of the equipment, reduced cooling efficiency, and ongoing refrigerant issues, LPH recommends scheduling a comfort consultation to review potential system replacement options.

The homeowner should weigh the cost of leak detection, repairs, and refrigerant recharging against the investment in a new HVAC system. A new system may offer improved energy efficiency, greater reliability, and new manufacturer and labor warranty coverage, depending on the equipment selected and applicable warranty terms.

LPH Recommendation:

LPH recommends reviewing both repair and replacement options to determine the most cost-effective long-term solution for the homeowner. A comfort consultation will help compare the available options based on upfront costs, energy efficiency, expected reliability, and long-term operating expenses.

invoices.summary: This afternoon I arrived at the Sellers family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies. The one recommendation I had was regarding the main breaker panel. The panel appears to be in okay physical condition with some signs of rusting/ corrosion, but no or burning arcing. However, the panel is nearing what we would deem to be the average life expectancy for breaker panels. The panel is over 30 years old now. As panels age, the safety features within their breakers can begin to fail to function in the event of an electrical fault. Separate from this, should any breakers fail, or need to be replaced, it can be difficult to find replacements as they do not manufacture these parts anymore. I noted that the panel brand, while the breakers are assorted, is a “Challenger”. The Product the Sellers’ have is not one that was inherently recalled, but the company itself has an extensive history of recalls related to breaker failures. I noted several of the Challenger breakers are forming a rather loose connection which can ultimately lead to power failures, or potential overheating. I informed Mr. Sellers that while I didn’t have any immediate concerns, this is something that should begin to take precedence as a project to prevent potential failures down the road. I also encouraged the Sellers’ to run dehumidifiers in the panel spaces as they seem to be falling victim to ambient moisture with time. I have provided an estimate to replace the main breaker panel for all of the above listed reasons, I provided one separate option to run a gas bonding wire to the homes gas piping in order to meet code compliance and safety standards. I understand that you have just moved in, and more than likely were not expecting some of these options, but we want you to know that we are here to guide and help make your new home safe, comfortable, and efficient. If you have any questions related to todays visit, please do not hesitate to reach out. Otherwise, thank you for having me out today and I look forward to our next visit!

invoices.summary:
Technician arrived to address loss of heating and cooling on split AC and gas furnace system. Customer reported there was a burning odor at one point. This issue began Saturday. Found water inside the furnace. I performed a thorough evaluation of the furnace to identify the root cause of the issue. Ultimately the immediate failure was caused by a failed furnace control board. Board will not energize motors, which would explain the water since the AC was ran and the coil would’ve frozen. Confirmed the blower motor functioned, although it needs a new capacitor. During my evaluation I inspected the heat Exchnager and found a crack in the rear of the left hand cell. There was also extreme rust present throughout with at least one dimple rusted out. 

Given this failure, it is unsafe to operate the furnace in heating. I have shut off the gas valve and tagged the appliance. We will be out tomorrow to give options on furnace replacement.

invoices.summary:
We were called out to evaluate why the kitchen overhead lighting was not functioning. On arrival, we spoke with the homeowners to get a good understanding of what was going on. Once we got a good understanding of the issue, we then started our thorough evaluation at the electrical panel and then worked their way to the kitchen switches. We received proper and adequate voltages at both the panel and switch locations, but identified that one of the switches failed internally. We provided an option to replace the switch which was approved and completed today. After the new switch installation, the kitchen lighting was functioning correctly at this time. One year worry free parts and labor warranty will be honored for the new switch that we installed today.

However, when we first arrived at this property, we noticed that the main PPL triplex wire was no longer attached to the home and was starting to pull on the new service wires that LPH installed earlier this year. We contacted PPL to inform them of our findings and got them to schedule some of their technicians to arrive and correct this issue. 

Invoice for today’s visit will be emailed to the homeowner for the record. We thank you for allowing us into your home to service your electrical concern and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

estimates.summary:
This is to do a sewer line replacement/reroute from the sanitary line to right before the pit. LPH will use an excavating machine to expose the existing compromised sewer line. Once the sewer line is exposed, LPH will remove it and then lay down a bed of crushed stone. LPH will reroute the sanitary line to exit approximately 10’ to the left from where it is currently exiting the home to avoid moving the condenser. LPH will then start to connect the new schedule 40 PVC sewer line. Once the sewer line is connected, LPH will use hydraulic cement on the inside and outside foundation wall. Another bed of crushed stone will be placed on top and an inspection will be performed. Backfill will begin and will be tamped to a raked finish. The homeowner is responsible to finish the landscaping. The homeowner is responsible to move all personal belongings in the area of the basement where we will be performing the work. The homeowner is responsible to have branches from the tree removed so we can have room for the excavator.

invoices.summary:
Electrical System Check Summary

LPH completed an electrical system check throughout the home, evaluating the electrical panel, breakers, visible wiring and connections, receptacles, switches, GFCI protection, grounding and bonding, and overall electrical safety. We also checked for signs of overheating, loose connections, physical damage, corrosion, and other conditions that could affect the safe and reliable operation of the electrical system.

During today’s evaluation, LPH identified two kitchen receptacles with loose plug connections and visible burn damage on the faces of the devices from previous overheating. These conditions can lead to continued overheating, poor electrical contact, and potential fire hazards if left unaddressed. We also identified an exterior receptacle with rust and corrosion caused by water intrusion. Moisture had affected the device and caused the GFCI protection for the circuit to trip. Additionally, the home’s grounding system was found to need improvement. The existing grounding arrangement relies on a single buried grounding conductor that is undersized for the home’s 200-amp electrical service.

Summary of Findings and Recommended Options

1. Kitchen Receptacle Replacement: LPH recommended replacing the two damaged kitchen receptacles with 20-amp-rated devices, provided the existing circuit wiring and overcurrent protection are compatible with the upgrade. This will address the deteriorated receptacles and restore reliable plug connections.

2. Exterior Receptacle Replacement: LPH recommended replacing the rusted and corroded exterior receptacle with a new weather-resistant outdoor-rated device. A properly fitted, extra-duty in-use bubble cover would also be installed and sealed to the siding to help prevent future water intrusion and protect the receptacle when cords are plugged in.

3. Grounding System Improvement: LPH recommended improving the home’s grounding and bonding system by adding a properly sized grounding/bonding connection to the metal water main, where applicable. The customer elected to proceed with a short run of grounding conductor alongside the electrical panel to the water meter. This improvement will supplement the existing grounding arrangement and help provide a more effective path for electrical fault current, allowing the appropriate protective devices to operate as intended. The connection will be completed in accordance with applicable grounding and bonding requirements.

4. Ceiling Fan Installation Wiring Option: LPH also discussed the option of installing the necessary wiring for a ceiling fan in a room that currently has no ceiling fixture. This option would include establishing a suitable power source, running the required wiring to the desired ceiling location, and installing the appropriate electrical box and fan-rated support as needed. This would provide the necessary electrical infrastructure for a ceiling fan where no existing ceiling fixture or wiring is available.

Completed Work and Closing Summary

The customer elected to proceed with replacing the two damaged kitchen receptacles with 20-amp-rated devices and installing a short run of grounding conductor alongside the electrical panel to the water meter. LPH completed the approved work, and everything was tested and confirmed to be functioning properly prior to departure.

The remaining recommendations, including replacement and weatherproofing of the exterior receptacle and the optional ceiling fan wiring installation, were reviewed with the customer for consideration.

Today’s invoice summary and electrical system check evaluation will be emailed to the homeowner for their records. Thank you for choosing Lancaster Plumbing Heating, and thank you for allowing us into your home. It was a pleasure working with you, and we look forward to servicing your electrical needs again in the future.

estimates.name: Whole Home Surge Protection
estimates.summary:
Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a City Soft water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. The system also requires a dedicated electrical outlet for operation and regeneration cycles. The home’s electrical panel is located approximately 5 feet away, and an outlet will need to be installed and provided at the equipment location prior to or as part of the installation. Once installed, the system will provide conditioned water to the entire home and help minimize the long-term effects of hard water and chlorine exposure on the plumbing system.

I went to the system in the basement and found nothing was running but the furnace was not locked out on an error code. I found that the pump was full. I moved the pump and it came on, after it finished pumping the furnace came on. I filled the pump several times and it shut the furnace off before it would pump. I discussed that with her and gave her options. We changed the bad pump. The system is now running properly.

Bathroom Exhaust Fan Replacement

LPH tested the existing bathroom fan/light combination and verified that power was present at the switch, with proper voltage reaching both the light and fan connections. The light was operating properly; however, the exhaust fan motor would not start. All accessible connection points were inspected and found to be secure, indicating that the motor itself had failed.

The existing fan had been in operation for approximately 12 years and had reached the end of its service life.

Lisa and Glenn approved the recommended replacement. LPH replaced the existing exhaust fan with a new, top-of-the-line Panasonic WhisperQuiet fan designed for quiet operation, effective ventilation, and long-term reliability. This upgrade restores proper bathroom ventilation while providing dependable performance for years to come. With proper installation and maintenance, this type of fan can offer a service life of 20 years or more, depending on operating conditions.

Following installation, the new fan was tested to verify proper operation before leaving the home.

Smoke Detector Installation

Lisa and Glenn also approved the installation of two carbon monoxide combination smoke detectors throughout the home. LPH completed the installation and tested the detectors as applicable to verify proper operation, providing the homeowners with an additional layer of fire safety and early warning protection.

Pull-Chain Ceiling Fan Troubleshooting and Repair

LPH also evaluated a ceiling fan that was not operating properly. During troubleshooting, we discovered that the fan was equipped with a remote control and receiver. The homeowners had previously replaced the remote’s batteries without success, and the remote had since been discarded.

LPH discussed the available repair options with Lisa, including installing a new receiver to restore remote-control functionality. Lisa elected to have the fan operate directly from the existing wall switch and pull chains without the remote-control system.

To accommodate her preference, LPH removed the existing receiver, allowing the fan to be controlled through the wall switch and pull chains rather than relying on the remote-control system.

Complimentary Receptacle Cover Plate

During the visit, Lisa also needed a cover plate for a receptacle that was missing one. As a courtesy, LPH provided her with a complimentary receptacle cover plate to address this need and help ensure the outlet had the proper protective covering.

Completion and Closing

All approved work was completed and tested prior to LPH leaving the home. Lisa and Glenn were informed of the completed work and the improvements made to their home’s electrical safety and bathroom ventilation.

Today’s invoice will be emailed to the homeowners for their records.

Thank you, Lisa and Glenn, for allowing LPH into your home. Lisa, it was an absolute pleasure working with you, and we truly appreciate the opportunity to take care of your home’s electrical needs. We look forward to helping you again in the future!

invoices.summary: This afternoon I arrived at the Thomas family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon my arrival, Mrs. Thomas informed me that she was having power issues with a GFCI receptacle that LPH had installed a couple of years ago. estimates.name: Water softener
estimates.summary:
Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 16 grains per gallon (GPG) and the chlorine level to be 1.0 ppm. A hardness level of 16 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, showerheads, and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a City Soft water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. Benefits of the system include improved soap and detergent performance, reduced spotting and scaling, softer-feeling water, and increased protection and efficiency of plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances.

The proposed installation location for the City Soft system is near the existing water heater. The water inlet from the water meter to the water softener would have to be routed about the bathroom area in order to supply treated water to home. Water meter is approximately 20’ away from proposed area. The softener’s backwash drain lines will be routed and connected to the washer drain approximately 5’ away. The system also requires a dedicated electrical outlet for operation and regeneration cycles. The home’s electrical panel is located approximately 75 feet away, and an outlet will need to be installed and provided at the equipment location prior to or as part of the installation. Homeowner is going to consult with LPH electrician once they are ready. Once installed, the system will provide conditioned water to the entire home and help minimize the long-term effects of hard water and chlorine exposure on the plumbing system.

estimates.name: Moen Flo
estimates.summary:
A Moen Flo Smart Water Monitor and Shutoff is a device installed on your home's main water supply line. It monitors water usage, looks for leaks and abnormal water flow, and can automatically shut off the water to help prevent costly damage.
The biggest benefits of a Moen Flo
1. Prevents major water damage
Flo can detect unusual water flow, such as a burst pipe or a running appliance, and automatically shut off your home's water supply when its leak-detection system identifies a qualifying problem. This can help prevent flooded basements, damaged floors and expensive repairs.
2. Detects small, hidden leaks
It monitors water flow and pressure to help identify potential problems, including slow leaks that might otherwise go unnoticed behind walls, under sinks or in plumbing fixtures.
3. Sends alerts to your phone
You can receive notifications about possible leaks, unusual water usage and system activity, giving you a chance to respond even when you're away from home.
4. Tracks water consumption
See how much water your household uses and identify unexpected increases that could indicate waste, a running toilet or a leak.
5. Provides peace of mind while traveling
If a pipe breaks while you're on vacation or a hose fails while you're away, automatic shutoff may significantly limit the amount of water that escapes.
6. May help with homeowners insurance
Some insurers offer discounts or incentives for approved water-leak prevention devices. Savings aren't guaranteed, so check with your insurer before purchasing.

invoices.summary: Homeowner stated that they have lived at the residence for approximately 30 years and have never experienced any groundwater issues in the basement. The basement is waterproofed beneath the concrete slab and is equipped with a sump pump pit. A 1-inch drainage channel runs along the perimeter of the basement at the foundation block wall. Homeowner expressed concern about the dehumidifier condensate draining into this channel. During the inspection, the technician observed that the furnace condensate also drains into the same channel and has been doing so since the home was built. Based on the homeowner’s experience and the existing drainage setup, the homeowner is not interested in installing a sump pump at this time.

invoices.summary:
Thank you for allowing me into your home today to discuss replacement options for your current HVAC system.

During our visit, we reviewed the condition of your existing system, which is currently not operational, and discussed your comfort needs, efficiency goals, and expectations for a new system. Based on our conversation and the measurements taken, I put together three replacement options offering different levels of efficiency and performance.

Two of the options feature Bosch systems, both of which would require a new dedicated electrical circuit to be run from your electrical panel to the outdoor unit. This work has been accounted for in the proposed options to ensure the new equipment is installed properly and meets applicable electrical codes.

As requested, I have emailed all three options for your review and comparison. I understand you are also gathering estimates from other companies and plan to make a decision soon. I encourage you to review not only the equipment and pricing but also the efficiency ratings, installation scope, and warranty coverage when comparing your options.

I left my business card with my contact information. If you have any questions, concerns, or would like to discuss the differences between the systems in more detail, please don’t hesitate to call or text me.

Thank you again for your time and the opportunity to earn your business. I look forward to the possibility of working with you on this project and helping you get your home’s heating and cooling system back up and running.

Thank you for trusting LPH with your plumbing needs. We strive to provide professional, high-quality service on every visit, and your feedback helps us continue improving.

We would greatly appreciate hearing about your experience with the technician who served you today. Your feedback regarding the quality of work performed, communication, professionalism, and overall service is extremely valuable to us.

Thank you again for choosing LPH. We truly appreciate your business and the opportunity to serve you!

Technician performed a thorough plumbing system inspection on all accessible plumbing fixtures throughout the home to evaluate overall operation, drainage, water flow, and visible plumbing conditions. During the inspection, technician identified a few concerns within the plumbing system and discussed recommended solutions with the homeowner to address the issues found. Technician reviewed available repair and improvement options to help maintain proper system performance and prevent future plumbing problems.

The second-floor hallway bathroom toilet failed the dye test, indicating that the flapper is not sealing properly and may be allowing water to leak from the tank into the toilet bowl. A faulty flapper can cause continuous water loss and unnecessary water usage. Technician recommends replacing the toilet flapper to restore a proper seal, prevent water waste, and help ensure the toilet operates efficiently.

The basement powder room toilet failed the dye test, indicating that the flapper is not sealing properly and allowing water to leak from the tank into the toilet bowl. Technician recommends replacing the toilet flapper to restore a proper seal, prevent continuous water loss, and improve the toilet’s overall flushing performance.

Technician recommends installing a reverse osmosis (RO) drinking water system at the kitchen sink to improve the quality and taste of drinking water.

The existing ejector pump pit is not properly vented, and the check valve is currently located inside the pit, making future maintenance and servicing more difficult. Additionally, the system is not equipped with a high-level alert alarm to provide notification if the wastewater level rises above its normal operating level due to a pump failure or other issue.

Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 8 grains per gallon (GPG) and the chlorine level to be 2.0 ppm. A hardness level of 8 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, showerheads, and water-using appliances.

estimates.summary:
The second-floor hallway bathroom toilet failed the dye test, indicating that the flapper is not sealing properly and may be allowing water to leak from the tank into the toilet bowl. A faulty flapper can cause continuous water loss and unnecessary water usage. Technician recommends replacing the toilet flapper to restore a proper seal, prevent water waste, and help ensure the toilet operates efficiently.

The basement powder room toilet failed the dye test, indicating that the flapper is not sealing properly and allowing water to leak from the tank into the toilet bowl. Technician recommends replacing the toilet flapper to restore a proper seal, prevent continuous water loss, and improve the toilet’s overall flushing performance.

Reverse Osmosis System Installation

Technician recommends installing a reverse osmosis (RO) drinking water system at the kitchen sink to improve the quality and taste of drinking water. The RO system would help reduce chlorine taste and odor, along with other impurities commonly found in municipal water. Having a dedicated RO faucet at the kitchen sink would provide convenient access to filtered drinking water while reducing the need to purchase bottled water, potentially saving money over time.


The existing ejector pump pit is not properly vented, and the check valve is currently located inside the pit, making future maintenance and servicing more difficult. Additionally, the system is not equipped with a high-level alert alarm to provide notification if the wastewater level rises above its normal operating level due to a pump failure or other issue.

Technician recommends replacing the existing ejector pump pit lid and repiping the pump discharge to relocate the check valve outside of the pit for easier access and future maintenance. A service valve would also be installed above the check valve to allow the discharge line to be isolated when servicing the system. Technician further recommends connecting the ejector pit vent to the main vent line above the pit to provide proper ventilation, help the system operate as intended, and reduce the potential for sewer gas odors entering the home. Adding a high-level alert alarm is also recommended to provide an early warning if the pit water level rises excessively, helping reduce the risk of a wastewater backup.

The existing ejector pump is not equipped with a high-level tank alarm. The homeowner reported a previous backup into the basement shower pan, indicating the potential for future wastewater backups if the ejector pump system experiences a failure or cannot keep up with incoming wastewater. Technician recommends installing a high-level tank alarm to provide an audible alert if the wastewater level inside the ejector pit rises above its normal operating level. This added safety measure would help provide an early warning of a potential pump failure or drainage issue, allowing the necessary action to be taken before wastewater backs up into the home. A separate electrical outlet would need to be provided for the high-level alarm, independent of the ejector pump’s existing outlet.

Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 8 grains per gallon (GPG) and the chlorine level to be 2.0 ppm. A hardness level of 8 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, showerheads, and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a City Soft water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. Benefits of the system include improved soap and detergent performance, reduced spotting and scaling, softer-feeling water, and increased protection and efficiency of plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances.

The proposed installation location for the City Soft system is near the existing water heater to allow for efficient integration into the home’s main water distribution system. The softener’s backwash drain lines will be routed and connected to the existing main drain located behind the water heater at the proposed installation area. The system also requires a dedicated electrical outlet for operation and regeneration cycles. An outlet is provided. Once installed, the system will provide conditioned water to the entire home and help minimize the long-term effects of hard water and chlorine exposure on the plumbing system.

invoices.summary:
Electrical Panel Inspection
During today’s electrical inspection, I observed that the electrical panel appears to be newer; however, a couple of older circuit breakers remain installed. Circuit breakers typically have an expected service life of approximately 25–30 years, depending on their condition and usage. As breakers age, they may become more prone to malfunction. I recommend evaluating and replacing the older breakers as needed to help maintain the safety and reliability of the electrical system.

2. Whole-Home Surge Protection
I also observed that no whole-home surge protection device is currently installed. Whole-home surge protection helps protect major household appliances and electronic equipment from voltage surges that can potentially cause damage. I recommend installing a whole-home surge protection device for added protection. The recommended device includes a lifetime warranty and $100,000 in connected-equipment coverage, subject to the manufacturer’s terms and conditions.

3. Doorbell Transformer Troubleshooting
I investigated the issue with the non-functioning doorbell. Proper voltage was present at the incoming side of the transformer, but no proper voltage was being supplied from the outgoing side. This indicates that the transformer is not functioning correctly and requires replacement.

I informed the homeowner that replacing the faulty transformer with a compatible replacement should restore proper doorbell operation, assuming no other issues are present. The homeowner stated that she would replace the transformer herself.

Invoice and Estimate
The invoice for today’s inspection and troubleshooting, along with an estimate for the recommended electrical work, will be provided separately.

Thank you for trusting LPH with your plumbing needs. We strive to provide professional, high-quality service on every visit, and your feedback helps us continue improving.

We would greatly appreciate hearing about your experience with the technician who served you today. Your feedback regarding the quality of work performed, communication, professionalism, and overall service is extremely valuable to us.

Thank you again for choosing LPH. We truly appreciate your business and the opportunity to serve you!

Homeowner reported that the water stopped flowing from the well during an evening shower. Technician checked the voltage at the disconnect and pressure switch, measuring 245 volts, and verified voltage across the pressure switch. Technician removed the well cover and discovered that the well pipe had separated from the pitless adapter, leaving the well pump suspended by the electrical wiring. Technician was able to manually retrieve the well pump and remove the pitless adapter, where a broken plastic barbed adapter was discovered.

Technician replaced the broken plastic barbed adapter with a stainless-steel barbed adapter for improved durability and secured the well wiring more securely to the well pipe. Technician checked continuity and measured the well depth at 54 feet, with the well pump positioned at 41 feet. After completing the repairs, Technician reinstalled the well pump into the well casing and restored power to the system. The pump’s amperage draw was measured at 5.7 amps.

The well pump is approximately 16 years old and is currently operating properly based on the technician’s checks. The issue was caused by the failed plastic barbed adapter, which allowed the well pipe to separate from the pitless adapter. The adapter was replaced, and the well system was returned to operation.

Technician also provided a solution for, 

During the well pump diagnostic, Technician noticed that the existing pressure tank and associated fittings are galvanized and appear to be original to the home. Due to the age of these components, Technician recommends proactively updating the pressure tank and related accessories to help maintain the reliability and proper operation of the well water system. The existing galvanized fittings should be removed and replaced with modern fittings, as galvanized piping and fittings can corrode internally over time, potentially restricting water flow and contributing to leaks or other plumbing issues. Updating the pressure tank and its associated components would also provide an opportunity to inspect the connections and related equipment for signs of wear, corrosion, or deterioration. Replacing these aging components can help reduce the risk of unexpected failures, improve system reliability, and provide greater peace of mind regarding the home’s well water system.

Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 24 grains per gallon (GPG) and the  level to be 8.0 ppm. A hardness level of 16 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, shower heads, and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

LPH Return Visit – Zoning Issues

LPH returned today to address ongoing zoning issues. The homeowner has a three-zone thermostat system with a total of 14 zone dampers. The homeowner reported that two zones were operating while the thermostat screen for Zone 1 was blank.

Upon inspection, LPH determined that Zone 1 was drawing excessive power due to the nine zone dampers connected to that zone. To correct the issue, LPH will order an SDCR (Secondary Damper Control Relay) and install an additional transformer to power the relay. The SDCR will help distribute the electrical load required to operate the dampers, allowing the zoning system to function properly.

In the meantime, LPH disconnected Zone 1 and its associated dampers to prevent further issues while maintaining heat to the home through the remaining two operational zones.

LPH will return once the necessary parts arrive to install the SDCR and additional transformer, reconnect Zone 1, and verify proper operation of the entire zoning system.

estimates.name: Constant pressure switch + well tank and accessories
estimates.summary:
Instead of having a pressure switch were the psi goes from 30 to 50. This unit gives constant pressure. And it protects the pump from dry firing. A sub drive package for a well system usually refers to a submersible pump drive package or a variable frequency drive (VFD) package used to control a well pump. In water-well and industrial well applications, it allows the pump to operate more efficiently by controlling the speed of its electric motor. 
1. Consistent water pressure
Reduces the pressure swings commonly experienced with traditional pressure-switch systems. Showers, faucets, and irrigation equipment can operate more consistently.
2. Better pump and motor protection
Depending on the model, built-in protections can detect overloads, low motor load associated with dry running, and certain electrical faults. This can help prevent costly damage.
3. Softer starts and stops
The drive gradually ramps motor speed up and down, reducing abrupt starting stresses and potentially reducing pressure surges and mechanical wear.
4. Potential energy savings
When water demand is low, the pump may run at a lower speed and use less power. Actual savings depend on pump sizing, operating conditions, and how much demand varies.
5. Smaller pressure tank
Many constant-pressure installations can use a smaller tank than a conventional on/off system, saving space and potentially reducing installation complexity.
6. Better control of well production
The pump can be adjusted to match water demand and, when properly configured, help limit pumping to the well's sustainable yield. This is particularly valuable for low-yield wells.

invoices.summary:
Miriam call us out today because she looked inside the brine tank and saw water above the salt. Since this was something that she has not witnessed in the past, she thought that there was an issue with her water softener. 

After evaluating the system, a technician was able to explain that this was normal because the last step in the regeneration for this specific water softener is when the brine tank is filled with water. The technician did run it through an abbreviated regeneration to make sure everything was operating properly and that the float switch to the water softener to cut water flow once the brine tank was filled sufficiently.

Today, I was called out to inspect an issue with the bathroom exhaust fan. Upon inspection, I found that the fan motor is beginning to fail, which is common as these units age. As the motor continues to deteriorate, it will likely become progressively louder before eventually seizing up and ceasing to function.

I attempted to locate a replacement motor; however, due to the age of the unit, I was unable to find a compatible replacement motor by itself. Based on my findings, I recommend replacing the entire bathroom exhaust fan.

I also attempted to locate the exterior vent cap for the bathroom exhaust but was unable to identify it. Additionally, I was unable to access the attic to verify the exhaust ductwork and confirm that the fan is properly vented to the exterior. I informed the homeowner that the fan may not be vented properly, and further inspection may be necessary to determine whether new venting is required.

Recommended Options:

Option 1: Replace Bathroom Exhaust Fan
Remove the existing bathroom exhaust fan and install a new unit. This option addresses the failing motor. Existing venting will be used if it can be verified as present and suitable for the new fan.

Option 2: Replace Bathroom Exhaust Fan and Install Venting if Needed
Remove the existing bathroom exhaust fan and install a new unit. Inspect the venting as access allows and, if the fan is not properly vented to the exterior, provide and install the necessary ductwork and exterior vent cap to ensure proper exhaust ventilation.

We were called out today because of a leak taking place on a waterline near the water heater. Upon arrival technician was able to diagnose where the leak was coming from and quickly went to figuring out how to shut the water off. The technician did try the whole home, shuttle valve located on the backside of the home, but due to the frailty of that shut off valve, the technician felt it best to shut the water off at the curb stop. The technician was able to locate a curb stop but was not able to determine whether or not that curb stop shut the water off for our customer. 

The technician took the time to track down the park maintenance supervisor in order to get assistance with figuring this out and to also getting the water shut off. Once the maintenance supervisor got on site he went to work digging out around the riser for the curb stop because there was mud in the way of getting onto the valve with the curb stop key. Once the hole was dug deep enough around the riser we were then able to use a piece of 1 inch PVC to dig the mud out above the valve. 

Once this was done, the technician was able to shut the water off. The repair took a little longer than anticipated due to the accessibility of two of the waterlines we were tying back onto. The repair was successfully made, water was restored to the home, and the technician proceeded to make sure all new connections were water tight, and water was flowing properly.  There were no further issues at this time.

If you have any other questions or concerns that arise after today’s visit, please do not hesitate to give us a call. Thank you for continuing to trust Lancaster Plumbing and Heating with all of your home service needs.

invoices.summary:
New 20-Amp Circuit and Receptacle Installation

LPH installed one new 20-amp circuit originating from the electrical panel, including two new receptacles mounted together in a two-gang electrical box. The wiring was routed down the wall in protective PVC conduit, with an approximate total run of 20 feet.

Basement Lighting Adjustment

LPH extended approximately 8 feet of wiring from an existing lighting junction box to relocate the power connection for the existing keyless light fixtures. This adjustment moved the lights a couple of feet closer to the front basement wall, improving their placement to better suit the homeowner’s needs.

Timer Switch Installation

LPH installed four homeowner-supplied timer switches. Two timer switches were installed to control the upstairs bathroom exhaust fans, and two additional timer switches were installed in a three-way switching arrangement for the attic lights. These additions provide convenient timer controls for the bathroom ventilation and attic lighting.

Exterior Electrical Service Connection Repair

LPH removed the existing reversible crimp connections on the exterior electrical service and replaced them with permanent crimp connections and appropriate protective covers. This corrected the existing connection concern and provided a more secure, permanent connection.

Final Testing and Completion

After completing all work, LPH tested the installations and verified that everything was operating properly. All completed work was reviewed with the homeowner.

Payment was collected for today’s services, and an invoice summary will be emailed to the homeowner for their records.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure working with you, and we look forward to servicing you again in the future!

invoices.summary:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, Dake had no major electrical concerns and he mentioned that this house was remodeled. His only minor concern, was his front exterior outlet did not work. We identified that the GFI in the powder room was tripped, and upon resetting, the outside outlet was now functioning correctly. We did identify that both exterior outlets do not have the style of covers that are designed to see direct weather.

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel.

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

invoices.summary:
Thank you for trusting LPH with your plumbing needs. We strive to provide professional, high-quality service on every visit, and your feedback helps us continue improving.

We would greatly appreciate hearing about your experience with the technician who served you today. Your feedback regarding the quality of work performed, communication, professionalism, and overall service is extremely valuable to us.

Thank you again for choosing LPH. We truly appreciate your business and the opportunity to serve you!

The homeowner reported experiencing low water pressure from the well system for approximately two months. Technician verified that the pressure switch was receiving the proper voltage of 248 VAC. Technician then shut off the breaker to the well pump and drained the pressure tank, confirming that the tank pressure was at 0 PSI. Technician attempted to recharge the pressure tank with air but found that the internal bladder would not hold air, indicating that the pressure tank has failed and requires replacement.
During the inspection, Technician also observed that the existing brass tank tee assembly was badly corroded. The pressure gauge was not functioning, and the existing 30/50 pressure switch showed signs of rust beneath the cap, along with visible burn marks on the plastic cap. Due to the condition of these components, Technician recommends replacing the pressure tank, tank tee assembly, pressure switch, pressure gauge, pressure relief valve, and drain-down valve. Stainless steel fittings would be used for the new tank connections to provide improved corrosion resistance and help ensure reliable operation of the well pressure system. Replacing these components would help restore proper system operation, improve pressure monitoring and control, and address the deteriorated fittings and electrical components.
