The homeowner reported experiencing low water pressure from the well system for approximately two months. Technician verified that the pressure switch was receiving the proper voltage of 248 VAC. Technician then shut off the breaker to the well pump and drained the pressure tank, confirming that the tank pressure was at 0 PSI. Technician attempted to recharge the pressure tank with air but found that the internal bladder would not hold air, indicating that the pressure tank has failed and requires replacement.
During the inspection, Technician also observed that the existing brass tank tee assembly was badly corroded. The pressure gauge was not functioning, and the existing 30/50 pressure switch showed signs of rust beneath the cap, along with visible burn marks on the plastic cap. Due to the condition of these components, Technician recommends replacing the pressure tank, tank tee assembly, pressure switch, pressure gauge, pressure relief valve, and drain-down valve. Stainless steel fittings would be used for the new tank connections to provide improved corrosion resistance and help ensure reliable operation of the well pressure system. Replacing these components would help restore proper system operation, improve pressure monitoring and control, and address the deteriorated fittings and electrical components.

estimates.name: Everything Option
estimates.summary:
LPH arrived at the residence to evaluate the existing electrical system and discuss recommended improvements to enhance electrical safety, reliability, and protection throughout the home.

Basement Trough and Disconnect Replacement:

Upon inspection, LPH identified extensive rust and corrosion within the existing basement electrical trough, indicating a history of water intrusion and moisture exposure. The moisture has affected the wiring connections, leaving a film of oxidation and corrosion on the connection points and lugs. Corroded connections can increase electrical resistance, generate excessive heat, and compromise the reliability of the electrical system.

Additionally, the disconnect supplying the upstairs bedroom electrical panel has exceeded its recommended service life and shows considerable rust and corrosion throughout the enclosure. The internal lugs have also developed oxidation and corrosion, further compromising the integrity of the electrical connections. This disconnect contains a discontinued Zinsco breaker, a product line widely associated with serious safety concerns, including breakers that may fail to trip during an overload or short circuit, overheating, and connections that can deteriorate over time. These concerns can increase the risk of electrical fires and may also create complications during insurance reviews or real estate transactions.

LPH recommends replacing the existing trough and disconnect arrangement with a new electrical trough mounted securely to a backer board. The existing wiring will be reconnected using heavy-duty Polaris insulated connectors, providing secure, reliable connections. A new 100-amp disconnect will also be installed on the backer board to supply the upstairs electrical panel. This replacement will eliminate the deteriorated equipment and outdated disconnect, improve the integrity of the electrical connections, and provide a safer, more dependable electrical distribution setup.

Whole-Home Surge Protection:

During the inspection, LPH also identified deterioration affecting the electronic driver components of the arc-fault circuit interrupter (AFCI) breaker in the upstairs electrical panel. This is the only AFCI breaker currently installed in the home. Electronic components can experience wear and deterioration over time from transient voltage spikes that occur throughout a home’s electrical system. These voltage fluctuations can be generated when motor-driven equipment, such as air conditioners, refrigerators, and other appliances, cycles on and off. Utility-related disturbances and lightning can also introduce damaging voltage surges.

LPH recommends installing a premium whole-home surge protector at the electrical service equipment. This device helps limit damaging transient overvoltages before they reach connected circuits and sensitive electronic equipment. By reducing exposure to these voltage spikes, whole-home surge protection can help protect appliance control boards, televisions, computers, and other valuable electronics, potentially extending their service life and reducing the likelihood of costly premature failures. While no surge protector can eliminate every electrical threat, this upgrade provides an additional layer of protection for the home’s electrical system and connected equipment.

Exterior Receptacle Safety Improvements:

During the evaluation, LPH discovered that the exterior receptacles lack GFCI protection and that two of the existing receptacles have improper covers. The receptacles currently installed are intended for indoor use and have deteriorated significantly from prolonged exposure to outdoor conditions. Moisture intrusion and corrosion can compromise receptacle connections, increase the likelihood of electrical failures, and create potential shock hazards.

LPH recommends replacing the affected exterior receptacles with weather-resistant devices designed for outdoor applications. The proposed improvements include one weather-resistant receptacle, three weather-resistant GFCI receptacles, and two extra-duty in-use bubble covers. GFCI protection helps reduce the risk of serious electrical shock by quickly interrupting power when a ground fault is detected. The weather-resistant receptacles and properly rated covers will provide improved protection against rain, moisture, and environmental exposure. The in-use bubble covers are designed to help protect receptacles while cords are plugged in, providing an additional layer of protection against water intrusion.

These improvements will address the deteriorated exterior devices, bring the receptacle installations closer to current safety expectations, and provide more dependable outdoor electrical service.

LPH recommends completing these improvements to address the existing corrosion, eliminate the outdated Zinsco disconnect, improve electrical connection reliability, and add protection against electrical shock and damaging voltage surges. Together, these upgrades will help improve the overall safety, reliability, and long-term performance of the home’s electrical system.

estimates.name: Water softener
estimates.summary:
Water softener is only four grain hard. That is where they start recommending installing a unit. 

A water softener removes or reduces the minerals that cause hard water, mainly calcium and magnesium. If your home has hard water, a water softener can make a noticeable difference in cleaning, bathing, and maintaining appliances.
The 7 main benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale buildup
Reduces white, chalky deposits on faucets, showerheads, sinks, glass shower doors, and inside plumbing and water-heating equipment.
2. Softer-feeling skin and hair
Many people find their skin feels less dry and their hair feels smoother because soap rinses away more easily. It won't cure skin conditions, however.
3. Softer, cleaner laundry
Clothes and towels may feel less stiff, detergent works more effectively, and mineral deposits on fabrics can be reduced.
4. Cleaner dishes and glassware
Helps prevent cloudy spots and mineral film on glasses, silverware, and dishes.
5. Helps protect appliances
Reduces scale inside water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and other water-using equipment. This can help maintain efficiency and reduce maintenance.
6. Less soap and detergent needed
Soft water allows soap to lather more easily, so you may use less shampoo, body wash, laundry detergent, and household cleaning products.
7. Easier household cleaning
Less time spent scrubbing mineral deposits off shower doors, faucets, sinks, and bathroom fixtures.

This option does not include having an electrical ran out to the unit. Are the technician can drill a hole through the drywall to plug into an outlet or electrician will have to come out and give a price.

estimates.name: Moen Flo
estimates.summary:
The Moen Flo Smart Water Monitor & Shutoff is a smart-home device designed to help protect your house from water leaks and flooding. It installs on your main water line and monitors your home's water use 24/7. Unlike a water softener, it doesn't soften water or remove minerals — its main purpose is to prevent water damage.
The 6 biggest benefits of Moen Flo
1. Automatically shuts off water during a potential leak
If it detects a serious leak or unusual water usage, Flo can close your home's main water valve to help prevent flooding. This is especially valuable if a washing machine hose, toilet supply line, or pipe fails while you're away. 
2. Detects small hidden leaks
Its daily MicroLeak tests can identify leaks as small as approximately one drop per minute, potentially catching a slow leak behind a wall or under a floor before it causes extensive damage. 
3. Protects your home when you're on vacation
You can receive alerts remotely and shut off the water through the app. Automatic shutoff adds another layer of protection when nobody is home to notice a burst pipe or leaking appliance. 
4. Helps reduce water waste
Flo tracks water flow, pressure, and usage patterns. You may discover running toilets, dripping fixtures, or other problems that increase your water bill. 
5. Monitors water pressure and temperature
It can flag unusual pressure or flow conditions and send freezing-condition warnings, helping you spot potential plumbing problems early. 
6. May help reduce expensive water-damage repairs
Catching a leak early can help protect hardwood floors, drywall, ceilings, cabinets, and finished basements. Some insurers may also offer discounts for qualifying leak-prevention systems. 


This option does not include having an electrical ran out to the unit. Are the technician can drill a hole through the drywall to plug into an outlet or electrician will have to come out and give a price.

Summary: Replacement of Saniflo Toilet Pump

The existing Saniflo Saniplus macerator pump was identified as not pumping properly, with the motor humming or running without effectively discharging wastewater. The planned work is to replace the complete macerator unit. The replacement process includes shutting off the water supply and disconnecting the electrical power, draining the unit as safely as possible, disconnecting the toilet inlet and discharge pipework, and removing the existing macerator. The new unit will be installed using the correct seals and compatible plumbing connections, ensuring that all pipework and discharge connections are properly secured. Once installation is complete, the water supply and electrical power will be restored, and the system will be tested to verify proper operation, effective waste discharge, and leak-free connections. All work will be carried out in accordance with the manufacturer’s installation instructions and applicable plumbing and electrical safety requirements.

Depending on the pump, technician may have to cut open some drywall to access piping.

estimates.name: Water softener
estimates.summary:
Homeowner was very interested in the water quality. Technician explained everything and tested the water. Homeowner has twice the amount of chlorine in the water that a pool has. Water is also six grains hard.

Top 7 benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale buildup
Helps prevent the white, chalky deposits on faucets, showerheads, glass doors, and inside pipes. Bathrooms and kitchens are generally easier to clean.
2. Helps appliances last longer
Reduces mineral scale in water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and other water-using equipment, potentially improving efficiency and reducing maintenance.
3. Better soap and shampoo performance
Soap lathers more easily, and you may use less detergent, shampoo, and cleaning products.
4. Softer-feeling skin and hair
Some people notice less soap residue, dry-feeling skin, or stiff hair after showering. Results vary, and a softener does not treat skin conditions.
5. Cleaner dishes and glassware
Can reduce cloudy spots on glasses, mineral film on dishes, and buildup around the sink.
6. Potential energy savings
Less scale inside a water heater can help it transfer heat more efficiently. The benefit depends on how hard your water is and how much scale would otherwise accumulate.
7. Less household maintenance
Less scrubbing, fewer mineral deposits, and potentially fewer plumbing or appliance issues over time.

To address this concern, we recommend installing the appropriate bonding conductors from the main electrical panel to the gas piping at the gas meter and the water piping at the water meter, as required by applicable electrical codes.

A water softener removes or reduces hardness minerals—mainly calcium and magnesium—from your household water. It can make a noticeable difference in cleaning, bathing, plumbing, and appliance maintenance, especially if you have hard water.
7 main benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale buildup
Reduces white, chalky deposits on showerheads, faucets, sinks, and glass. It also helps prevent scale buildup inside pipes and water heaters.
2. Softer-feeling skin and hair
Soap rinses away more easily, and some people notice less residue, dryness, or stiffness in their hair. Results vary depending on your skin and hair type.
3. Softer, cleaner laundry
Clothes and towels may feel less stiff, and mineral deposits on fabrics can be reduced.
4. Less soap and detergent
Soft water allows soap to lather more readily, so you may need less laundry detergent, dish soap, and some cleaning products.
5. Better appliance efficiency

invoices.summary: LPH arrived at the Jacunski family home to conduct their annual electrical system check. Upon performing an annual electrical system and safety check I found no major discrepancies. I noted a couple of double tapped breakers in the main breaker panel which I provided an estimate to replace. Double tapped breakers mean there is a single breaker supplying two or more separate circuits. These breakers are only designed to support one circuit. When they have two or more, it can be difficult for the single wire lug to make a secure connection to both lines, over time these lugs can work themselves loose and lead to potential overheating. This can cause damage to both the circuit, the breaker, and the panels bus bar. I provided a solution to install tandem breakers in order to remove the double tapped set up. I provided an additional solution to replace a faulty timer inside of a landscape lighting transformer located on the back of the home. It seems as though the gearing within the timer is not making proper contact, and in turn it isn’t actuating the on and off switch for the lights. I was able to manually turn the gears and restore power to the lights to verify proper function through the rest of the system. Otherwise, the home appears to be in good electrical condition. If you have any questions, or if you would like to move forward with these options, please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you!

invoices.summary:
We arrived to complete our annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, the homeowners had no immediate concerns prior to our electrical inspection. However, upon our interior panel inspection, we noticed some voltage concerns that caught our attention. 

We received 128 V on one phase conductor from neutral, the other phase conductor was at 121 V to neutral, and combined was at 249 V. Next we turned off the solar disconnect underneath the inverter and received 125 V on the one phase conductor( the same one that previously read 128V) and the other phase conductor was at 123 V. Whilst the solar disconnect was off, we then put this panel under a heavy load by kicking on the AC and the dryer, but did not notice any severe voltage drops/spikes on any of the phase conductors at this time. Upon re-engaging the solar disconnect underneath the inverter. The first phase conductor spiked to 130 V while the second phase conductor dropped to 119 V, and then proceeded to drop to the previous 128/121 V that we previously received at the start of this call. 

We then took voltages at the exterior meter base, to help identify if this was a service wire issue. We received a steady 124 V on each phase conductor with a combined voltage of 249 V. Before we put the panel cover back on to speak with the homeowner, we did another set of testing and then received the normal in-line voltage readings on both phase conductors. This leads us to the conclusion that the solar system would need to be at least addressed by a solar technician to ensure that system is functioning properly, and not affecting the overall voltages coming into the home. Please refer to pictures attached to the email for extra information.

We then proceeded to go through the rest of the electrical system check in the home and was informed that the homeowner had a new bathroom exhaust fan on hand that they wanted to quote for. We also identified that the receptacle in this bathroom is not properly protected by GFI. However, when we brought this GFI protection concern to the homeowner, they informed us that this receptacle was previously protected by GFI breaker. We confirmed this to be the case by looking at the previous pictures, where we identified the old GFI breaker that was not replaced upon the panel replacement. We installed a brand new white GFI receptacle in the bathroom to resolve this issue. The only GFI receptacle we had on hand that matched the color that the homeowners wanted was a might light combo unit that was installed at this time. This new GFI receptacle will come with a one year worth free parts and labor warranty. The homeowners also wanted an updated warranty for the smoke detectors they paid for. These units will come with a 10 year worry free parts warranty and a 10 year sealed battery as well. Invoice for today will be emailed to the customer for quick access but they requested that this be mailed to them so they had a hardcopy on hand.

estimates.name: Water softener
estimates.summary:
A water softener can make a noticeable difference in your home, especially if you have hard water, which contains high levels of calcium and magnesium. It replaces or removes these minerals to reduce the problems they cause.
7 key benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale and mineral buildup
Helps prevent white, chalky deposits on faucets, showerheads, glass shower doors, sinks, and inside pipes.
2. Softer skin and smoother-feeling hair
Reduces mineral residue that can leave skin feeling dry or hair feeling rough. It may help soap rinse away more easily, although it won't treat underlying skin or scalp conditions.
3. Softer laundry
Clothes and towels may feel less stiff, colors can stay brighter, and less detergent is generally needed.
4. Cleaner dishes and glassware
Can reduce cloudy spots and mineral film on glasses, silverware, and dishes.
5. Helps protect plumbing and appliances
Reduces scale accumulation in water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and pipes, potentially improving efficiency and extending equipment life.
6. Less soap and detergent
Soft water allows soap to lather more readily, so you may use less laundry detergent, dish soap, shampoo, and body wash.
7. Easier household cleaning
Less time scrubbing mineral deposits from showers, tubs, sinks, and fixtures.

The water softener also gets rid of the chlorine in the water. Chlorine is a chemical and is unsafe to consume. It gets consumed whenever you shower, wash your hands, etc. 


This option does not include having electrical ran to the unit. If there is no outlet for the unit to plug-in further charges may apply. Technician may also have to open up some drywall.

estimates.name: Moen Flo
estimates.summary:
The Moen Flo Smart Water Monitor and Shutoff is a smart device installed on your home's main water line. Its biggest benefit is that it can detect unusual water use, alert you to potential leaks, and automatically shut off your home's water to help prevent expensive flooding.  
1. Helps prevent catastrophic water damage
If a pipe bursts, a toilet supply line fails, or an appliance hose leaks, Flo can detect abnormal water flow and automatically shut off the main water supply. This may prevent thousands of dollars in damage.
2. Detects small hidden leaks
Its daily MicroLeak tests can identify leaks as small as approximately one drop per minute, helping uncover problems in plumbing that you might not otherwise notice.
3. Protects your home while you're away
Receive alerts on your phone when unusual water use or potential leaks are detected. This is especially valuable on vacation, at a second home, or when you're away at work.
4. Monitors water consumption
Track water usage, flow rate, and pressure. This can help you spot running toilets, unexpected water consumption, or other potential plumbing problems.
5. Lets you shut off water remotely
You can turn off your home's water from the app if you suspect a problem or want to shut it off while away, without needing to be physically at the valve.
6. May reduce insurance costs
Some insurers offer discounts for approved automatic water shutoff devices. Eligibility and savings depend on your insurance company, so check before purchasing.

This option does not include having electrical ran to the unit. If there is no where to plug into further charges may apply. Technician may also have to open up drywall.

invoices.summary:
Today, I completed the annual electrical system inspection. Upon evaluation, I found the main electrical panel to be in excellent condition, with no signs of rust or corrosion. All electrical connections were verified to be tight, no signs of overheating were observed, and voltage readings were confirmed to be within acceptable ranges.

However, I did note that the main panel is not equipped with a whole-home surge protection device. This device is important for protecting the home’s electrical equipment and appliances from voltage surges.

I also observed that the exterior service entrance wiring is in very poor condition. This is common with wiring that has been exposed to direct sunlight for many years, as prolonged UV exposure can cause the outer insulation to deteriorate and crack. Once the insulation is compromised, moisture can enter and travel into the electrical panel, potentially causing rust and corrosion to the connections and resulting in more extensive and costly repairs.

I discussed these findings with the customer and explained that, given the condition of the existing meter base and service components, replacing only the wiring between the panel and the meter would still require an inspection and coordination with the utility company to disconnect and restore power. Therefore, I recommended replacing the entire service to address the existing issues and avoid additional labor and potential future repairs.

The recommended service replacement would include new service entrance wiring, PVC conduit to provide additional protection and extend the life of the wiring, a new meter base, and a slip riser.

The invoice and estimate were emailed to the customer for review.

invoices.summary:
The homeowner reported sewer gas odors and poor flushing performance from the third-floor hallway bathroom toilet. The bathroom is not used regularly. Upon inspection, the technician found that the water level in the toilet tank was too low to provide sufficient water for a proper flush. The technician adjusted the fill valve float to raise the water level in the tank. After the adjustment, the toilet was tested and is now flushing properly.

The technician also explained that infrequently used plumbing fixtures can develop sewer gas odors when the water in the P-traps evaporates, allowing odors from the drainage system to enter the home. To help prevent this issue, the technician recommended running the water in the bathroom sink and bathtub and flushing the toilet at least once a month. This will help maintain the water seals in the P-traps and reduce the likelihood of sewer gas odors.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

invoices.summary:
We were called out to evaluate Robert issue with his bathroom GFI on the first floor, constantly tripping and not being able to be reset. Robert also showed us, some other locations that were affected. We started our thorough evaluation at the main electrical panel to identify if this was a power supply issue or if it was an issue with the circuit that this GFI was protecting. We were able to identify that the power supply for the GFI was in really good shape and not the issue. We were able to identify one of the exterior outlets are a part of this circuit. This exterior plug contained two cords actively used at this receptacle. We unplugged both of these cords, reset the GFI, and identified that the system was functioning correctly. While the system was still on, we then re-plugged in the cords back into the exterior outlet and noticed that this GFI tripped again with the gazebo ceiling fan cord. Upon further inspection of this cord, we noticed that the ceiling fan cord was plugged into another extension cord, which had water stuck in between the plug joint. Once we unplugged this plug joint, the GFI was able to reset and functioning. We informed and showed Robert the main culprit of his issue and provided an option to install receptacle underneath the gazebo roof where the ceiling fan cord can plug into without having this issue. We also identified the exterior receptacle has seen some signs of weather and should be replaced as preventative maintenance.

Prior to leaving, Robert had another question with his bathroom lighting that would be delayed when turning on. We did a thorough evaluation and some research, coming to the conclusion that the quality of the bulbs should be where we start and then build on from there. We recommend high-quality Phillips LED lightbulbs to replace the existing mid grade supply house bulbs, that were existing. 

Robert opted to have the solutions provided for the gazebo emailed for his record and to review. We collected the dispatch fee for today’s troubleshooting and diagnostics. We thank you for trusting LPH and we look forward to servicing in the future.

invoices.summary:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, no immediate concerns/questions were reported prior to our electrical inspection. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel. 

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was identifying the majority of the smoke detectors in the home were removed from the ceiling. We did identify existing carbon monoxide detectors that are up-to-date in the home. invoices.summary:
Electrical System Check Evaluation

LPH completed an electrical system check to evaluate the condition of the home’s electrical components, identify existing concerns, and provide recommendations for improving the safety, reliability, and overall condition of the electrical system.

During the evaluation, several areas of concern were identified, including the age and condition of the existing electrical service equipment, deficiencies in the home’s grounding and bonding system, and multiple interior electrical devices that have deteriorated due to overheating and electrical arcing.

1. Main Electrical Service and Panel

The existing electrical service is rated at 100 amps and is estimated to be up to 45 years old. The main electrical panel is a discontinued model, and the exterior meter base exhibits extensive rust and corrosion affecting both the exterior and interior of the equipment. The existing exterior service cables are also aged and dry-rotted. This type of cable is known to allow moisture intrusion through deterioration of its outer jacket, potentially compromising the conductors inside.

Given the age and condition of these components, LPH recommends a complete upgrade to a new 200-amp electrical service. This would replace the existing service equipment and wiring with new components, including a meter base, exterior emergency disconnect, service cables, PVC conduit, and service head. The upgrade would also include a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel with all new breakers and premium whole-home surge protection.

The existing equipment has reached a stage in its service life where continued reliance on these components raises concerns regarding long-term reliability, moisture intrusion, and potential electrical connection failures. Replacing the service would address these concerns while providing additional electrical capacity for the home’s future needs.

2. Grounding and Bonding System

The existing grounding arrangement is improper and currently relies on a connection to a water pipe above the electrical panel, with a separate small jumper to the meter. LPH recommends correcting the grounding and bonding system to meet applicable electrical code requirements.

A separate estimate has been provided for these grounding improvements, including installing two new ground rods, establishing a continuous grounding connection to the home’s incoming water service piping, and properly bonding the gas piping system.

Please note that the complete grounding and bonding improvements are already included as part of the proposed 200-amp electrical service upgrade. If the homeowners elect to proceed with the complete service replacement, the separate grounding estimate would not need to be completed as an additional project.

3. Deteriorated Receptacles and Basement Light Switch

During the evaluation, three receptacles were identified as deteriorated and damaged, with signs of loosening and overheating associated with excessive electrical loads. These conditions can compromise the electrical connections and increase the potential for continued overheating, electrical arcing, and further device damage.

Additionally, the switch controlling the basement lighting has deteriorated and produces electrical arcing when switched on and off.

LPH recommends replacing all three affected receptacles and the deteriorated basement light switch. Accessible wiring and connections should also be inspected during replacement for any additional signs of heat damage or deterioration that may require repair.

Addressing these issues will help restore reliable operation and reduce the risks associated with continued use of damaged electrical devices.

4. Proposed 60-Amp Electrical Feed to the Garage for a Tesla Supercharger

The current tenant also expressed interest in installing a new electrical feed to the garage to accommodate a Tesla Supercharger and indicated that he may be interested in covering the cost of the project.

At the tenant’s request and based on the proposed installation, LPH prepared a separate estimate for a new 60-amp electrical feed extending from the home’s main panel to the detached garage. The proposed installation includes the necessary exterior conduit, service head and point of attachment, overhead triplex cable, garage riser, interior feeder wiring, a new 60-amp disconnect, and wiring extending to the designated charger location.

This project is contingent on completing the proposed 200-amp electrical service upgrade. The existing 100-amp service would need to be upgraded before proceeding with the proposed installation, subject to verification of the available service capacity and the final electrical requirements of the charging equipment.

5. Estimates and Property Owner Authorization

The proposed 200-amp service upgrade and the new electrical feed to the garage were discussed after the current tenant expressed interest in having this work completed and potentially paying for the projects himself with permission from the property owners.

LPH prepared these estimates to provide the property owners with clear pricing and an understanding of the proposed work. The estimates are being provided for the homeowners’ review and consideration, and the decision to proceed with any of the proposed improvements, regardless of whether the tenant offers to cover the costs, is entirely at the property owners’ discretion.

Although the tenant initiated the discussion regarding the service upgrade and garage feed, LPH independently recommends the complete 200-amp service upgrade due to the age, deterioration, and overall condition of the existing electrical service components. This recommendation is based on the findings of the electrical evaluation, not solely on the proposed Tesla charging installation.

The separate grounding estimate is available for consideration if the homeowners choose not to proceed with the complete service upgrade. However, the grounding improvements are already included in the full 200-amp service replacement estimate.

Conclusion

LPH has provided separate estimates outlining the recommended repairs and potential upgrades identified during the electrical system check. These options include replacing the deteriorated receptacles and basement light switch, correcting the grounding and bonding system, upgrading the existing 100-amp service to 200 amps, and installing a new 60-amp electrical feed to the garage for the proposed Tesla Supercharger.

The service upgrade is the primary recommendation due to the age and deteriorated condition of the existing service equipment and wiring. The remaining options have been presented to give the property owners a clear understanding of the identified concerns, available improvements, and associated costs.

LPH will email all estimates and the completed electrical evaluation to the property owners for their review and consideration.

Thank you for allowing LPH the opportunity to evaluate the home’s electrical system and provide these recommendations.

estimates.name: Complete 200-Amp Electrical Service Upgrade
estimates.summary:
Complete 200-Amp Electrical Service Upgrade

LPH recommends upgrading the existing 100-amp electrical service to a new 200-amp service to replace the home’s severely aging electrical equipment and bring the service and grounding system up to current applicable electrical code requirements.

The existing electrical service is estimated to be up to 45 years old. The main electrical panel is a discontinued model, the exterior meter base is heavily rusted and corroded, and the existing service cables show signs of significant age and deterioration. The current service equipment and wiring have reached a stage where continued reliance on the existing components presents increasing concerns regarding long-term reliability, moisture intrusion, and the potential for electrical connection failures.

Scope of Work

1. New 200-Amp Electrical Service

* Upgrade the existing 100-amp service to a complete 200-amp electrical service.
* Install a new meter base to replace the existing rusted and discontinued equipment.
* Install a new exterior emergency disconnect to provide an accessible means of disconnecting power to the home during an emergency.
* Replace the existing upper and lower service cable runs, including the wiring from the utility connection to the meter, from the meter to the exterior disconnect, and from the disconnect into the home.
* Protect the exterior service wiring in PVC conduit from the service entrance through the exterior wall, including a new PVC service head and the necessary conduit fittings and connections.

2. New Main Electrical Panel

* Install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel to replace the existing discontinued panel.
* Install all new circuit breakers compatible with the new panel.
* Transfer and reconnect the existing branch circuits to the new panel, as appropriate for the existing wiring and circuit conditions.
* Properly terminate and organize the wiring within the new enclosure.
* Install premium whole-home surge protection to help protect sensitive electronics, appliances, and other connected equipment from damaging voltage surges caused by utility disturbances, lightning-related events, and electrical switching within the home.

3. Complete Grounding and Bonding Improvements

* Install two new grounding electrodes in the form of ground rods to establish a proper grounding electrode system.
* Upgrade the existing grounding connections to the home’s water piping in the basement, including a new continuous grounding conductor routed to the meter and connected as required.
* Install the necessary bonding connections to the home’s gas piping to meet applicable electrical code requirements.
* Install a new exterior bonding bridge to properly connect the required service bonding components.

4. Service Coordination and Code Compliance

* Coordinate the service replacement with the utility company as required.
* Complete the necessary service installation, grounding, bonding, and labeling.
* Arrange applicable permits and inspections as required for the project.

Why LPH Recommends This Upgrade

The existing service has several age-related concerns that make replacement a worthwhile investment in the home’s electrical safety and long-term reliability.

The exterior service cables are old and dry-rotted. This style of cable is known to allow moisture to enter through deterioration of the outer jacket, potentially damaging the conductors and compromising the integrity of the service. Replacing these cables eliminates the need to continue relying on deteriorated wiring.

The existing meter base is a discontinued model with extensive exterior rust and corrosion that has also affected the interior. This deterioration raises concerns about the integrity of the electrical connections and the equipment’s ability to remain reliable over time. Replacing the meter base and associated service equipment addresses these concerns as part of a complete upgrade.

The existing main panel is also a discontinued model that has been in service for decades. Given its age and the condition of the surrounding service equipment, continued use carries increasing uncertainty regarding long-term reliability and replacement-part availability. A new Eaton CH panel provides modern circuit protection, additional circuit spaces, and a new foundation for the home’s electrical distribution system.

Finally, the home’s existing grounding arrangement is inadequate for a modern service installation. The current system relies on a connection to a water pipe above the panel, with a separate small jumper to the meter. LPH will install a properly configured grounding electrode system and correct the grounding and bonding connections to provide a more complete, code-compliant path for electrical faults and help ensure the service equipment and required metallic piping are properly bonded.

The Benefit to the Homeowner: This upgrade replaces aging, deteriorated, and discontinued equipment with a new 200-amp service, modern circuit protection, whole-home surge protection, and an improved grounding and bonding system. It also provides additional electrical capacity for future needs while addressing the existing service’s most significant reliability and safety concerns.

All work will be completed in accordance with applicable electrical codes and permitting requirements. Final installation details will be determined by existing site conditions, utility requirements, and the applicable inspection authority.

estimates.name: Replace Deteriorated Devices
estimates.summary:
Replacement of Deteriorated Receptacles, Light Switch, and Smoke Detector

LPH recommends replacing three deteriorated receptacles, one basement light switch, one kitchen countertop GFCI receptacle, and one expired smoke detector to address existing electrical safety concerns and restore reliable operation.

Scope of Work

1. Replacement of Three Deteriorated Receptacles

LPH will remove and replace three receptacles that have sustained damage and become loose due to overheating associated with excessive electrical loads. These conditions can compromise the integrity of the electrical connections and increase the risk of continued overheating, electrical arcing, and potential damage to the surrounding devices.

2. Replacement of Basement Light Switch

LPH will remove and replace the deteriorated switch controlling the basement lighting. The existing switch produces electrical arcing when operated, indicating deterioration that warrants replacement. Installing a new switch will address the damaged device and help restore reliable control of the basement lighting.

3. Installation of Kitchen Countertop GFCI Receptacle

LPH will replace the existing kitchen countertop receptacle with a new GFCI-protected receptacle. GFCI protection is designed to help protect against electrical shock by quickly interrupting power when a ground fault is detected. Kitchen countertop receptacles are particularly important locations for this protection due to their proximity to sinks, water, and commonly used appliances.

4. Replacement of Expired Front Bedroom Smoke Detector

LPH will remove and replace the expired smoke detector located in the front bedroom. The existing detector has also accumulated excessive dust, which can interfere with proper operation and contribute to nuisance alarms or reduced detection performance. Installing a new smoke detector will provide updated fire detection protection and help maintain an effective early warning system for the home.

LPH will inspect the accessible wiring and connections at the affected electrical devices during replacement for any visible signs of overheating, damaged insulation, or additional deterioration that may require further attention.

Why This Work Is Recommended

Electrical devices that have deteriorated due to overheating or produce electrical arcing should not be left in service. Continued use can lead to further connection damage, electrical failures, and increased fire risk.

Adding GFCI protection at the kitchen countertop helps reduce the risk of electrical shock in an area where water and electrical appliances are frequently used. Replacing the expired, dust-clogged smoke detector also helps maintain dependable fire detection and provides the occupants with an appropriate early warning in the event of a fire.

LPH recommends completing these replacements to address the identified concerns, improve electrical safety, and maintain reliable operation of the home’s electrical devices and fire detection equipment.

estimates.summary:
Electrical Grounding and Bonding Upgrade

LPH recommends updating the home’s existing grounding and bonding system to address the deficiencies identified during the electrical evaluation and bring the installation into compliance with applicable electrical code requirements.

The current grounding arrangement relies on a connection to a water pipe above the main electrical panel, with a separate small jumper running to the meter. This setup does not provide the properly configured grounding and bonding system needed for a modern electrical installation.

Scope of Work

* Installation of Two New Ground Rods: LPH will drill through the basement concrete foundation as necessary to route the grounding conductors to the exterior and install two new grounding electrodes (ground rods) to establish a proper grounding electrode system.
* Proper Water Main Grounding: LPH will install a new, continuous grounding conductor to the home’s incoming metal water service piping, establishing the required grounding connection without relying on the existing improper arrangement.
* Gas Piping Bonding: LPH will install the necessary bonding conductor and connections to bond the home’s gas piping system in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements.
* Grounding and Bonding Connections: LPH will properly connect and secure the new grounding and bonding components to establish a coordinated grounding system for the home’s electrical service.

Why This Upgrade Is Recommended

A properly installed grounding and bonding system is an essential part of a home’s electrical safety. It helps provide a low-impedance path for electrical fault current, allowing protective devices to operate as intended, while bonding helps reduce dangerous voltage differences between interconnected metallic systems.

The existing grounding arrangement is inadequate for a modern electrical installation and should be corrected rather than continuing to rely on an isolated connection to a water pipe above the panel. Installing two new ground rods, correcting the water service grounding, and properly bonding the gas piping will provide a more complete and reliable grounding and bonding system.

LPH recommends completing these improvements to address the existing deficiencies and bring the home’s grounding and bonding system into compliance with applicable electrical code requirements.

invoices.summary:
LPH responded to the home to investigate reported brownout issues and fluctuations in electrical power. We performed an in-depth evaluation of the electrical system, including the incoming service at the meter and all connections and components within the main electrical panel.

Multiple load tests were performed throughout the home. We cycled power on and off and operated various electrical devices and appliances to intentionally increase and vary the electrical demand on the system. This testing was performed to help identify any potential loose neutral connections, voltage instability, or other electrical issues that could be contributing to the reported brownouts.

All testing performed came back clean. Throughout our evaluation, the electrical system remained stable, with no abnormalities identified at the meter, service connections, or main panel. We were unable to reproduce the reported issue during our visit.

After reviewing the test results and discussing the history of the problem with the homeowner, our suspicion is that the issue may be originating upstream of the home’s electrical service, potentially involving the utility transformer or shared distribution lines supplying other properties. An issue affecting another service connected to the same transformer could potentially contribute to voltage fluctuations at this home, even when the homeowner’s own service wiring and electrical equipment are functioning properly.

Recommended Next Steps:

We recommend contacting PPL again and requesting that they install a temporary power-quality monitoring device on the home’s incoming service for approximately one week. This extended monitoring period will allow the utility to track voltage conditions over time and capture any intermittent fluctuations that may not be present during a scheduled service visit.

This is the best next step to help determine whether the issue is originating on the utility’s side of the service, including a potential problem with the transformer or shared distribution equipment, rather than within the home’s electrical system.

At this time, LPH did not identify any electrical deficiencies during our testing that would explain the reported brownout conditions. The electrical system was stable throughout our evaluation.

Whole-Home Surge Protection:

Separately from the brownout investigation, LPH installed whole-home surge protection to provide an additional layer of protection for the home’s electrical system and connected electronics and appliances. We discussed with the homeowner that while this upgrade helps protect against damaging voltage spikes and transient surges, it will not correct or resolve the current brownout symptoms or underlying voltage fluctuations being experienced. The homeowner understands that the surge protection is a preventative upgrade and that further investigation through PPL is still necessary to identify the source of the reported issue.

At this time, LPH did not identify any electrical deficiencies during our testing that would explain the reported brownout conditions. The electrical system remained stable throughout our evaluation.

Today’s invoice summary will be emailed to the homeowner for their records. Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure working with you, and we look forward to assisting you with any future electrical needs.

estimates.name: Whole Home Surge Protection
estimates.summary:
Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Smoke Detector Evaluation – Reported Overnight Alarms

LPH responded to the home after the homeowners reported smoke alarms sounding unexpectedly in the middle of the night. Upon arrival, LPH inspected the existing smoke detectors for signs of electrical faults, excessive dust, or other conditions that could contribute to nuisance alarms and indicate a need for cleaning. No visible issues of this nature were identified during today’s evaluation.

During the inspection, LPH did discover some loose wire-nut connections where the smoke detector pigtail wiring was connected. However, testing confirmed that all smoke detectors were receiving proper AC voltage at the time of our visit.

The existing smoke detectors are Kidde brand units, which have been associated with nuisance alarms in some installations. Although no definitive cause for the reported alarms could be confirmed during today’s evaluation, LPH cannot guarantee that the existing detectors will not experience the same issue again.

LPH’s Recommended Solution

To address the homeowners’ concerns and provide greater peace of mind, LPH will warranty the existing smoke detector installation by replacing the current units with three new First Alert hardwired smoke detectors featuring 10-year lithium battery backup, along with three matching First Alert combination smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. These replacements will provide updated detection equipment while helping reduce the likelihood of continued nuisance alarms.

Unfortunately, our electrical supplier is closed today, preventing us from obtaining the replacement detectors during this visit. LPH will return as soon as the necessary equipment can be obtained to complete the replacement.

Today’s evaluation summary will be emailed to the homeowners for their records. LPH will also be in contact to coordinate a return visit and schedule the installation at a convenient time.

I was out today to discuss the cost and options for replacing the homeowner’s current heating and cooling system. After speaking with the homeowner and evaluating the existing setup, I found that the home currently has a SpacePak system for cooling and an Aqua Coil boiler system for heating.

After taking measurements and performing a scan of the home, we discussed the homeowner’s interest in eliminating the existing Aqua Coil boiler setup and upgrading to a new Unico high-velocity heat pump system that would provide both heating and cooling.

We went over the scope of work in detail, which would include removing the existing equipment, replacing the current ductwork, and installing a completely new Unico heat pump system. The project is estimated to take approximately two days to complete.

After reviewing the proposed installation and discussing everything involved, the homeowner requested a couple of days to consider the option before making a final decision. She will reach out once she has decided how she would like to proceed.

I left my business card with my contact information. If you have any questions or concerns in the meantime, please don’t hesitate to call or text me.

Plumbing; main sewer line cleaning requested after a backup occurred. House built in 1985, line has never been cleaned.

Today, Monday, October 26, 2026 (all day slot offered and accepted).

invoices.summary:
Upon arrival, tech met with Randy. He stated they had a backup this past Saturday. He rented a cable machine from bombergers and was able to restore flow. They were still experiencing some gurgling from the downstairs toilet but that stopped as well. We checked the cleanout near the tank but couldn’t see any buildup. Tech had randy flush a toilet to see if we could hear or see the flush. We did not. Randy then ran a hose through the inside cleanout while tech watched at the septic tank. Tech had no water come down to the tank. The hose got stuck in the pipe. Tech was able to retrieve the hose for Randy. Tech observed a fernco from the kitchen branch line connecting onto a broken sanitary tee on the stack as well. With Randy’s approval, we performed a video inspection from the inside cleanout going towards the tank. We came across water being held throughout most of the line. Randy called his septic company to see if they have availability to pump out the tank. Tech then performed a video inspection from the outside cleanout at the tank and came across buildup.  Tech pushed his camera and released the buildup and the water came flowing down. We inspected going back towards the house and there was some water still being held. Randy is going to have the tank pumped then call us back for another video inspection. Tech presented a solution for the broken tee connection. Randy does not want to move forward at this time. He will give us a call in a few weeks when they are ready to move forward. Thanks for trusting Lancaster plumbing and heating. 

This is to attempt to perform a video inspection of the main line.

invoices.summary: Technician arrived and found a fitting that had come undone underneath the modular home. The technician attempted to re-prime and glue the fitting; however, due to the tight positioning of the piping, the fitting continued to pop out and could not be properly secured. Upon further inspection, the technician discovered that the kitchen branch line is completely back-pitched, with sections of piping running up and down. Since the drainage system relies on gravity, the improper pitch prevents wastewater from flowing properly. This issue will continue to recur until the piping is corrected. The homeowner stated that they have snaked the line multiple times in the past, which temporarily resolved the issue. The technician provided options to snake the kitchen branch line or re-pipe the line to correct the improper pitch and address the underlying issue. The homeowner stated that the pricing was too high. Thank you for trusting LPH with your plumbing needs!

Upon arrival, tech met with John. He was rerouting his rain gutter through the driveway out to his back yard per the city. He has tried to snake it but hasn’t had success. Tech had him flush a toilet while checking the house trap. Tech was unable to hear or see the flush. invoices.summary:
Second-Floor Hallway Bathroom – Customer-Supplied Tub/Shower Installation

LPH will install a customer-supplied bathtub and shower surround, along with a new tub/shower valve, in the second-floor hallway bathroom. Technician will shut off the water supply to the home to safely remove the existing tub/shower valve and modify the existing water lines as needed to accommodate the new valve installation. An access opening will be required behind the tub/shower area to provide access for removal of the existing valve and installation of the new tub/shower valve.

Technician will modify the existing duct return in the bathtub area as needed to allow the new bathtub and surround to fit properly. Technician will also remove the existing brass waste and overflow assembly and replace it with a new PVC waste and overflow assembly.

Once the necessary plumbing modifications are complete, technician will apply mortar beneath the bathtub to provide proper support and stability before setting the new bathtub and installing the customer-supplied shower surround. All plumbing connections will be checked upon completion, and the tub/shower system will be tested for leaks to verify proper operation.


Third-Floor Master Bathroom – Customer-Supplied Shower Stall Installation

LPH will install a customer-supplied shower stall and a new shower valve in the third-floor master bathroom. Technician will shut off the water supply to the home to safely remove the existing shower valve and prepare the plumbing for the new installation. An access opening will be required behind the shower area to allow for removal of the existing valve and installation of the new shower valve.

Technician will relocate the existing shower drain as needed to accommodate the new shower stall. This will require opening the subfloor from above to access and modify the drain piping. After the drain relocation is complete, technician will patch the subfloor as needed to prepare the area for installation of the new shower stall.

Technician will apply mortar beneath the shower stall to provide additional support and stability before setting the customer-supplied shower stall. Upon completion, technician will inspect the accessible plumbing connections and test the new shower valve and drain for proper operation and leaks.

LPH is not responsible for drywall repair or finishing associated with access openings required to complete the plumbing work. Any necessary drywall repair, taping, mudding, sanding, texturing, or painting will be the responsibility of others.

Technician will have to return to replace the chrome waste and overflow trim to bras finish trim as well as add an access panel.

invoices.summary:
Second-Floor Hallway Bathroom – Customer-Supplied Tub/Shower Installation

LPH will install a customer-supplied bathtub and shower surround, along with a new tub/shower valve, in the second-floor hallway bathroom. Technician will shut off the water supply to the home to safely remove the existing tub/shower valve and modify the existing water lines as needed to accommodate the new valve installation. An access opening will be required behind the tub/shower area to provide access for removal of the existing valve and installation of the new tub/shower valve.

Technician will modify the existing duct return in the bathtub area as needed to allow the new bathtub and surround to fit properly. Technician will also remove the existing brass waste and overflow assembly and replace it with a new PVC waste and overflow assembly.

Once the necessary plumbing modifications are complete, technician will apply mortar beneath the bathtub to provide proper support and stability before setting the new bathtub and installing the customer-supplied shower surround. All plumbing connections will be checked upon completion, and the tub/shower system will be tested for leaks to verify proper operation.


Third-Floor Master Bathroom – Customer-Supplied Shower Stall Installation

LPH will install a customer-supplied shower stall and a new shower valve in the third-floor master bathroom. Technician will shut off the water supply to the home to safely remove the existing shower valve and prepare the plumbing for the new installation. An access opening will be required behind the shower area to allow for removal of the existing valve and installation of the new shower valve.

Technician will relocate the existing shower drain as needed to accommodate the new shower stall. This will require opening the subfloor from above to access and modify the drain piping. After the drain relocation is complete, technician will patch the subfloor as needed to prepare the area for installation of the new shower stall.

Technician will apply mortar beneath the shower stall to provide additional support and stability before setting the customer-supplied shower stall. Upon completion, technician will inspect the accessible plumbing connections and test the new shower valve and drain for proper operation and leaks.

LPH is not responsible for drywall repair or finishing associated with access openings required to complete the plumbing work. Any necessary drywall repair, taping, mudding, sanding, texturing, or painting will be the responsibility of others.

invoices.summary:
This morning I arrived at the Savvy family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies. The main breaker panel, as well as the external meterbase have been replaced within the last ten years and show no signs of failure, deterioration, and or burning, arcing, or corrosion. I did notice that the panel, while in good condition is almost entirely unlabeled. Labeling is of utmost importance when it comes to breaker panels. If a panel is unlabeled, it will prove very difficult to turn off a system in case of emergency, or for general maintenance. I have provided an estimate to perform a full labeling of the panel, consisting of a full scale analysis of the all circuits in the home. We will trace and identify each breakers connected system and properly and professionally identify and level said breaker in the panel. 

LPH also noticed that the appliances in the home are missing active surge protection to defend against any spike of voltage that can enter/be produced inside of the home and potentially damage motherboards or other electrical components inside appliances. A whole home surge protection device that gets mounted and connected at the panel will help defend against these harmful spikes of voltage. The device installed will come with lifetime parts warranty and up to $100,000 of repair or replacement (whichever is less) of coverage in the event that a grounded appliance or piece of equipment that are commonly found within a home such as A/C, Furnace, other home intergraded heating system (boilers and water heaters), water purification system, range, microwave, refrigerator, and etc.) becomes damaged due to a surge with this device installed. *Whole home surge protection device is NOT a power conditioner, meaning that the home surge device will not eliminate the minor flickering for bulbs entirely but will alleviate most of the major/noticeable flickering/strobing*. I have provided an option to install one of these devices in the home.

Lastly,  I provided two estimates to meet code compliance and safety standards in the home, consisting of a new combination smoke detector in the basement as the current is expired, and installing 1 junction box to contain an open splice on the basements lighting circuit.

If you have any questions, or if you would like to move forward with any of these options, please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you for having me out today and I look forward to our next visit!

invoices.summary:
LPH completed an electrical system check to evaluate the overall condition, safety, and operation of the home’s electrical system. During the evaluation, we inspected the electrical panel, breakers, and accessible electrical connections for signs of deterioration, overheating, corrosion, or other visible concerns. We also checked the operation and condition of the home’s switches and receptacles, tested GFCI protection where applicable, and evaluated the accessible electrical devices for proper operation and signs of wear.

During the inspection, we found that a portion of the first-floor devices and all devices on the second floor were wired using the back-stab method, where the wiring is pushed into the back of the device rather than secured under the side terminal screws. This connection method is known to be more susceptible to loosening and deterioration over time. We tested several devices in each room, and the connections we checked were holding up well, with no loose connections identified during our inspection. Although no immediate issues were found with the sampled devices, we discussed the long-term reliability concerns associated with back-stabbed connections and the option of proactively replacing these devices to help reduce the likelihood of future connection problems.

LPH also identified a worn 3-way switch in the dining area that exhibited some looseness in its upper position and light arcing during operation. We recommend replacing this switch to address the internal wear and reduce the risk of further deterioration or excessive heat buildup.

Additionally, two exterior receptacles, located at the front and back of the home, were found to be non-weather-rated devices. Although they have GFCI protection and appropriate bubble covers, prolonged exposure to moisture and humidity has contributed to oxidation of the internal metal contacts. A garage receptacle was also found to have rough plug insertion, with visible oxidation and pitting on the internal contacts. These deteriorated contact surfaces can increase electrical resistance and potentially contribute to excessive heat buildup under load. We recommend replacing all three receptacles with appropriate new devices, including weather-rated receptacles for the exterior locations.

Recommended Estimates:

* Dining Area 3-Way Switch Replacement: Replace the worn switch to restore reliable operation and address the observed internal arcing.
* Exterior and Garage Receptacle Replacements: Replace two deteriorated exterior receptacles with weather-rated devices and replace the worn garage receptacle to address the oxidized and pitted contacts.
* Back-Stabbed Device Replacement: Provide an estimate to proactively replace the affected first- and second-floor switches and receptacles with new devices using more secure terminal connections.
* Whole-Home Surge Protection: Provide an estimate to install a whole-home surge protection device at the electrical panel. This upgrade helps protect sensitive electronics and appliances from damaging voltage surges caused by lightning, utility disturbances, and electrical equipment cycling on and off within the home.

The recommended repairs and upgrades were discussed as options to address the conditions identified during today’s inspection and improve the long-term reliability of the home’s electrical system. The estimates will be emailed to the homeowner for review, along with today’s electrical system check evaluation.

Thank you for choosing Lancaster Plumbing Heating (LPH). We appreciate the opportunity to inspect your home’s electrical system and provide recommendations to help keep it operating safely and reliably.

estimates.name: Devices Only
estimates.summary:
Dining Room 3-Way Switch Replacement

During the electrical system check, LPH identified a 3-way switch in the dining area that is beginning to show signs of wear. While testing the switch’s internal spring mechanism, we noticed some looseness when the switch was in the upper position, along with light arcing when operating the switch back and forth. These signs indicate that the internal components are beginning to wear. LPH recommends replacing this switch with a new 3-way switch to restore proper operation and reduce the risk of further deterioration or heat buildup from continued use.

Weather-Rated Receptacle Upgrades

LPH also inspected the exterior receptacles and identified two receptacles, one at the front of the home and one at the back, that are not weather-rated. Although both receptacles currently have GFCI protection and appropriate bubble covers, the internal metal contacts have gradually deteriorated from prolonged exposure to outdoor humidity and moisture. This has resulted in oxidation and rough contact surfaces when plugging in electrical devices.

Oxidized or pitted contact surfaces can increase electrical resistance, potentially leading to excessive heat buildup when the receptacles are under load. While the existing GFCI protection helps protect against electrical shock, it does not prevent overheating caused by deteriorated electrical contacts. LPH recommends replacing both exterior receptacles with weather-rated devices designed to better withstand outdoor conditions.

Additionally, LPH identified a garage receptacle showing similar deterioration. The receptacle was noticeably rough when inserting a plug, and an inspection of the internal contacts with a light revealed visible pitting and oxidation along the metal contact surfaces. Due to the condition of these contacts and the potential for increased resistance and heat buildup, LPH recommends replacing this receptacle as well.

Recommended Repairs:

* Replace one worn 3-way switch in the dining area.
* Replace two exterior receptacles with weather-rated devices at the front and back of the home.
* Replace one deteriorated garage receptacle with a new device.

These recommended repairs will address the identified wear and deterioration, improve the reliability of the affected devices, and help reduce the risk of electrical overheating associated with worn or oxidized contacts.

* Replace one deteriorated garage receptacle with a new device.

These recommended repairs will address the identified wear and deterioration, improve the reliability of the affected devices, and help reduce the risk of electrical overheating associated with worn or oxidized contacts.

Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Weather-Rated Receptacle Upgrades

LPH also inspected the exterior receptacles and identified two receptacles, one at the front of the home and one at the back, that are not weather-rated. Although both receptacles currently have GFCI protection and appropriate bubble covers, the internal metal contacts have gradually deteriorated from prolonged exposure to outdoor humidity and moisture. This has resulted in oxidation and rough contact surfaces when plugging in electrical devices.

Oxidized or pitted contact surfaces can increase electrical resistance, potentially leading to excessive heat buildup when the receptacles are under load. While the existing GFCI protection helps protect against electrical shock, it does not prevent overheating caused by deteriorated electrical contacts. LPH recommends replacing both exterior receptacles with weather-rated devices designed to better withstand outdoor conditions.

Additionally, LPH identified a garage receptacle showing similar deterioration. The receptacle was noticeably rough when inserting a plug, and an inspection of the internal contacts with a light revealed visible pitting and oxidation along the metal contact surfaces. Due to the condition of these contacts and the potential for increased resistance and heat buildup, LPH recommends replacing this receptacle as well.
