invoices.summary: I arrived today for the system not heating. I verified that the thermostat was calling for heat. I went to the furnace and the fan was running because it was set to fan on. I found that the furnace was locked out. I reset it from the code. We completed a heating check less than a month ago. When the furnace kicked on it went through its sequence and the igniter lit but no main gas valve. I found that the gas valve was not getting voltage. I traced the wiring and found that the one pressure switch was not closing. I found that the main system trap was clogged and the pressure switch tubing was clogged. I cleared the drain and the tubbing. I restarted the system and i was now getting proper voltage to the gas valve. I tested the inlet and outlet gas pressures and they were good. The system lit and was making heat. The systems is now operating properly. I did notice that the air scrubber bulb is older than 2 years and I gave her an option to change it. She respectfully declined.

invoices.summary:
Out to home today for the yearly plumbing system check. Upon arrival to home, there was one major concern. The toilet in the hall bathroom has been giving issues for months at this point. Homeowner states that the toilet doesn’t flush very well and has had it serviced several times. Homeowner believes there may be a clog outside causing the issue. Ran other fixtures inside the home to test for proper flow. Ran tub and sink at the same time and check outside. Heard and visibly saw water flowing from the outside cleanout. At this point, LPH had confirmed that there were no issues currently with the main sewer line. Attempted to plunge and then augured toilet and was able to restore proper flow and operation with the toilet. With how often the toilet has been clogging, evaluated potential causes of poor flushing from toilet. Identified that the toilet has an older style 2” flapper and only a 1.28 gallon flush providing an extremely weak and inefficient flush capability. Suggested installing a modern toilet with a standard 1.6 gallon flush using the new 3” style flush mechanism. Went over costs and scheduled to return tomorrow to perform install. Collected a 30% deposit for work to be completed. Remainder of cost will be collected upon completion of the service. 

From there, performed the full home plumbing inspection today. Tested water quality inside the home to verify the water treatment is working properly. Tested water pressure inside the home to verify safe operating pressure throughout the plumbing system. Tested hot water temperature to very mixer valve is working properly feeding off the boiler system. 

No other concerns were found during today’s visit. Thank you for trusting LPH.

invoices.summary:
Technician found error code 71 displayed on the control panel of the existing Rinnai CX199i tankless water heater. Technician removed the unit’s cover and discovered corrosion around the bypass tee. Technician cleaned the flame rods on the heat exchanger and restarted the tankless water heater; however, error code 71 remained displayed.

Technician contacted Rinnai technical support and worked through the diagnostic process to evaluate the unit’s control board and error code history. The recorded error history showed the following codes: 1-11, 2-11, 3-72, 4-72, 5-71, and 6-71. Following the diagnostic procedure, error code 71 did not return.

According to Rinnai technical support, error code 71 indicates a solenoid valve circuit failure or a potential control board failure. Moisture inside the unit can sometimes contribute to these issues. During further inspection of the bypass tee, technician identified that the water leak was originating from the elbow connected to the heat exchanger.

Rinnai technical support will ship a replacement heat exchanger, bypass tee, and new O-rings to Lancaster Plumbing and Heating (LPH). Once the replacement materials arrive, LPH will contact the owner to schedule a follow-up appointment to replace the affected components and address the leak.

Technician is also going to provide a solution for adding commercial grade water treatment to the water distribution system. Technician is waiting on pricing.

When the water overflows, it pools on the patio and can form an ice hazard in the winter time. The homeowner is concerned there may be an issue with the pump system and is looking a 2nd opinion. Homeowner stated the original contractors had came out once or twice and identified pooling water to be caused from ground water. Upon taking apart the well head, found the water table to be sitting about 2-3 feet below the top of the well head. Homeowner states that the well pump is set down about 340 feet. With how high the water table is, if there is any amount of rain the well will overflow. 

The solution for the high water table is to trench an overflow pipe from just above the pitless adapter to over by the pool where there is proper grade to relocate the water away from the patio. If homeowner would like a quote to have work done, our underground specialist can come out and provide direct pricing. 

From there, performed full home plumbing inspection of the house and barn unit. 

Tested water quality to the home to be soft and at the proper pH. Inspected both water heater systems and performed routine flush of both systems. During evaluation, found both units to be past the expected lifespan of 8-12 years. Suggested proactive replacement of both systems to maintain constant and reliable hot water inside the home. Lastly, verified water pressures in the home. Well systems are holding and maintaining pressure normally. 

Other concerns found during today’s visit include a leaking laundry valve and a malfunctioning UV system in the basement. One last note make is the far bathroom upstairs does not get enough use and is allowing the traps to dry out. When the traps dry out, sewer gases will back up into the home freely and will cause a poor smell. 

Sent over pricing for all recommendations found during inspection today. If there are any questions about anything that was found during the inspection, do not hesitate to reach out to our office. Pricing provided today is valid for 60 days. Thank you for trusting LPH.

materials.bookingNotes:
Purpose: 

Please provide Scott with the following message. 
I’ve been looking into alternatives for controlling my AprilAire Model 600 humidifier. My concern is that the existing duct-mounted humidity control is very close to where the warm, humidified bypass air from the Model 600 re-enters the return duct, so I’m not sure it is getting a representative reading of the humidity in the occupied part of the house.

Rather
than continuing to relocate the duct-mounted sensor, I’d like you to consider
controlling the Model 600 based on humidity measured in the living area.

A
few AprilAire options that appear worth considering:

•
AprilAire S86WMUPR Wi-Fi thermostat — combination HVAC thermostat and
IAQ/humidifier control. This could potentially replace my existing thermostat
and control the Model 600 directly.

•
AprilAire Z10IDT Wireless Indoor Temperature & Humidity Sensor — can be
located in the living area and communicate wirelessly with the compatible
S86WMUPR thermostat. This seems particularly attractive if we want the humidity
measurement taken in a representative living-space location without running
additional sensor wiring.

•
AprilAire Z10ODT Wireless Outdoor Temperature & Humidity Sensor — can also
be paired with the S86WMUPR and used for automatic humidity control based on
outdoor conditions, which could help reduce humidity automatically during very
cold weather and minimize window condensation.

•
AprilAire Model 65 Digital Humidistat — another possibility if we want to keep
my existing HVAC thermostat. It can be located in the living area and wired
back to the Model 600, although this would require wiring and would provide
manual rather than the same type of automatic outdoor-temperature compensation.

Could
you look at my existing thermostat wiring and the Model 600 installation and
let me know which approach you recommend?

My
preference would be, in order: (1) keep my existing thermostat and use a
wireless living-area humidity sensor if there is a compatible way to do that;
(2) replace the existing thermostat with the AprilAire S86WMUPR and use the
Z10IDT wireless indoor sensor; or (3) use the existing thermostat and run
wiring to a Model 65 living-area humidistat.

The
main objective is to have the Model 600 controlled by a humidity reading from a
representative occupied area of the house rather than from the return duct
immediately adjacent to the humidifier bypass connection.

invoices.summary: LPH completed annual electrical system check. During my evaluation I noticed the main panel was in good condition. All breaker screws were tightened and proper voltages were coming into the home. I also did not notice any rust or corrosion. The homeowner did have home surge protection at the main panel. This was brought up to customer and LPH explained what home surge protection does. Home Surge protection protections your home from any surges that may occur in the home. 20 percent of surges come from outside the home such as a surge from the power company or stray lighting strikes. The other 80 percent comes from your bigger appliances such as dryer, AC motors, or fridge compressors.The home had adequate GFI protection. GFI protection is like shock protection for the homeowner. The electrical system was properly bonded both gas and water systems were properly bonded. All switches were working properly and made no popping or cracking sounds. The outside meterbase was not in great shape the wire has a gash in it and is leaking water in the panel. Provided options for replacements.

invoices.summary: Out to home today for a slow / clogged drain in the kitchen. Whenever they run water in the upstairs sinks or in the kitchen, water backs up in the kitchen sink. Upon evaluation, determined that the blockage needs to be removed by machine. Offered pricing for drain cleaning services today. With homeowner approval, brought in drain equipment and disconnected plumbing under sink. Ran drain machine through line about 40 feet over to main drain. Pulled back hair and grease buildup. Upon completion of drain cleaning, assembled drain piping and tested for leaks. Once no leaks were determined, filled sink several times to verify drain is working properly. After three basins of water, confirmed sink to be draining normally at this time. With a garbage disposal, advised homeowner to run the water a while after running the disposal to flush debris properly down the drain. When the debris sits in the piping, it can solidify and buildup with time. While onsite today, also signed home up for our partnership plan. Drain cleaning is guaranteed for 30 days. Thank you for trusting LPH.

estimates.name: Tankless Water Heater Install
estimates.summary:
Provide and install one (1) Rinnai Sensei Series 9.8 GPM condensing tankless water heater with integrated recirculation pump. The system features Rinnai Smart-Circ™ Intelligent Recirculation technology, which learns household hot water usage patterns over a seven-day period and automatically schedules recirculation to deliver hot water during peak demand while optimizing energy efficiency.

Scope of work includes all necessary piping and connections to existing water, gas, and venting systems. Installation requires external (outside air) intake and exhaust. Unit is rated for up to three (3) bathrooms, with an input of 199,000 BTU and an energy factor of up to 0.95.

Includes: 
- Installing new vent piping installed exposed through utility room and bathroom
- Dedicated circuit installed by our electricians to power tankless unit and condensation pump
- Updating & Upsizing outside gas piping into home to 3/4 hard pipe outside and 3/4 flexible piping inside to feed tankless unit and furnace
- Dedicated 3/4 main water feed for tankless water heater piping up and over to location of new tankless. Piping will be installed exposed and below the ceiling.
